+# The total named source family
+
+## Abstract
+
+Signed source cycles and minimum natural block bases
+
+Let p present the entire finite set X of declared names, B be a finite list of selected BranchEquation cases, and S be the actual successful free-shape unifier of shapeEquations(B). The assignment s=action(p,S) retains every named term, including unused names. A residual occurrence records its name, its ordered address and its residual sort. The list occurrenceVertices(p,s) includes isolated occurrences. An occurring sort j has at least one such vertex. Decidable equality on X supports finite sort selection and equality tests on occurrence labels.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The actual sort edges).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.sortEdges`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.sortEdges` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+sortEdges(B,s,j) filters sourceOffsetEdges(B,s) by the sort of the left endpoint. It preserves list order, every repeated equation and every parallel edge. For a successful unifier, both endpoints are actual vertices of the same sort. A source shift contributes its original nonnegative integer offset. Ordinary and equality comparisons contribute zero. Explicit primitive ranks are separately decorated at their named addresses. The complete comparison inventory below retains scalar equations r=r'+d and r=d and one shared natural collapse parameter with ranks r,r+1,r+2. Its block projection is exactly sourceOffsetEdges; it does not solve the independent scalar equations.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Both orientations retain each edge identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedGraph`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedGraph` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each indexed sort edge U=V+d, signedGraph has a forward edge from V to U and a reverse edge from U to V. The Boolean orientation is part of the edge identity. Thus zero offsets, repeated edges and parallel edges remain explicit, and reversing an edge changes only its orientation and weight.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The signed offset).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedWeight`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedWeight` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The forward weight is d and the reverse weight is -d. A walk has the sum of its oriented edge weights. For a potential delta satisfying every original edge, the sum is delta(finish)-delta(start), so two paths with the same endpoints have the same sum.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Zero signed sum on every closed walk).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.ZeroCycles`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.ZeroCycles` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+ZeroCycles asserts that every closed walk at every occurrence has weight zero. The condition refers to the actual sort edge list rather than an epoch or head-power graph. Vertices without incident edges contribute only empty walks.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Integer differences on the source edges).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.Potential`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.Potential` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Potential(B,s,j,delta) states delta(U)=delta(V)+d for every edge U=V+d of the selected sort. Pairing both orientations identifies this exact equality with the inequalities of Maths.MaxPlusPotential.IsPotential. The finite supplier theorem exists_isPotential_iff_forall_closedWalk_nonpos supplies the existence criterion. The actual witness used for minimum normalization is computedSourcePotential on this source graph; its correctness reuses the existing cycle-pruning supplier.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Natural ranks on an arbitrary leaf carrier).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.BlockSolution`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.BlockSolution` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A block valuation u assigns a natural rank u(U,l) to each occurrence U and each leaf l. BlockSolution imposes the original signed integer equation at every leaf and every selected edge. The carrier L may be any type; no cardinality bound is imposed. Detecting inconsistency requires L to be nonempty. In particular this includes every nonempty finite ground-shape leaf set.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Enumerate every signed source edge).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedEdges`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.signedEdges` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+signedEdges enumerates both Boolean orientations for every index of sortEdges. Indices preserve repeated and parallel source comparisons. No vertex enumeration or connected-component choice is an input.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (Finite integer relaxation on the actual source graph).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.sourceRelaxation`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.sourceRelaxation` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At round zero every occurrence has value zero. Each successive round takes the maximum of zero and every previous-round source value plus the actual signed edge weight whose target is this occurrence. The recurrence uses finite lists, decidable equality and integer arithmetic. A round is attained by a real walk, and bounds every real walk of that length. The original NativeComputedEpochPotential.base_le_fold_max and fold_max_property supply the two max-fold facts directly at their relaxation consumers, with base zero. The existing SupplierDual cycle-pruning theorem reduces an arbitrary candidate to a walk with no repeated visited vertex, hence no repeated signed edge.
+
+**Definition 1.9 (An executable source potential candidate).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.computedSourcePotential`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.computedSourcePotential` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For k indexed source edges the candidate runs exactly 2k relaxation rounds, the number of signed edges. It takes only B,s,j and the queried occurrence. It requires no cycle proof, solution, potential witness, ground filling or classical choice at runtime. If every signed cycle has weight zero, cycle pruning bounds a maximizing extended walk by the signed-edge count and proves both oriented inequalities. Their conjunction is precisely every original integer source offset equation. The function is total also for inconsistent graphs; correctness is asserted only under ZeroCycles.
+
+**Definition 1.10 (Decide consistency by exact finite edge equations).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.checkSourceConsistency`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.checkSourceConsistency` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The certified potential returned by this check is used by minimum-base normalization and hence by canonical and native reconstruction. The Boolean checker computes the 2k-round candidate and tests delta(U)=delta(V)+d on every entry of sortEdges. It uses only finite list traversal, the supplied decidable equality on names, and exact integer arithmetic. Repeated and parallel edges are tested separately. No bound on offsets, vertex names, ordered addresses or residual sorts is imposed. The empty edge list is accepted; isolated vertices retain candidate value zero.
+
+**Theorem 1.11 (The executable checker is equivalent to the original closed-walk criterion).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_consistency_iff`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_consistency_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite branch list B, every substituted term family s, and every residual sort j, checkSourceConsistency(B,s,j)=true if and only if ZeroCycles(B,s,j). Acceptance verifies every exact source edge equation for computedSourcePotential. The resulting potential telescopes on every original signed closed walk, proving soundness. Conversely, zero sums on all closed walks make the finite relaxation candidate a potential by cycle pruning, so every checked edge equation holds. This proves completeness for the original labelled graph, including arbitrary repeated or parallel signed edges, zero offsets, empty lists and isolated occurrences. No successful unifier or native solution is required for this equivalence.
+
+**Theorem 1.12 (All original closed walks and integer feasibility).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.zeroCycles_iff`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.zeroCycles_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every B,s,j, ZeroCycles(B,s,j) holds exactly when there exists an integer Potential(B,s,j). The existing max-plus closed-walk theorem supplies existence, and the original edge equations telescope on every signed walk. This equivalence converts any natural block valuation at one leaf into the original consistency condition.
+
+**Definition 1.13 (An original source comparison obstruction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.parallelSourceInput`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.parallelSourceInput` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+This concrete input is the literal BranchEquation list U=shift(3,V), U=shift(3,V), U=shift(4,V), with U=true and V=false, substituted term family s(x)=variable(false), and selected sort false. Both named terms have the common free shape forced by these original shift equations. All three indexed parallel edges remain present; their signed orientations have weights 3,-3,3,-3,4,-4. Six exact relaxation rounds yield delta(U)=6 and delta(V)=3, and checkSourceConsistency returns false: the two offset-three equations pass and the offset-four equation fails. If any natural BlockSolution on any nonempty leaf carrier existed, selecting a leaf would give an integer Potential. zeroCycles_iff would imply ZeroCycles, and source_consistency_iff would force this same checker to return true, contradicting its actual computation. Hence these original block comparisons have no natural solution on any nonempty finite shape.
+
+**Definition 1.14 (An effective decision returns a certified potential).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.effectiveSourcePotential`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.effectiveSourcePotential` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The effective function runs checkSourceConsistency and returns some computedSourcePotential together with its exact Potential proof when accepted, or none when rejected. Proofs are erased during execution. The checker equivalence makes rejection equivalent to failure of the original ZeroCycles condition. Minimum normalization below obtains its potential and edge proof from this returned value; the same potential therefore supplies canonical and native block recovery.
+
+**Theorem 1.15 (Minimum-potential normalization classifies every natural block solution).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_sort_minimum_base`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_sort_minimum_base` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every p,B,S,j as above with at least one occurrence of j, the theorem has two conclusions. If ZeroCycles fails, then for every nonempty type L and every natural block valuation u on L, BlockSolution fails. If ZeroCycles holds, there exist one integer potential delta equal to computedSourcePotential(B,s,j), one actual vertex b of sort j, and natural offsets a(U), independent of L and u. The chosen b minimizes delta among all actual vertices of sort j, a(b)=0, and a(U)=delta(U)-delta(b) as an integer at every such vertex. For every L, including the empty type, and every u, BlockSolution holds exactly when u(U,l)=u(b,l)+a(U) for every actual vertex U of sort j and every l. Consequently every natural base function gives a solution by that formula, with arbitrary values outside the selected sort.
+
+A nonempty leaf valuation at any fixed leaf gives an integer potential, which telescopes around closed walks and excludes nonzero cycle sums. Conversely the exact finite consistency checker accepts when cycles vanish, and effectiveSourcePotential returns the certified relaxation candidate used for minimum normalization. Connectivity of the actual MGU source graph identifies all vertices of the same residual sort. Subtracting any two edge potentials gives a constant along this equivalence closure. Choosing a minimum on the finite vertex list makes every potential difference nonnegative; exact integer-to-natural conversion then gives the natural rank classification. The reverse implication uses the actual endpoints of every source edge and the same potential equation. This argument includes isolated unused names, empty branch lists, zero offsets, repeated and parallel constraints. If no sort occurs, the theorem is unnecessary and there is no block-base factor.
+
+This theorem establishes the signed-cycle and natural-rank classification using a terminating potential computation on the original source graph. The canonical recovery theorem below first presents the rank-to-code step with its precise inputs. The native source theorem then derives those inputs from an original native solution and its actual branch, without assuming a BlockSolution or desired subtree identities. The finite positive image cover and signed pullback are separate results.
+
+**Definition 1.16 (Nonempty finite leaves of an ordered shape).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.Leaves`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.Leaves` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The leaves of a primitive shape form Unit; leaves of a pair form the disjoint sum of the two child leaf sets. These types are finite and nonempty. Distinct positions remain distinct even when their ranks are equal.
+
+**Definition 1.17 (Fill the same ground shape with natural ranks).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.fill`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.fill` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+fill(T,r) puts rank r(l) at each ordered leaf l of T. Adding a natural number a to every rank gives exactly shiftCode(a,fill(T,r)). This is a structural property of finite ordered codes, with no normality assumption.
+
+**Theorem 1.18 (Recover normal occurrence blocks by the actual native shifts).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_canonical_block_recovery`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.source_canonical_block_recovery` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every actual successful source unifier and occurring sort with zero signed cycle sums, there are one actual base vertex b and natural offsets a with a(b)=0, independent of all ground fillings. The base minimizes computedSourcePotential over every actual occurrence of this sort, and a(o) equals its exact integer potential difference from b. Let T be any finite ground shape, u a natural rank valuation on its nonempty leaf type satisfying BlockSolution, and C the entire family of normal named codes. Suppose that at every actual occurrence v of this sort, the subtree of C(v.name) at v.address is exactly fill(T,u(v)). Then fill(T,u(b)) is normal. For every actual v of the sort, fill(T,u(v)) equals shiftCode(a(v),fill(T,u(b))); its expansion is the actual native substitution iterated a(v) times on the expansion of the base; and rankInverse(a(v),u(v,l)) is exactly some(u(b,l)) at every leaf.
+
+The rank classification supplies the same minimum vertex for all fillings. Normality descends along the actual ordered subtree address in the normal named code. Structural filling converts the pointwise rank equation to literal code translation. NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shift_expand gives the native equality, and exact_natural_rank_inverse gives every exact inverse rank without truncated subtraction. No desired normal base, integer potential or reconstruction equality is assumed. The concrete subtree identities and BlockSolution are hypotheses of this intermediate theorem. They are derived automatically on the live proof path of native_source_block_recovery.
+
+**Definition 1.19 (Separate scalar positions).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.ScalarPosition`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.ScalarPosition` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A scalar label consists of a declared name and its ordered address. Every explicit primitive occurrence gets its own label, while repeated uses of one name reuse the same decorated term. Residual blocks retain the existing name, address and sort labels.
+
+**Definition 1.20 (Natural scalar variables and constants).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.RankExpression`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.RankExpression` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A rank expression is either a separately addressed natural scalar or a supplied natural constant. Its value is evaluated independently of the residual block valuation.
+
+**Definition 1.21 (A complete decoration of each named term).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.DecoratedTerm`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositivePotentialCover.DecoratedTerm` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+

+# Three-state overlap intervals need not be tight
+
+## Abstract
+
+Five overlaps of four pure states force the sixth to be one quarter, although intersection of the three-state lower bounds gives zero.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The three-state upper bound).**
+
+$$\forall \left(x: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\forall \left(y: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper}\left(x, y\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \left(\operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(x\right) \cdot \left(y\right)\right) + \operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - x\right) \cdot \left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - y\right)\right)\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For real x and y, upper is the square of the sum of the two square roots. For known pure-state overlaps in the unit interval, this is the upper bound in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 118–122. The definition is a total real function and does not assume that its arguments lie in that interval.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The three-state lower bound).**
+
+$$\forall \left(x: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\forall \left(y: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower}\left(x, y\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{ite}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) < x + y\right), \left(\operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(x\right) \cdot \left(y\right)\right) - \operatorname{Real.sqrt}\left(\left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - x\right) \cdot \left(\left(1: \mathbb{R}\right) - y\right)\right)\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}, \left(0: \mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The lower bound is the square of the difference of the two square roots when x + y is strictly greater than one, and zero otherwise, including x + y = 1. This is the piecewise bound in overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 125–131, extended as a total function on all real arguments.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Squared overlap of two vectors).**
+
+$$\forall \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(u: \operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(v: \operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap}\left(u, v\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \left(\left\lVert \operatorname{inner}\left(\mathbb{C}, u, v\right) \right\rVert\right)^{\left(2: \mathbb{N}\right)}\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/PureState/OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.overlap` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Ernesto F. Galvão; Daniel J. Brod (2020). *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.101.062110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.11039v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The overlap is the squared norm of the complex inner product of u and v in the n-dimensional complex Euclidean space. For unit vectors this is the pure-state overlap of overlap_pra_v3.tex, lines 97–102. The definition itself imposes no normalization condition and includes dimension zero.
+

+$$\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procLower}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{sSup}\left(\{\left(t: \mathbb{R}\right) \mid \left(\exists \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left(k \ne i_{0}\right) \land \left(\left(k \ne j_{0}\right) \land \left(t = \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.lower}\left(r\left(k, i_{0}\right), r\left(k, j_{0}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$

+
+$$\forall \left(m: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(i_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(j_{0}: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(r: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.procUpper}\left(m, i_{0}, j_{0}, r\right): \mathbb{R}\right) = \operatorname{sInf}\left(\{\left(t: \mathbb{R}\right) \mid \left(\exists \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(m\right)\right), \left(\left(k \ne i_{0}\right) \land \left(\left(k \ne j_{0}\right) \land \left(t = \operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation.upper}\left(r\left(k, i_{0}\right), r\left(k, j_{0}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$

+   digest: Signed source occurrence cycles and minimum natural block bases. -/
+import D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativePositiveBranchReduction
+import D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.LayeredCirculation.SupplierDual
+import D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativeComputedEpochPotential
+/-! Integer consistency and minimum natural ranks on the actual source graph. -/
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.NativePositivePotentialCover
+open NativePositiveBranchReduction NativePositiveImageCover NativeTermUnification
+open NativeGroundSolutionSpace Maths Maths.MaxPlusPotential
+open Lambda Strata.Util
+variable {X : Type} [DecidableEq X]
+/-- Select one residual sort without identifying repeated or parallel edges. -/
+def sortEdges (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :=
+  (sourceOffsetEdges B s).filter (fun e => e.1.1.2.2 == j)
+abbrev Edge (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :=
+  Fin (sortEdges B s j).length × Bool
+def signedGraph (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    EdgeGraph (Occurrence X) (Edge B s j) where
+  source e := if e.2 then ((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).1.1
+    else ((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).1.2
+  target e := if e.2 then ((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).1.2
+    else ((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).1.1
+def signedWeight (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X)
+    (e : Edge B s j) : Int :=
+  if e.2 then -((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).2 else ((sortEdges B s j).get e.1).2
+def ZeroCycles (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) : Prop :=
+  ∀ (v : Occurrence X) (c : (signedGraph B s j).Walk v v),
+    walkWeight (signedWeight B s j) c = 0
+def Potential (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X)
+    (δ : Occurrence X → Int) : Prop :=
+  ∀ e ∈ sortEdges B s j, δ e.1.1 = δ e.1.2 + e.2
+/-- The leaf carrier is arbitrary; nonemptiness is needed only to detect
+inconsistent cycles. No shape or rank bound is imposed. -/
+def BlockSolution (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X)
+    {L : Type} (u : Occurrence X → L → Nat) : Prop :=
+  ∀ e ∈ sortEdges B s j, ∀ l, (u e.1.1 l : Int) = (u e.1.2 l : Int) + e.2
+private theorem potential_iff (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X)
+    (δ : Occurrence X → Int) :
+    Potential B s j δ ↔ IsPotential (signedGraph B s j) (signedWeight B s j) δ := by
+  constructor
+  · intro h e
+    have eq := h _ (List.get_mem (sortEdges B s j) e.1)
+    cases e with | mk i b => cases b <;> simp_all [signedGraph, signedWeight] <;> omega
+  · intro h e he
+    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := List.mem_iff_get.mp he
+    have hf := h (i, false)
+    have hb := h (i, true)
+    simp only [signedGraph, signedWeight, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] at hf hb
+    omega
+private theorem walk_exact {B : List (BranchEquation X)} {s : X → Term X} {j : X}
+    {δ : Occurrence X → Int} (h : Potential B s j δ)
+    {v w : Occurrence X} (c : (signedGraph B s j).Walk v w) :
+    walkWeight (signedWeight B s j) c = δ w - δ v := by
+  induction c with
+  | nil => simp [walkWeight]
+  | concat c e legal ih =>
+      have eq := h _ (List.get_mem (sortEdges B s j) e.1)
+      rw [walkWeight_concat, ih]
+      subst legal
+      cases e with | mk i b => cases b <;> simp_all [signedGraph, signedWeight] <;> omega
+theorem zeroCycles_iff (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    ZeroCycles B s j ↔ ∃ δ, Potential B s j δ := by
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    obtain ⟨δ, hδ⟩ :=
+      (exists_isPotential_iff_forall_closedWalk_nonpos
+        (G := signedGraph B s j) (signedWeight B s j)).mpr (fun v c => (h v c).le)
+    exact ⟨δ, (potential_iff B s j δ).mpr hδ⟩
+  · rintro ⟨δ, hδ⟩ v c
+    simpa using walk_exact hδ c
+/-- Enumerate the two signed orientations of every actual source edge.
+The list retains separate indices for repeated and parallel comparisons. -/
+def signedEdges (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    List (Edge B s j) :=
+  (List.finRange (sortEdges B s j).length).flatMap fun i => [(i, false), (i, true)]
+private theorem signedEdges_complete (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (e : Edge B s j) : e ∈ signedEdges B s j := by
+  rcases e with ⟨i, b⟩
+  apply List.mem_flatMap.mpr
+  refine ⟨i, List.mem_finRange i, ?_⟩
+  cases b <;> simp
+/-- Finite max-plus relaxation on the original source occurrence graph.
+Zero is a lower bound at every vertex, including isolated occurrences. -/
+def sourceRelaxation (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    Nat → Occurrence X → Int
+  | 0, _ => 0
+  | t + 1, v =>
+      ((signedEdges B s j).map fun e =>
+        if (signedGraph B s j).target e = v then
+          sourceRelaxation B s j t ((signedGraph B s j).source e) + signedWeight B s j e
+        else 0).foldr max 0
+/-- An executable integer potential candidate, with no solution, potential,
+path, cycle decision or classical choice supplied as input. The number of
+rounds is the number of signed indexed source edges. -/
+def computedSourcePotential (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    Occurrence X → Int :=
+  sourceRelaxation B s j (2 * (sortEdges B s j).length)
+private theorem sourceRelaxation_nonneg (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (t : Nat) (v : Occurrence X) :
+    0 ≤ sourceRelaxation B s j t v := by
+  cases t with
+  | zero => exact le_rfl
+  | succ t => exact NativeComputedEpochPotential.base_le_fold_max _ 0
+private theorem sourceRelaxation_edge (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (t : Nat) (e : Edge B s j) :
+    sourceRelaxation B s j t ((signedGraph B s j).source e) + signedWeight B s j e ≤
+      sourceRelaxation B s j (t + 1) ((signedGraph B s j).target e) := by
+  apply List.le_max_of_le' (0 : Int)
+  · exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨e, signedEdges_complete B s j e, rfl⟩
+  · simp only [ite_true]
+    exact le_rfl
+private theorem source_walk_le_relaxation (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (t : Nat) {v w : Occurrence X}
+    (c : (signedGraph B s j).Walk v w) (hlen : c.length ≤ t) :
+    walkWeight (signedWeight B s j) c ≤ sourceRelaxation B s j t w := by
+  induction t generalizing v w with
+  | zero =>
+      cases c with
+      | nil => simp [walkWeight, EdgeGraph.Walk.edges, sourceRelaxation]
+      | concat c e legal => simp at hlen
+  | succ t ih =>
+      cases c with
+      | nil => simpa [walkWeight, EdgeGraph.Walk.edges] using
+          sourceRelaxation_nonneg B s j (t + 1) v
+      | concat c e legal =>
+          have hp := ih c (by simpa using Nat.le_of_succ_le_succ hlen)
+          have he := sourceRelaxation_edge B s j t e
+          rw [legal] at he
+          rw [walkWeight_concat]
+          omega
+private theorem sourceRelaxation_attained (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (t : Nat) (v : Occurrence X) :
+    ∃ (start : Occurrence X) (c : (signedGraph B s j).Walk start v),
+      c.length ≤ t ∧ sourceRelaxation B s j t v = walkWeight (signedWeight B s j) c := by
+  induction t generalizing v with
+  | zero => exact ⟨v, .nil, le_rfl, by simp [sourceRelaxation, walkWeight, EdgeGraph.Walk.edges]⟩
+  | succ t ih =>
+      apply NativeComputedEpochPotential.fold_max_property (b := 0)
+        (P := fun z => ∃ (start : Occurrence X) (c : (signedGraph B s j).Walk start v),
+          c.length ≤ t + 1 ∧ z = walkWeight (signedWeight B s j) c)
+      · exact ⟨v, .nil, Nat.zero_le _, by simp [walkWeight, EdgeGraph.Walk.edges]⟩
+      · intro z hz
+        obtain ⟨e, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hz
+        by_cases he : (signedGraph B s j).target e = v
+        · simp only [if_pos he]
+          obtain ⟨start, c, hlen, hvalue⟩ := ih ((signedGraph B s j).source e)
+          refine ⟨start, (c.concat e rfl).castFinish he, ?_, ?_⟩
+          · simpa using Nat.add_le_add_right hlen 1
+          · rw [walkWeight_castFinish, walkWeight_concat, hvalue]
+        · simp only [if_neg he]
+          exact ⟨v, .nil, Nat.zero_le _, by simp [walkWeight, EdgeGraph.Walk.edges]⟩
+private theorem computed_source_potential (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (j : X) (good : ZeroCycles B s j) :
+    Potential B s j (computedSourcePotential B s j) := by
+  apply (potential_iff B s j _).mpr
+  intro e
+  obtain ⟨start, c, _, hvalue⟩ := sourceRelaxation_attained B s j
+    (2 * (sortEdges B s j).length) ((signedGraph B s j).source e)
+  obtain ⟨pruned, hnodup, hweight⟩ := exists_nodup_visited_walkWeight_le
+    (fun v c => (good v c).le) (c.concat e rfl).length (c.concat e rfl) le_rfl
+  have hcard : pruned.length ≤ 2 * (sortEdges B s j).length := by
+    simpa only [EdgeGraph.Walk.edges_length, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin,
+      Fintype.card_bool, Nat.mul_comm] using
+      pruned.edges_nodup_of_visited_nodup hnodup |>.length_le_card
+  have hbound := source_walk_le_relaxation B s j _ pruned hcard
+  rw [walkWeight_concat] at hweight
+  change sourceRelaxation B s j _ ((signedGraph B s j).source e) + signedWeight B s j e ≤
+    sourceRelaxation B s j _ ((signedGraph B s j).target e)
+  omega
+/-- Check every original indexed source equation against the finite relaxation
+candidate. Empty edge lists are accepted, and no vertex or integer bound is
+assumed. All arithmetic and equality tests are executable. -/
+def checkSourceConsistency (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) : Bool :=
+  (sortEdges B s j).all fun e => decide
+    (computedSourcePotential B s j e.1.1 = computedSourcePotential B s j e.1.2 + e.2)
+private theorem check_source_consistency_iff_potential
+    (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    checkSourceConsistency B s j = true ↔ Potential B s j (computedSourcePotential B s j) := by
+  simp only [checkSourceConsistency, List.all_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, Potential]
+/-- The finite executable check is sound and complete for the original
+condition on all closed walks of the labelled signed source graph. -/
+theorem source_consistency_iff (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    checkSourceConsistency B s j = true ↔ ZeroCycles B s j := by
+  rw [check_source_consistency_iff_potential]
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    exact (zeroCycles_iff B s j).mpr ⟨computedSourcePotential B s j, h⟩
+  · exact computed_source_potential B s j
+/-- Return a certified computed potential precisely when the finite check
+accepts. The certificate is erased during execution; rejection returns none. -/
+def effectiveSourcePotential (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) (j : X) :
+    Option {δ : Occurrence X → Int // Potential B s j δ} :=
+  if h : checkSourceConsistency B s j = true then
+    some ⟨computedSourcePotential B s j,
+      (check_source_consistency_iff_potential B s j).mp h⟩
+  else none
+/-- Original shifts U=V+3, U=V+3, U=V+4 on their common residual sort. -/
+def parallelSourceInput : List (BranchEquation Bool) × (Bool → Term Bool) × Bool :=
+  ([.shift true 3 false, .shift true 3 false, .shift true 4 false],
+    (fun _ => .of (.inr false)), false)
+private theorem edge_spec (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    {e : (Occurrence X × Occurrence X) × Int}
+    (he : e ∈ sourceOffsetEdges B (action p S)) :
+    e.1.1 ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧
+    e.1.2 ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧ e.1.1.2.2 = e.1.2.2.2 := by
+  apply (mgu_occurrence_graph_exact p (shapeEquations B) S hok).2.1
+  rw [← source_comparison_graph_identification]
+  exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨e, he, rfl⟩
+private theorem connected_sort (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    {v w : Occurrence X} (h : sourceConnected B (action p S) v w) :
+    v.2.2 = w.2.2 := by
+  induction h with
+  | rel a b he =>
+      obtain ⟨e, he, eq⟩ := List.mem_map.mp he
+      have hs := (edge_spec p B S hok he).2.2
+      simpa only [eq] using hs
+  | refl => rfl
+  | symm _ _ _ ih => exact ih.symm
+  | trans _ _ _ _ _ ih1 ih2 => exact ih1.trans ih2
+private theorem common_difference (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (j : X) {f g : Occurrence X → Int}
+    (hf : Potential B (action p S) j f) (hg : Potential B (action p S) j g)
+    {v w : Occurrence X} (h : sourceConnected B (action p S) v w) :
+    v.2.2 = j → f v - g v = f w - g w := by
+  induction h with
+  | rel v w he =>
+      intro hv
+      obtain ⟨e, he, eq⟩ := List.mem_map.mp he
+      have pair : e.1 = (v,w) := eq
+      have mem : e ∈ sortEdges B (action p S) j := by
+        simp only [sortEdges, List.mem_filter, beq_iff_eq]
+        exact ⟨he, by simpa only [pair] using hv⟩
+      have h1 := hf e mem
+      have h2 := hg e mem
+      simp only [pair] at h1 h2
+      omega
+  | refl v => intro _; rfl
+  | symm v w h ih =>
+      intro hw
+      have hv : v.2.2 = j := (connected_sort p B S hok h).trans hw
+      exact (ih hv).symm
+  | trans v w z h1 h2 ih1 ih2 =>
+      intro hv
+      have hw : w.2.2 = j := (connected_sort p B S hok h1).symm.trans hv
+      exact (ih1 hv).trans (ih2 hw)
+/-- The actual source comparison graph admits one minimum natural base per
+occurring sort. Nonzero cycles exclude solutions on every inhabited leaf
+carrier; zero cycles classify all natural solutions, including a singleton
+isolated occurrence. The theorem does not assert native code reconstruction. -/
+theorem source_sort_minimum_base (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (j : X) (occurs : ∃ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j) :
+    (¬ ZeroCycles B (action p S) j →
+      ∀ (L : Type) [Nonempty L] (u : Occurrence X → L → Nat),
+        ¬ BlockSolution B (action p S) j u) ∧
+    (ZeroCycles B (action p S) j →
+      ∃ (δ : Occurrence X → Int) (b : Occurrence X) (a : Occurrence X → Nat),
+        δ = computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j ∧
+        Potential B (action p S) j δ ∧
+        b ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧ b.2.2 = j ∧ a b = 0 ∧
+        (∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+          δ b ≤ δ v ∧ (a v : Int) = δ v - δ b) ∧
+        (∀ (L : Type) (u : Occurrence X → L → Nat),
+          BlockSolution B (action p S) j u ↔
+          ∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+            ∀ l, u v l = u b l + a v)) := by
+  classical
+  constructor
+  · intro bad L _ u hu
+    let l : L := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty L)
+    apply bad
+    exact (zeroCycles_iff B (action p S) j).mpr ⟨fun v => (u v l : Int), fun e he => hu e he l⟩
+  · intro good
+    have accepted := (source_consistency_iff B (action p S) j).mpr good
+    have available : (effectiveSourcePotential B (action p S) j).isSome := by
+      simp [effectiveSourcePotential, accepted]
+    let certified := (effectiveSourcePotential B (action p S) j).get available
+    let δ := certified.val
+    have hδ : Potential B (action p S) j δ := certified.property
+    have hcomputed : δ = computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j := by
+      simp [δ, certified, effectiveSourcePotential, accepted]
+    let V := (occurrenceVertices p (action p S)).toFinset.filter (fun v => v.2.2 = j)
+    have hV : V.Nonempty := by
+      obtain ⟨v, hv, hj⟩ := occurs
+      exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨List.mem_toFinset.mpr hv, hj⟩⟩
+    obtain ⟨b, hb, hmin⟩ := V.exists_min_image δ hV
+    have hb' := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    let a : Occurrence X → Nat := fun v => (δ v - δ b).toNat
+    have ha : ∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+        δ b ≤ δ v ∧ (a v : Int) = δ v - δ b := by
+      intro v hv hj
+      have hm := hmin v (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨List.mem_toFinset.mpr hv, hj⟩)
+      exact ⟨hm, Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)⟩
+    refine ⟨δ, b, a, hcomputed, hδ, List.mem_toFinset.mp hb'.1, hb'.2, ?_, ha, ?_⟩
+    · simp [a]
+    · intro L u
+      constructor
+      · intro hu v hv hj l
+        have conn := (source_connected_iff_sort p B S hok b v
+          (List.mem_toFinset.mp hb'.1) hv).mpr (hb'.2.trans hj.symm)
+        have hd := common_difference p B S hok j
+          (f := fun w => (u w l : Int)) (g := δ)
+          (fun e he => hu e he l) hδ conn hb'.2
+        have hav := (ha v hv hj).2
+        omega
+      · intro hu e he l
+        have he' := (List.mem_filter.mp he).1
+        have hj : e.1.1.2.2 = j := by
+          simpa only [beq_iff_eq] using (List.mem_filter.mp he).2
+        have spec := edge_spec p B S hok he'
+        have hu1 := hu e.1.1 spec.1 hj l
+        have hu2 := hu e.1.2 spec.2.1 (spec.2.2.symm.trans hj) l
+        have ha1 := (ha e.1.1 spec.1 hj).2
+        have ha2 := (ha e.1.2 spec.2.1 (spec.2.2.symm.trans hj)).2
+        have hed := hδ e he
+        omega
+/-- Leaves retain their ordered positions even when all ranks coincide. -/
+def Leaves : FreeMagma Unit → Type
+  | .of _ => Unit
+  | .mul A B => Leaves A ⊕ Leaves B
+
+instance leavesNonempty : (T : FreeMagma Unit) → Nonempty (Leaves T)
+  | .of _ => inferInstanceAs (Nonempty Unit)
+  | .mul A B =>
+      letI := leavesNonempty A
+      inferInstanceAs (Nonempty (Leaves A ⊕ Leaves B))
+def fill : (T : FreeMagma Unit) → (Leaves T → Nat) → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code
+  | .of _, r => .of (r ())
+  | .mul A B, r => .mul (fill A (fun l => r (.inl l))) (fill B (fun l => r (.inr l)))
+private theorem fill_shift (T : FreeMagma Unit) (r : Leaves T → Nat) (a : Nat) :
+    fill T (fun l => r l + a) = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (fill T r) := by
+  induction T using FreeMagma.rec with
+  | of => rfl
+  | mul A B ihA ihB =>
+      exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (ihA _) (ihB _)
+private theorem normal_subtree (C : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) (q : List Bool)
+    (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) (hC : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Normal C)
+    (h : subtree C q = some D) : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Normal D := by
+  induction q generalizing C with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      exact h ▸ hC
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases C with
+      | of n => cases h
+      | mul A B =>
+          cases b
+          · exact ih A hC.1 h
+          · exact ih B hC.2.1 h
+/-- Actual occurrence subtrees turn the minimum rank base into a normal
+native block. Rank inverses and expansion recover the identical blocks. -/
+theorem source_canonical_block_recovery (p : Presentation X)
+    (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (j : X) (occurs : ∃ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j)
+    (good : ZeroCycles B (action p S) j) :
+    ∃ (b : Occurrence X) (a : Occurrence X → Nat),
+      b ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧ b.2.2 = j ∧ a b = 0 ∧
+      (∀ o ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), o.2.2 = j →
+        computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j b ≤ computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j o ∧
+        (a o : Int) = computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j o -
+          computedSourcePotential B (action p S) j b) ∧
+      ∀ (T : FreeMagma Unit) (u : Occurrence X → Leaves T → Nat)
+        (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code),
+        BlockSolution B (action p S) j u →
+        (∀ x, NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Normal (C x)) →
+        (∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+          subtree (C v.1) v.2.1 = some (fill T (u v))) →
+        NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Normal (fill T (u b)) ∧
+        ∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+          fill T (u v) = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode (a v) (fill T (u b)) ∧
+          NativeFiniteNormalInversion.expand (fill T (u v)) =
+            GenealogicalFiberTransport.substitution^[a v]
+              (NativeFiniteNormalInversion.expand (fill T (u b))) ∧
+          (∀ l, NativeFiniteNormalInversion.rankInverse (a v) (u v l) = some (u b l)) := by
+  obtain ⟨δ, b, a, hcomp, hδ, hb, hj, hab, hmin, law⟩ :=
+    (source_sort_minimum_base p B S hok j occurs).2 good
+  subst δ
+  refine ⟨b, a, hb, hj, hab, hmin, ?_⟩
+  intro T u C hu hC actual
+  have ranks := (law (Leaves T) u).mp hu
+  refine ⟨normal_subtree (C b.1) b.2.1 _ (hC b.1) (actual b hb hj), ?_⟩
+  intro v hv hvj
+  have heq : u v = fun l => u b l + a v := funext (ranks v hv hvj)
+  have code : fill T (u v) = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode (a v) (fill T (u b)) := by
+    rw [heq]
+    exact fill_shift T (u b) (a v)
+  refine ⟨code, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [code]
+    exact NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shift_expand (a v) (fill T (u b))
+  · intro l
+    exact ((NativeFiniteNormalInversion.exact_natural_rank_inverse (a v) (u v l)).1
+      (u b l)).mpr (ranks v hv hvj l).symm
+/-- The actual code at an occurrence address. Invalid addresses have a
+fixed default; all results below prove validity before using a block. -/
+def occurrenceCode (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) (v : Occurrence X) :
+    NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code :=
+  (subtree (C v.1) v.2.1).getD (.of 0)
+private def Fits (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) :
+    Term (Occurrence X) → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code → Prop
+  | .of (.inl _), .of _ => True
+  | .of (.inl _), .mul _ _ => False
+  | .of (.inr v), D => D = occurrenceCode C v
+  | .mul A B, .mul D E => Fits C A D ∧ Fits C B E
+  | .mul _ _, .of _ => False
+private theorem subtree_child {A : Type} (C : FreeMagma A) (q : List Bool)
+    (D E : FreeMagma A) (h : subtree C q = some (.mul D E)) :
+    subtree C (q ++ [false]) = some D ∧ subtree C (q ++ [true]) = some E := by
+  induction q generalizing C with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      subst C
+      constructor <;> simp [subtree]
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases C with
+      | of a => cases h
+      | mul A B => cases b <;> exact ih _ h
+private theorem fits_decorate (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (w : X → NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Source) (x : X) (t : Term X)
+    (q : List Bool) (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (actual : subtree (C x) q = some D)
+    (sh : shape D = evaluate w t) : Fits C (decorateFrom x q t) D := by
+  induction t generalizing q D with
+  | of a =>
+      cases a with
+      | inl b => cases D <;> simp_all [shape, evaluate, Fits, decorateFrom]
+      | inr j =>
+          change D = (subtree (C x) q).getD (.of 0)
+          rw [actual]
+          rfl
+  | mul A B ihA ihB =>
+      cases D with
+      | of n => cases sh
+      | mul D E =>
+          have hs : shape D = evaluate w A ∧ shape E = evaluate w B := by
+            injection sh with hD hE
+            exact ⟨hD, hE⟩
+          have hc := subtree_child (C x) q D E actual
+          exact ⟨ihA _ _ hc.1 hs.1, ihB _ _ hc.2 hs.2⟩
+private theorem fits_offsets (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (A B : Term (Occurrence X)) (D E : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (a : Nat) (hA : Fits C A D) (hB : Fits C B E)
+    (eq : D = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a E) :
+    ∀ e ∈ offsetComparisonEdges (a : Int) A B,
+      e.2 = (a : Int) ∧ occurrenceCode C e.1.1 =
+        NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (occurrenceCode C e.1.2) := by
+  induction A generalizing B D E with
+  | of b =>
+      cases B with
+      | of c =>
+          cases b with
+          | inl b => cases c <;> simp [offsetComparisonEdges]
+          | inr v =>
+              cases c with
+              | inl b => simp [offsetComparisonEdges]
+              | inr w =>
+                  intro e he
+                  have heq : e = ((v, w), (a : Int)) := List.mem_singleton.mp he
+                  subst e
+                  simp only [Fits] at hA hB
+                  exact ⟨rfl, by simpa only [hA, hB] using eq⟩
+      | mul l r => simp [offsetComparisonEdges]
+  | mul A₁ A₂ ihA ihB =>
+      cases B with
+      | of c => simp [offsetComparisonEdges]
+      | mul U V =>
+          cases E with
+          | of n => cases hB
+          | mul E F =>
+              subst D
+              rcases hA with ⟨hD, hE⟩
+              rcases hB with ⟨hU, hV⟩
+              intro e he
+              rcases List.mem_append.mp he with he | he
+              · exact ihA _ _ _ hD hU rfl e he
+              · exact ihB _ _ _ hE hV rfl e he
+private theorem actual_source_offsets (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (factor : ∀ x, evaluate (fun y => shape (C y)) (s x) = shape (C x))
+    (sat : ∀ b ∈ B, b.Holds C) :
+    ∀ e ∈ sourceOffsetEdges B s, ∃ a : Nat, e.2 = (a : Int) ∧
+      occurrenceCode C e.1.1 = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a
+        (occurrenceCode C e.1.2) := by
+  have fit (x : X) : Fits C (decorate s x) (C x) :=
+    fits_decorate C (fun y => shape (C y)) x (s x) [] (C x) (by simp [subtree]) (factor x).symm
+  intro e he
+  obtain ⟨b, hb, he⟩ := List.mem_flatMap.mp he
+  have hs := sat b hb
+  cases b with
+  | primitive z n => cases he
+  | collapse z x y => cases he
+  | shift z a x => exact ⟨a, fits_offsets C _ _ _ _ a (fit z) (fit x) hs e he⟩
+  | ordinary z x y =>
+      refine ⟨0, fits_offsets C _ _ (C z) (.mul (C x) (C y)) 0 (fit z) ?_ ?_ e he⟩
+      · exact ⟨fit x, fit y⟩
+      · simpa only [NativePositiveBranchReduction.shift_zero, BranchEquation.Holds] using hs
+  | same x y =>
+      refine ⟨0, fits_offsets C _ _ _ _ 0 (fit x) (fit y) ?_ e he⟩
+      simpa only [NativePositiveBranchReduction.shift_zero, BranchEquation.Holds] using hs
+private def codeTree : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code → FreeMagma Unit
+  | .of _ => .of ()
+  | .mul A B => .mul (codeTree A) (codeTree B)
+private def groundShape : FreeMagma Unit → NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Source
+  | .of _ => .of true
+  | .mul A B => .mul (groundShape A) (groundShape B)
+private theorem codeTree_shape (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) :
+    groundShape (codeTree D) = shape D := by
+  induction D with
+  | of n => rfl
+  | mul A B ihA ihB => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul ihA ihB
+private def readRanks : (T : FreeMagma Unit) → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code → Leaves T → Nat
+  | .of _, .of n => fun _ => n
+  | .mul A B, .mul D E => Sum.elim (readRanks A D) (readRanks B E)
+  | _, _ => fun _ => 0
+private theorem fill_readRanks (T : FreeMagma Unit) (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (sh : shape D = groundShape T) : fill T (readRanks T D) = D := by
+  induction T using FreeMagma.rec generalizing D with
+  | of u => cases D with
+    | of n => rfl
+    | mul A B => cases sh
+  | mul A B ihA ihB =>
+      cases D with
+      | of n => cases sh
+      | mul D E =>
+          have hs : shape D = groundShape A ∧ shape E = groundShape B := by
+            injection sh with hD hE
+            exact ⟨hD, hE⟩
+          exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (ihA D hs.1) (ihB E hs.2)
+private theorem readRanks_shift (T : FreeMagma Unit) (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (sh : shape D = groundShape T) (a : Nat) (l : Leaves T) :
+    readRanks T (NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a D) l = readRanks T D l + a := by
+  induction T using FreeMagma.rec generalizing D with
+  | of u => cases D with
+    | of n => rfl
+    | mul A B => cases sh
+  | mul A B ihA ihB =>
+      cases D with
+      | of n => cases sh
+      | mul D E =>
+          have hs : shape D = groundShape A ∧ shape E = groundShape B := by
+            injection sh with hD hE
+            exact ⟨hD, hE⟩
+          cases l with
+          | inl l => exact ihA D hs.1 l
+          | inr l => exact ihB E hs.2 l
+private theorem code_at_residual (w : X → NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Source)
+    (t : Term X) (D : NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) (q : List Bool) (j : X)
+    (sh : shape D = evaluate w t)
+    (occ : subtree t q = some (.of (.inr j))) :
+    ∃ E, subtree D q = some E ∧ shape E = w j := by
+  induction q generalizing t D with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at occ
+      subst t
+      exact ⟨D, by simp [subtree], sh⟩
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases t with
+      | of c => cases occ
+      | mul A B =>
+          cases D with
+          | of n => cases sh
+          | mul D E =>
+              have hs : shape D = evaluate w A ∧ shape E = evaluate w B := by
+                injection sh with hD hE
+                exact ⟨hD, hE⟩
+              cases b
+              · exact ih A D hs.1 occ
+              · exact ih B E hs.2 occ
+private theorem actual_occurrence_code (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (factor : ∀ x, evaluate (fun y => shape (C y)) (action p S x) = shape (C x))
+    (v : Occurrence X) (hv : v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S)) :
+    subtree (C v.1) v.2.1 = some (occurrenceCode C v) ∧
+      shape (occurrenceCode C v) = shape (C v.2.2) := by
+  have occ := (mgu_occurrence_graph_exact p (shapeEquations B) S hok).1 v |>.mp hv
+  obtain ⟨D, hD, hs⟩ := code_at_residual (fun y => shape (C y))
+    (action p S v.1) (C v.1) v.2.1 v.2.2 (factor v.1).symm occ
+  have eq : occurrenceCode C v = D := by simp only [occurrenceCode, hD, Option.getD_some]
+  exact ⟨by rw [eq]; exact hD, by rw [eq]; exact hs⟩
+private theorem actual_rank_blocks (p : Presentation X) (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (C : X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (factor : ∀ x, evaluate (fun y => shape (C y)) (action p S x) = shape (C x))
+    (sat : ∀ b ∈ B, b.Holds C) (j : X) :
+    let T := codeTree (C j)
+    let u := fun v => readRanks T (occurrenceCode C v)
+    BlockSolution B (action p S) j u ∧
+      ∀ v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S), v.2.2 = j →
+        subtree (C v.1) v.2.1 = some (fill T (u v)) := by
+  dsimp only
+  have valid (v : Occurrence X) (hv : v ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S))
+      (hj : v.2.2 = j) : shape (occurrenceCode C v) = groundShape (codeTree (C j)) := by
+    rw [(actual_occurrence_code p B S hok C factor v hv).2, hj, codeTree_shape]
+  constructor
+  · intro e he l
+    have he' := (List.mem_filter.mp he).1
+    have hj : e.1.1.2.2 = j := by
+      simpa only [beq_iff_eq] using (List.mem_filter.mp he).2
+    have spec := edge_spec p B S hok he'
+    obtain ⟨a, ha, code⟩ := actual_source_offsets B (action p S) C factor sat e he'
+    have hr := readRanks_shift (codeTree (C j)) (occurrenceCode C e.1.2)
+      (valid e.1.2 spec.2.1 (spec.2.2.symm.trans hj)) a l
+    change (readRanks (codeTree (C j)) (occurrenceCode C e.1.1) l : Int) =
+      (readRanks (codeTree (C j)) (occurrenceCode C e.1.2) l : Int) + e.2
+    rw [code, hr, ha]
+    omega
+  · intro v hv hj
+    rw [fill_readRanks _ _ (valid v hv hj)]
+    exact (actual_occurrence_code p B S hok C factor v hv).1
+/-- Explicit primitive positions and residual positions have separate labels. -/
+abbrev ScalarPosition (X : Type) := X × List Bool
+inductive RankExpression (X : Type) where
+  | scalar : ScalarPosition X → RankExpression X
+  | constant : Nat → RankExpression X
+inductive DecoratedTerm (X : Type) where
+  | scalar : Bool → RankExpression X → DecoratedTerm X
+  | block : Occurrence X → DecoratedTerm X
+  | pair : DecoratedTerm X → DecoratedTerm X → DecoratedTerm X
+def RankExpression.value (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat) : RankExpression X → Nat
+  | .scalar q => r q
+  | .constant n => n
+def DecoratedTerm.erase : DecoratedTerm X → Term X
+  | .scalar b _ => .of (.inl b)
+  | .block o => .of (.inr o.2.2)
+  | .pair A B => .mul A.erase B.erase
+def DecoratedTerm.value (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat)
+    (u : Occurrence X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) :
+    DecoratedTerm X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code
+  | .scalar _ n => .of (n.value r)
+  | .block o => u o
+  | .pair A B => .mul (A.value r u) (B.value r u)
+def scalarDecorateFrom (x : X) (q : List Bool) : Term X → DecoratedTerm X
+  | .of (.inl b) => .scalar b (.scalar (x,q))
+  | .of (.inr j) => .block (x,q,j)
+  | .mul A B => .pair (scalarDecorateFrom x (q ++ [false]) A)
+      (scalarDecorateFrom x (q ++ [true]) B)
+def scalarDecorate (s : X → Term X) (x : X) : DecoratedTerm X :=
+  scalarDecorateFrom x [] (s x)
+/-- A finite structural inventory. Every leaf equation is scalar or block;
+there is no mixed scalar/block equation. -/
+inductive ComparisonInventory (X : Type) where
+  | scalar : RankExpression X → RankExpression X → Nat → ComparisonInventory X
+  | block : Occurrence X → Occurrence X → Nat → ComparisonInventory X
+  | both : ComparisonInventory X → ComparisonInventory X → ComparisonInventory X
+  | incompatible : ComparisonInventory X
+def ComparisonInventory.Holds (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat)
+    (u : Occurrence X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) : ComparisonInventory X → Prop
+  | .scalar n m a => (n.value r : Int) = (m.value r : Int) + (a : Int)
+  | .block v w a => u v = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (u w)
+  | .both I J => I.Holds r u ∧ J.Holds r u
+  | .incompatible => False
+def comparisonInventory (a : Nat) : DecoratedTerm X → DecoratedTerm X →
+    ComparisonInventory X
+  | .scalar _ n, .scalar _ m => .scalar n m a
+  | .block v, .block w => .block v w a
+  | .pair A B, .pair C D =>
+      .both (comparisonInventory a A C) (comparisonInventory a B D)
+  | _, _ => .incompatible
+private theorem scalar_decorate_erase (x : X) (q : List Bool) (t : Term X) :
+    (scalarDecorateFrom x q t).erase = t := by
+  induction t generalizing q with
+  | of b => cases b <;> rfl
+  | mul A B ihA ihB => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (ihA _) (ihB _)
+private def comparisonProjection : DecoratedTerm X → Term (Occurrence X)
+  | .scalar b _ => .of (.inl b)
+  | .block o => .of (.inr o)
+  | .pair A B => .mul (comparisonProjection A) (comparisonProjection B)
+/-- Project exactly the original indexed block equations, preserving repetitions. -/
+def ComparisonInventory.blockEdges : ComparisonInventory X →
+    List ((Occurrence X × Occurrence X) × Int)
+  | .scalar _ _ _ => []
+  | .block v w a => [((v,w),(a : Int))]
+  | .both I J => I.blockEdges ++ J.blockEdges
+  | .incompatible => []
+private theorem comparison_inventory_edges (a : Nat) (A B : DecoratedTerm X) :
+    (comparisonInventory a A B).blockEdges =
+      offsetComparisonEdges (a : Int) (comparisonProjection A) (comparisonProjection B) := by
+  induction A generalizing B with
+  | scalar b n => cases B <;> rfl
+  | block v => cases B <;> rfl
+  | pair A₁ A₂ ihA ihB =>
+      cases B with
+      | scalar c m => rfl
+      | block w => rfl
+      | pair C D => simp only [comparisonInventory, ComparisonInventory.blockEdges,
+          comparisonProjection, offsetComparisonEdges, ihA, ihB]
+private theorem scalar_decorate_projection (x : X) (q : List Bool) (t : Term X) :
+    comparisonProjection (scalarDecorateFrom x q t) = decorateFrom x q t := by
+  induction t generalizing q with
+  | of a => cases a <;> rfl
+  | mul A B ihA ihB => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (ihA _) (ihB _)
+/-- Equality of the erased terms is the actual shape-unifier invariant.
+The two valuations are otherwise arbitrary and independent. -/
+private theorem comparison_inventory_iff (a : Nat) (A B : DecoratedTerm X)
+    (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat) (u : Occurrence X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (same : A.erase = B.erase) :
+    (comparisonInventory a A B).Holds r u ↔
+      A.value r u = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (B.value r u) := by
+  induction A generalizing B with
+  | scalar b n =>
+      cases B with
+      | scalar c m =>
+          change ((n.value r : Int) = (m.value r : Int) + (a : Int)) ↔
+            FreeMagma.of (n.value r) = FreeMagma.of (m.value r + a)
+          constructor
+          · intro h
+            congr 1
+            omega
+          · intro h
+            have hn : n.value r = m.value r + a := by injection h
+            omega
+      | block w => cases same
+      | pair C D => cases same
+  | block v =>
+      cases B with
+      | scalar c m => cases same
+      | block w => rfl
+      | pair C D => cases same
+  | pair A₁ A₂ ihA ihB =>
+      cases B with
+      | scalar c m => cases same
+      | block w => cases same
+      | pair C D =>
+          have parts : A₁.erase = C.erase ∧ A₂.erase = D.erase := by
+            injection same with hA hB
+            exact ⟨hA,hB⟩
+          change (_ ∧ _) ↔ FreeMagma.mul _ _ = FreeMagma.mul _ _
+          constructor
+          · intro h
+            exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul ((ihA C parts.1).mp h.1)
+              ((ihB D parts.2).mp h.2)
+          · intro h
+            have hc : A₁.value r u = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (C.value r u) ∧
+                A₂.value r u = NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shiftCode a (D.value r u) := by
+              injection h with h₁ h₂
+              exact ⟨h₁,h₂⟩
+            exact ⟨(ihA C parts.1).mpr hc.1, (ihB D parts.2).mpr hc.2⟩
+/-- Each collapse has one natural witness shared by all three comparisons. -/
+inductive BranchInventory (X : Type) where
+  | comparison : ComparisonInventory X → BranchInventory X
+  | collapse : (Nat → ComparisonInventory X) → BranchInventory X
+def BranchInventory.Holds (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat)
+    (u : Occurrence X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code) : BranchInventory X → Prop
+  | .comparison I => I.Holds r u
+  | .collapse I => ∃ n : Nat, (I n).Holds r u
+def branchInventory (s : X → Term X) : BranchEquation X → BranchInventory X
+  | .primitive z n => .comparison
+      (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s z) (.scalar true (.constant n)))
+  | .shift z a x => .comparison
+      (comparisonInventory a (scalarDecorate s z) (scalarDecorate s x))
+  | .ordinary z x y => .comparison
+      (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s z)
+        (.pair (scalarDecorate s x) (scalarDecorate s y)))
+  | .same x y => .comparison
+      (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s x) (scalarDecorate s y))
+  | .collapse z x y => .collapse fun n => .both
+      (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s x) (.scalar true (.constant (n+1))))
+      (.both (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s y) (.scalar true (.constant n)))
+        (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s z) (.scalar true (.constant (n+2)))))
+def BranchInventory.blockEdges : BranchInventory X →
+    List ((Occurrence X × Occurrence X) × Int)
+  | .comparison I => I.blockEdges
+  | .collapse _ => []
+private theorem branch_inventory_edges (s : X → Term X) (b : BranchEquation X) :
+    (branchInventory s b).blockEdges = sourceOffsetEdges [b] s := by
+  have proj (x : X) : comparisonProjection (scalarDecorate s x) = decorate s x :=
+    scalar_decorate_projection x [] (s x)
+  cases b with
+  | primitive z n =>
+      change (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s z)
+        (.scalar true (.constant n))).blockEdges = []
+      rw [comparison_inventory_edges]
+      cases comparisonProjection (scalarDecorate s z) with
+      | of a => cases a <;> rfl
+      | mul A B => rfl
+  | collapse z x y => rfl
+  | shift z a x =>
+      change (comparisonInventory a (scalarDecorate s z) (scalarDecorate s x)).blockEdges =
+        offsetComparisonEdges (a : Int) (decorate s z) (decorate s x) ++ []
+      simp only [comparison_inventory_edges, proj, List.append_nil]
+  | ordinary z x y =>
+      change (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s z)
+        (.pair (scalarDecorate s x) (scalarDecorate s y))).blockEdges =
+        offsetComparisonEdges 0 (decorate s z) (.mul (decorate s x) (decorate s y)) ++ []
+      simp only [comparison_inventory_edges, comparisonProjection, proj, List.append_nil]
+      norm_num
+  | same x y =>
+      change (comparisonInventory 0 (scalarDecorate s x) (scalarDecorate s y)).blockEdges =
+        offsetComparisonEdges 0 (decorate s x) (decorate s y) ++ []
+      simp only [comparison_inventory_edges, proj, List.append_nil]
+      norm_num
+/-- Complete normalization of one original comparison, including its natural
+collapse witness. No scalar constraint is an external hypothesis. -/
+private theorem branch_inventory_iff (s : X → Term X) (b : BranchEquation X)
+    (r : ScalarPosition X → Nat) (u : Occurrence X → NativeFiniteNormalInversion.Code)
+    (sh : ∀ e ∈ b.shapeEquations, substitute s e.1 = substitute s e.2) :
+    (branchInventory s b).Holds r u ↔
+      b.Holds (fun x => (scalarDecorate s x).value r u) := by
+  have er (x : X) : (scalarDecorate s x).erase = s x :=
+    scalar_decorate_erase x [] (s x)
+  have cmp (a : Nat) (A B : DecoratedTerm X) (h : A.erase = B.erase) :=
+    comparison_inventory_iff a A B r u h
+  cases b with
+  | primitive z n =>
+      have h := sh _ (List.mem_singleton_self _)
+      change s z = .of (.inl true) at h
+      simpa only [branchInventory, BranchInventory.Holds, BranchEquation.Holds,
+        DecoratedTerm.value, RankExpression.value, NativePositiveBranchReduction.shift_zero]
+        using cmp 0 (scalarDecorate s z) (.scalar true (.constant n)) (by simpa only [DecoratedTerm.erase, er] using h)
+  | shift z a x =>
+      have h := sh _ (List.mem_singleton_self _)
+      change s z = s x at h
+      exact cmp a _ _ (by simpa only [er] using h)
+  | ordinary z x y =>
+      have h := sh _ (List.mem_singleton_self _)
+      change s z = .mul (s x) (s y) at h

+    · simpa only [identity o ho hoj, identity b hb hj] using (recovered.2 o ho hoj).2.1

+    (hψ : realizes 2 3 givenOverlaps ψ) : overlap (ψ 2) (ψ 3) = 1 / 4 := by
+  have hab : overlap (ψ 0) (ψ 1) = 0 := hψ.2 0 1 (by decide) (by decide)
+  have hac : overlap (ψ 0) (ψ 2) = 1 / 2 := hψ.2 0 2 (by decide) (by decide)
+  have had : overlap (ψ 0) (ψ 3) = 1 / 2 := hψ.2 0 3 (by decide) (by decide)
+  have hbc : overlap (ψ 1) (ψ 2) = 1 / 2 := hψ.2 1 2 (by decide) (by decide)
+  have hbd : overlap (ψ 1) (ψ 3) = 0 := hψ.2 1 3 (by decide) (by decide)
+  have hc := span_saturation (ψ 0) (ψ 1) (ψ 2)
+    (hψ.1 0) (hψ.1 1) (hψ.1 2) hab hac hbc
+  have hbd0 : inner ℂ (ψ 1) (ψ 3) = 0 := by
+    exact norm_eq_zero.mp (sq_eq_zero_iff.mp hbd)
+  change ‖inner ℂ (ψ 2) (ψ 3)‖ ^ 2 = 1 / 4
+  rw [hc, inner_add_left, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_left, hbd0,
+    mul_zero, add_zero, norm_mul, RCLike.norm_conj, mul_pow]
+  change ‖inner ℂ (ψ 0) (ψ 2)‖ ^ 2 = 1 / 2 at hac
+  change ‖inner ℂ (ψ 0) (ψ 3)‖ ^ 2 = 1 / 2 at had
+  rw [hac, had]
+  norm_num
+
+private lemma feasible_nonempty : (feasible 4 2 3 givenOverlaps).Nonempty := by
+  exact ⟨overlap (witness 2) (witness 3), 3, witness, witness_realizes, rfl⟩
+
+private lemma feasible_singleton : feasible 4 2 3 givenOverlaps = {1 / 4} := by
+  ext t
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨n, ψ, hψ, rfl⟩
+    exact forced_overlap ψ hψ
+  · intro ht
+    have htq : t = 1 / 4 := ht
+    exact ⟨3, witness, witness_realizes, htq.trans (forced_overlap witness witness_realizes).symm⟩
+
+private lemma instance_infimum : sInf (feasible 4 2 3 givenOverlaps) = 1 / 4 := by
+  rw [feasible_singleton, csInf_singleton]
+
+/-- Three-state interval propagation is not always tight for four pure states. -/
+theorem result : ¬ claim := by
+  intro h
+  have hbound := (h 4 2 3 givenOverlaps (by norm_num) (by decide) feasible_nonempty).1
+  rw [instance_lower, instance_infimum] at hbound
+  norm_num at hbound
+
+end
+
+end D5.S3.Quantum.PureState.OverlapIntervalPropagationRefutation

+可继续调用，其完整增量记录由探针名和输出位 $w$ 组成，转移为
+
+$$
+(E_i,h)\xrightarrow[\ p_i^w(1-p_i)^{1-w}\ ]{\mathsf P,w}
+(E_i,h\mathbin{\|}(\mathsf P,w)),\qquad w\in\{0,1\}.
+$$
+
+这里 $\|$ 是向有序档案尾部追加，$q(E_i,h)=i+1$；固定的动作名可从 $W_j$

+$$
+\alpha_i=\begin{cases}2^{1-r}\binom ri&i\text{ 偶},\\0&i\text{ 奇},\end{cases}

+\beta_i=\begin{cases}0&i\text{ 偶},\\2^{1-r}\binom ri&i\text{ 奇}
+\end{cases}
+\tag{UJB.7408}

+探针输出的 law 在 $k<r$ 时完全相同，在 $k=r$ 时满足

+d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathsf{Law}_{R_+}(b_\ast,W_1,\ldots,W_r),
+                 \mathsf{Law}_{R_-}(b_\ast,W_1,\ldots,W_r))
+ =r!\,\delta^r.
+\tag{UJB.7409}
+$$

+
+固定有限的事件—记录字母表 $B$、终止字母表 $T$、探针字母表 $\mathcal A$，以及
+一个有限的已实现后继商
+
+$$
+C=\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad m\ge 2.
+$$
+
+一次首动作的完整行由一个概率分布 $\rho$ 给出。它的质量分别写成
+$\rho(b,c)$ 和 $\rho(b,t)$，其中 $(b,c)\in B\times C$ 是带有首事件和整条首记录的
+成功后继，$(b,t)\in B\times T$ 是带有同一首记录的终止后继。$b$ 必须包含合法性、
+拒绝原因和权限结果等会影响后续选择或解释的字段；若这些字段不能被写入 $b$，
+下文只在所有候选来源共有的合法域上成立。终端 $t$ 不与任何 $c$ 合并。
+
+固定首动作前已经取得的档案；以下各行 $\rho$ 都在这个共同初始条件下比较。
+令 $S_{\mathrm{actual}}$ 为所有成功后可达的实际状态（包括带完整档案的实际配置），
+并令 $q:S_{\mathrm{actual}}\to C$ 为把实际状态或配置映射到其已实现后继商类的商映射。
+首动作成功后的实际状态记为 $S_0$，令 $C_0=q(S_0)$。$H_0$ 是此时的完整
+已取得上下文，包含旧档案和首记录 $b$。连续调用同一个长度为 $L$ 的宏探针
+$\mathsf P$；$W_j\in\mathcal A^L$ 是第 $j$ 次调用实际写入的完整有序事件—记录词，
+$S_j$ 和 $H_j$ 分别是调用后的实际状态与完整已取得上下文。特别地，$H_j$
+保留 $H_0,W_1,\ldots,W_j$，不覆盖、删除或重排已有记录。
+
+令 $\mathcal F_j$ 为到第 $j$ 次调用结束为止的实际过去所生成的滤过，包含
+$S_0,\ldots,S_j$、$H_0,\ldots,H_j$ 以及这些调用的全部记录、控制状态和权限。
+$\mathcal F_0$ 是第一次探针之前的实际过去，$\mathcal F_{j-1}$ 是第 $j$ 次
+探针的调用前信息。这里包含实际状态只是为了陈述来源核的条件，不赋予观察者
+读取隐藏类或完整 law 的操作。每个允许的实际代表元和每个允许的调用前历史
+上的来源转移核都须满足同一个点态校准律，其条件期望写法是
+
+$$
+\Pr(W_j=w\mid\mathcal F_{j-1})=P_{C_0}(w),
+\qquad w\in\mathcal A^L,\quad 1\le j\le r.
+\tag{UJB.7401}
+$$
+
+其中 $P_c$ 与代表元和实际过去无关；零概率历史处采用所声明的点态转移核，
+不对零概率事件作条件除法。每次宏探针在所有支持分支上合法，每一个支持结果
+都满足 $q(S_j)=C_0$，且权限允许下一次所需调用；完整的实际状态和完整记录
+仍被保留。这一来源条件约束的是给定实际过去的下一输出，而不只是各次调用
+未经历史条件化的边缘律。
+
+由此，对每个有正概率的初始条件 $(C_0,H_0)=(c,h_0)$，
+
+$$
+\Pr(W_1=w_1,\ldots,W_r=w_r\mid C_0=c,H_0=h_0)
+ =\prod_{j=1}^rP_c(w_j).
+\tag{UJB.7402}
+$$
+

+它属于 $\mathcal F_{k-1}$，而 $C_0,H_0$ 属于 $\mathcal F_0$。条件期望的塔式律给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+&\Pr(D_{k-1},W_k=w_k\mid C_0,H_0)\\
+&\quad=\mathbb E\!\left[
+ \mathbf1_{D_{k-1}}\Pr(W_k=w_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})
+ \mid C_0,H_0\right]\\
+&\quad=P_{C_0}(w_k)\Pr(D_{k-1}\mid C_0,H_0).

+$$

+写
+
+$$
+\Delta=\min_{c\ne d}d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_c,P_d)>0,
+\qquad
+d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu,\nu)=\frac12\sum_x|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|.
+\tag{UJB.7403}
+$$
+
+这里的总变差是有限字母表上的通常归一化距离。给定 $r=m-1$ 次宏探针，

+调用探针。因此首动作与后续档案的联合 law 为
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathcal M_\rho(b,\mathsf{term},t)&=\rho(b,t),\\
+\mathcal M_\rho(b,\mathsf{succ},w_1,\ldots,w_r)
+ &=\sum_{c\in C}\rho(b,c)\prod_{j=1}^rP_c(w_j).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{UJB.7404}
+$$
+
+它保留 $b$ 与 $c$ 的联合关系、每个终端的身份和每一个实际写入的探针词。

+### 2.5 接回四视图及不可恢复边界
+
+引理 2.1 只恢复一个实际首行及其终端部分。把恢复的行重新放回
+(UJB.7301) 的 typed joint law 后，只有当合法性、selector、记录更新和后继都
+沿同一商纤维下降，才可继续使用 (UJB.7310)--(UJB.7313) 的四视图运输。于是
+空间、时间、边界、记忆仍必须是同一实际共同来源上的四个因子；恢复首行并不
+推出 $K_n=A_n^{\mathrm{law}}$ 的全层恒等，也不推出物理时空的本体恢复。
+
+有三类边界必须保留。第一，若探针会破坏 $c$、使所需后续调用不再合法，或只有
+单次边缘校准而不满足给定实际过去的 (UJB.7401)，则没有本章的来源保证，不能
+据此推出 (UJB.7402) 或把相同边缘律乘成张量 law。第二，若
+合法性或拒绝原因藏在不可见字段，(UJB.7405) 只能在声明的共同合法范围内使用，
+不能把非法分支静默合并。第三，即使行 law 已由引理唯一确定，重叠支持的一个
+有限实际记录仍不能零误差识别隐藏的 $c$；那是 law 级统计逆，不是一次运行的
+历史恢复。只有额外的互不相交支持或等价的可测分割，才会回到 UJB.7307--7309

+$\mathcal M_\rho$ 唯一决定 $\rho$，并且对任意两个允许的首行动作行
+$\rho,\rho'$ 有
+
+$$
+d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\rho,\rho')
+ \le \min\left\{1,
+m\Delta^{-(m-1)}d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathcal M_\rho,\mathcal M_{\rho'})\right\}.
+\tag{UJB.7405}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 对每一对 $c\ne d$，从有限字母表的总变差定义选取
+$f_{cd}:\mathcal A^L\to[0,1]$，使
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_{P_c}f_{cd}-\mathbb E_{P_d}f_{cd}
+ =d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_c,P_d)\ge\Delta.
+$$
+
+令 $g_{cd}=f_{cd}-\mathbb E_{P_d}f_{cd}$。于是 $|g_{cd}|\le1$，
+$\mathbb E_{P_d}g_{cd}=0$，且 $\mathbb E_{P_c}g_{cd}\ge\Delta$。把
+$C\setminus\{c\}$ 任意双射到 $\{1,\ldots,r\}$，定义
+
+$$
+h_c(w_1,\ldots,w_r)=\prod_{d\ne c}g_{cd}(w_{\iota_c(d)}).
+$$
+
+由 (UJB.7402)，对 $k\ne c$，$P_k^{\otimes r}$ 下至少一个因子（$d=k$）均值为零，故
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_{P_k^{\otimes r}}h_c=0\quad(k\ne c),
+\qquad
+\alpha_c:=\mathbb E_{P_c^{\otimes r}}h_c\ge\Delta^r.
+\tag{UJB.7406}
+$$
+

+$F:B\times(C\sqcup T)\to[-1,1]$ 定义一个复合记录上的函数 $G_F$：在终端

+
+$$
+G_F(b,\mathsf{succ},w_1,\ldots,w_r)
+ =\sum_{c\in C}F(b,c)\frac{h_c(w_1,\ldots,w_r)}{\alpha_c}.
+$$

+
+沿用 §481 与 §485 的记号。定理 485.2–485.3 在 RH 不成立时给出 $\liminf\mathcal T=-\infty$ 与 $\limsup\mathcal T=+\infty$，在 RH 下只给出 $\liminf\mathcal T\le-1/2\le1/2\le\limsup\mathcal T$。本节在 RH 下也得到两侧无界，于是两侧无界无条件成立。工具是正测度的 Laplace 变换在虚轴上的边界极限满足的有限 Gram 正性。下侧只用到零点有无穷多个；上侧还要用到零点计数的增长与 $0$ 附近的无零点间隙。

+经典输入除 §485 所列各项外，还有 Riemann–von Mangoldt 公式
+$$
+N(T,2T)=\frac T{2\pi}\Bigl(\log\frac T{2\pi}+2\log2-1\Bigr)+O(\log T),
+\tag{486.1}
+$$
+其中 $N(T_1,T_2)$ 是纵坐标落在 $(T_1,T_2]$ 中的非平凡零点个数（计重数）。下文只用它推出的 $N(T,2T)/T\to\infty$。

+$$
+L(t)=\lim_{\sigma\downarrow0}\sigma\,G(\sigma+it).
+$$

+# Three-state overlap interval propagation is not always optimal
+
+## Problem
+
+E. F. Galvão and D. J. Brod, *Quantum and classical bounds for two-state overlaps*, Phys. Rev. A 101, 062110 (2020), arXiv:1902.11039v3, Section II.B, `overlap_pra_v3.tex`, line 165:
+
+> We leave it as an open question whether this procedure is optimal, but emphasize that even the initial iteration that produces a complete graph already provides bounds for every pair of vertices, which may be useful even if not tight.
+
+The procedure is specified at lines 151–156: use the three-state bounds through each common neighbour of an unmeasured pair, intersect the inferred intervals, add the edge, and continue. Line 165 also allows revisiting inferred edges. The source's definitions and bounds are at lines 97–131; see [the literature note](../Library/Observer/galvaobrod2020overlaps.md).
+
+Issue [#23699](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23699) fixes the reading to graphs with exactly one unknown pair. Write
+$U(x,y)=(\sqrt{xy}+\sqrt{(1-x)(1-y)})^2$, and let $L(x,y)=(\sqrt{xy}-\sqrt{(1-x)(1-y)})^2$ when $x+y>1$, and $L(x,y)=0$ otherwise. These are the module's `upper` and `lower`.
+
+For $m$ labelled states, distinct indices $i_0,j_0$, and an array $r$, a realization is a family of unit vectors $\psi_i\in\mathbb C^n$ satisfying $|\langle\psi_i,\psi_j\rangle|^2=r_{ij}$ for every ordered pair of distinct indices except the unordered pair $\{i_0,j_0\}$. Diagonal entries impose no conditions. The set $F$ of feasible unknown overlaps ranges over every finite dimension $n$. The procedure's endpoints are
+$\ell=\sup\{L(r_{ki_0},r_{kj_0}):k\ne i_0,j_0\}$ and $u=\inf\{U(r_{ki_0},r_{kj_0}):k\ne i_0,j_0\}$, encoded by `procLower` and `procUpper`.
+
+The proposition `claim` asserts that, for every $m\ge3$, every distinct $i_0,j_0$, and every $r$ with $F\ne\varnothing$, both $\ell=\inf F$ and $u=\sup F$. This universal tightness statement is refuted.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Inferring unmeasured overlaps from measured ones is the paper's organizing problem. Section IV.B applies overlap bounds to characterizing multiphoton indistinguishability with fewer pairwise measurements. Optimal propagation would recover the strongest bounds allowed by all the measured overlaps. The counterexample separates bounds obtained from individual triples from constraints requiring the same states to realize all measured pairs together.

+
+## 1. Graphs and joint profiles
+
+All graphs below are finite, simple and connected. For integers $n\ge2$ and $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal G(n,\ell)$ be the graphs with $n$ vertices and
+
+$$
+m=n-1+\ell
+$$
+
+edges. For an edge $uv$ write
+
+$$
+r_{uv}=\frac{\min(d_u,d_v)}{\max(d_u,d_v)},\qquad
+g(r)=\sqrt{1+r^2}-1,
+$$
+
+and set
+
+$$
+E(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}g(r_{uv}),\qquad
+\Phi(G)=m+E(G),
+$$
+
+so minimizing the CDSO index $\Phi$ at fixed $(n,\ell)$ is the same as minimizing $E$. These are the conventions of *CDSO sink incidences and density limits*, §§1--3.
+
+A two-layer graph has independent hubs $[s]=\{1,\ldots,s\}$ and sources outside $[s]$, with every edge joining a source to a hub. For a source $v$, write $T(v)\subseteq[s]$ for its nonempty hub neighborhood. If $N_T$ is the number of sources with $T(v)=T$, put
+
+$$
+N_s=n-s,\qquad x_T=\frac{N_T}{N_s},\qquad
+y_i=\sum_{T\ni i}x_T.
+$$
+
+The same source distribution determines every quantity below. Its mean source degree and excess are
+
+$$
+q=\sum_{\varnothing\ne T\subseteq[s]}|T|x_T=\sum_{i=1}^s y_i,
+\qquad a=q-1=\sum_T(|T|-1)x_T.
+$$
+
+The normalized joint profile domain is
+
+$$
+\mathcal P_s(a)=\left\{(x_T):
+\begin{array}{l}
+x_T\ge0,\quad \sum_Tx_T=1,\quad \sum_T(|T|-1)x_T=a,\\
+ y_i=\sum_{T\ni i}x_T>0\quad(1\le i\le s)
+\end{array}\right\}.
+$$
+
+For $x\in\mathcal P_s(a)$ define the profile energy
+
+$$
+J_s(x)=\frac12\sum_Tx_T|T|^2\sum_{i\in T}\frac1{y_i^2}.
+$$
+
+The positivity condition on every $y_i$ is the finite-energy hub condition. Types of zero mass remain in the domain.
+
+For an actual two-layer graph, the same edge count gives
+
+$$
+\sum_TN_T=N_s,\qquad
+\sum_T(|T|-1)N_T=\ell+s-1,
+\qquad D_i=\sum_{T\ni i}N_T,
+$$
+
+and therefore
+
+$$
+a=\frac{\ell+s-1}{N_s},\qquad q=\frac{m}{N_s}.
+$$
+
+The elementary remainder identity
+
+$$
+0\le \frac{r^2}{2}-g(r)
+=\frac{r^4}{2(\sqrt{1+r^2}+1)^2}
+\le \frac{r^4}{8}
+$$
+
+will always be applied to the actual source--hub edges.

+
+$$

+
+$$

+
