+and let $H^{(4)}_{n,\ell}$ be the two-layer graph with four hubs, $c$ sources adjacent to all four hubs, and $b$ sources adjacent to all but one hub, with the four missing-hub counts equal to $q+1$ for $r$ hubs and $q$ for the other $4-r$ hubs. Its hub degrees are $N-q-1$ on the first group and $N-q$ on the second group.
+
+**Lemma 4.1 (The balanced candidate has a uniform upper bound).** With $a_4=(\ell+3)/N\in[2,3]$,
+
+$$
+E(H^{(4)}_{n,\ell})
+\le \frac{F_4(a_4)}{N}+\frac{204}{N^3}<\frac{34}{n}.
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Put $y_i=D_i/N$. The four missing-hub counts differ by at most one, so
+
+$$
+\sum_{i=1}^4\left(y_i-\frac{a_4+1}{4}\right)^2\le\frac1{N^2}.
+$$
+
+For the pure three- and four-neighborhood profile,
+
+$$
+J_4=\sum_{i=1}^4h_{a_4}(y_i),
+\qquad
+h_a(y)=\frac9{2y}+\frac{7(a-2)}{2y^2}.
+$$
+
+On $1/2\le y\le1$ and $2\le a\le3$,
+
+$$
+0<h_a''(y)=\frac9{y^3}+\frac{21(a-2)}{y^4}\le408.
+$$
+
+Taylor's theorem around $(a_4+1)/4$, whose first-order terms sum to zero, gives
+
+$$
+J_4\le F_4(a_4)+204N^{-2}.
+$$
+
+Since $g(t)\le t^2/2$, the same upper bound divided by $N$ holds for $E(H^{(4)}_{n,\ell})$. Finally $F_4(a_4)\le32$ and
+$(1+4/N)(32+204/N^2)<34$ for $N\ge2{,}999{,}996$. ∎
+
+**Theorem 4.2 (Exact four-hub minimum at the specified finite orders).** For every integer pair $(n,\ell)$ in the range above, $H^{(4)}_{n,\ell}$ is the unique minimizing isomorphism class in $\mathcal G(n,\ell)$. Its exact minimum excess is
+
+$$
+E^\ast(n,\ell)
+=(4-r)M_c(N-q)+rM_c(N-q-1),
+$$
+
+and the exact minimum CDSO index is
+
+$$
+\Phi^\ast(n,\ell)=n-1+\ell+E^\ast(n,\ell).
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Let $G$ minimize $E$ and compare it with $H^{(4)}_{n,\ell}$. Lemma 4.1 gives $E(G)<34/n$. The sink-incidence reduction in *CDSO sink incidences and density limits*, Theorem 3.1, with $C=34$, applies because its explicit sufficient threshold is
+
+$$
+36\cdot34^2\cdot69=2{,}871{,}504<3{,}000{,}000.
+$$
+
+Thus $G$ is two-layer, has at most nine hubs, and every hub degree is at least $n/102$. A two-layer graph with $s\le3$ hubs has at most $s(n-s)\le3n-9$ edges, while the present graphs have
+$m\ge3n-8$; hence $s\ge4$.
+
+Suppose $s\ge5$. Put $N_s=n-s$ and $a_s=(\ell+s-1)/N_s$. The scalar incidence bound in the proof of Theorem 2.4 is valid for this $a_s$ as well, and the edge remainder gives
+
+$$
+E(G)\ge \frac{J_s}{N_s}-\frac{B}{n^3},
+\qquad
+B=\frac{9^4 102^4}{2}=355091870088.
+$$
+
+Because $s\ge5$, $a_s\ge a_4$, and the certificate is increasing in $s$ and $a$, so
+
+$$
+E(G)\ge\frac{40+\frac{32}{3}(a_4-3)}{N}-\frac{B}{n^3}
+>\frac{F_4(a_4)+4}{N}-\frac{B}{n^3}.
+$$
+
+The last expression is larger than the upper bound in Lemma 4.1: indeed
+
+$$
+\frac{B}{n^2}+\frac{204}{N^2}<4
+$$
+
+at $n\ge3{,}000{,}000$. This contradiction leaves $s=4$.
+
+For four hubs, Lemma 2.1 gives, for every hub $i$,
+
+$$
+\sum_{T\ni i}|T|^2N_T\ge9D_i.
+$$
+
+Every edge cost is at most $34/n$, so the edge inequality
+$g(r)\ge r^2/(2+34/n)$ and the preceding display imply
+
+$$
+E(G)\ge\frac9{(2+34/n)D_i}.
+$$
+
+Since $E(G)<34/n$ and $n\ge3{,}000{,}000$, this gives $D_i\ge n/8$ for every hub. The remainder bound now improves to
+
+$$
+E(G)\ge\frac{J_4}{N}-\frac{B_0}{n^3},
+\qquad
+B_0=\frac{4^4 8^4}{2}=524288.
+$$
+
+Let $p_k=\sum_{|T|=k}x_T$. Summing the residuals in Lemma 2.1 for $s=4$ gives
+
+$$
+\sum_iR_i=48p_1+18p_2.
+$$
+
+Because $y_i\le1$, the exact decomposition in that lemma yields
+
+$$
+J_4\ge F_4(a_4)+24p_1+9p_2.
+$$
+
+If $p_1+p_2>0$, integrality gives $24p_1+9p_2\ge9/N$, and therefore
+
+$$
+E(G)\ge\frac{F_4(a_4)}N+\frac9{N^2}-\frac{B_0}{n^3}
+>\frac{F_4(a_4)}N+\frac{204}{N^3}\ge E(H^{(4)}_{n,\ell}),
+$$
+
+where the strict inequality follows from
+$B_0/n+204/N<9$. Hence $p_1=p_2=0$.
+
+It follows that exactly $c$ sources have degree four and exactly $b$ have degree three. If $b_i$ is the number of degree-three sources missing hub $i$, then
+
+$$
+\sum_i b_i=b,\qquad D_i=N-b_i,\qquad
+E(G)=\sum_{i=1}^4M_c(D_i).
+$$
+
+For $f_k(D)=g(k/D)$,
+
+$$
+ f_k''(D)=\frac{k^2(3D^2+2k^2)}{D^3(D^2+k^2)^{3/2}}.
+$$
+
+Writing
+
+$$
+Q_D(t)=\frac{t(3D^2+2t)}{(D^2+t)^{3/2}},
+$$
+
+we have
+
+$$
+Q_D'(t)=\frac{6D^4+5D^2t+2t^2}{2(D^2+t)^{5/2}}>0.
+$$
+
+Also
+
+$$
+M_c''(D)=\frac9{(D^2+9)^{3/2}}+c\bigl(f_4''(D)-f_3''(D)\bigr)>0.
+$$
+
+If $D_j\ge D_i+2$, then $b_i\ge b_j+2$, so choose a degree-three source $v$ missing $i$. It is adjacent to $j$. Delete $vj$ and add $vi$, making $v$ a source missing $j$. Since $vi$ was absent, no repeated edge or loop is introduced. The $c\ge4$ full-neighborhood sources are unchanged and connect all four hubs; every other source still has three or four hub neighbors. Thus the graph remains simple and connected, with the same $n,m,\ell$, the same numbers of hubs and sources, and the same source-degree counts $b,c$. Only $(D_i,D_j)$ changes, to $(D_i+1,D_j-1)$, and strict convexity of $M_c$ strictly lowers the energy. Repeating the exchange proves that every minimizer has the four $b_i$ differing by at most one. The resulting multiset is uniquely $q+1$ repeated $r$ times and $q$ repeated $4-r$ times. The full and missing-one neighborhoods then determine the graph up to hub and source relabelling, giving the stated unique isomorphism class and exact value. ∎

+## 5. Density limits and complete near-minimum structure
+
+**Theorem 5.1 (The four-hub density phase).** Let $(\ell_n)$ be an integer sequence with
+
+$$
+\frac{\ell_n}{n}\longrightarrow\alpha\in[2,3),
+\qquad
+\ell_n\ge2n-7
+$$
+
+for all sufficiently large $n$. Then eventually $\ell_n\le3n-15$, and
+
+$$
+\lim_{n\to\infty}nE^\ast(n,\ell_n)
+=F_4(\alpha)=\frac{8(37\alpha-47)}{(1+\alpha)^2}.
+$$
+
+For any choice $G_n\in\mathcal G(n,\ell_n)$, the following are equivalent:
+
+1. $E(G_n)-E^\ast(n,\ell_n)=o(n^{-1})$;
+2. $nE(G_n)\to F_4(\alpha)$;
+3. After labelling the hubs whenever they exist, $G_n$ is eventually a two-layer graph with exactly four hubs, and its profile satisfies
+   $$
+   x_{[4],n}\to\alpha-2,
+   \qquad
+   x_{[4]\setminus\{i\},n}\to\frac{3-\alpha}{4}\quad(1\le i\le4),
+   $$
+   while the total mass of all one- and two-neighborhood types tends to zero. Equivalently, $G_n$ is eventually a two-layer graph with exactly four hubs, the total mass of all one- and two-neighborhood types tends to zero, and
+   $$
+   \frac{D_{i,n}}n\to\frac{1+\alpha}{4}\quad(1\le i\le4).
+   $$
+
+The exact finite minimizers supplied by Theorem 4.2 have no one- or two-neighborhood sources. Near-minimizing sequences only force their total number to be $o(n)$; zero-limit types may occur at finitely many or sublinear many vertices to provide a connected bridge.
+
+**Proof.** Since $\alpha<3$, the upper finite capacity inequality holds eventually, so Theorem 4.2 applies and gives the exact minimum for all sufficiently large $n$. Its balanced profile has $a_4\to\alpha$, and the same remainder estimate used in §4 gives
+
+$$
+ nE^\ast(n,\ell_n)\longrightarrow F_4(\alpha).
+$$
+
+Thus (1) and (2) are equivalent.
+
+Assume (2). The sequence has bounded $nE(G_n)$, so the sink-incidence reduction gives an eventual two-layer graph with a bounded number of hubs and hub degrees bounded below linearly. Passing to a subsequence with fixed hub number and a convergent profile is legitimate because there are finitely many types for each fixed number. The exact edge identities give a limit profile in $\mathcal P_s(\alpha)$. Write $x_n$ for the profiles on this fixed-$s$ subsequence and $x$ for their limit. Choose a fixed $C>0$ bounding $nE(G_n)$. The same actual-edge calculation as in §3 applies uniformly: the fixed-$C$ reduction bounds $s$ solely in terms of $C$ and gives $D_{i,n}\ge n/(3C)$, so source degrees are bounded, every edge ratio is $O_C(n^{-1})$, and there are $O_C(n)$ edges. Summing the remainder in §1 therefore gives an $O_C(n^{-3})$ error in $E(G_n)$, and hence
+
+$$
+nE(G_n)-\frac{n}{n-s}J_s(x_n)=O_C(n^{-2})\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+
+The same degree bound gives $y_{i,n}=D_{i,n}/(n-s)\ge1/(3C)>0$. Thus $J_s$ is continuous at the limit profile, including boundary faces where some type masses vanish while all hub masses remain positive, and $J_s(x_n)\to J_s(x)$. Since $n/(n-s)\to1$, it follows that $nE(G_n)\to J_s(x)$. If $s\ge5$ occurs infinitely often, Theorem 2.4 gives a limiting value strictly larger than $F_4(\alpha)$, a contradiction. The capacity inequality excludes $s\le3$ because $\ell_n\ge2n-7$. Hence exactly four hubs occur eventually. Every profile limit must attain equality in Theorem 2.2, so all profile limits are the unique profile displayed in (3). Therefore the whole sequence of profiles converges, including the vanishing total mass of the one- and two-neighborhood types and the hub-degree limits.
+
+To verify the alternative formulation of (3), use the same profile array throughout and put
+
+$$
+p_{k,n}=\sum_{|T|=k}x_{T,n},\qquad
+L_{i,n}=\sum_{\substack{|T|\le2\\i\in T}}x_{T,n},\qquad
+y_{i,n}=\frac{D_{i,n}}{n-4}.
+$$
+
+Its exact mean constraint is $a_n=(\ell_n+3)/(n-4)=p_{2,n}+2p_{3,n}+3p_{4,n}\to\alpha$. Together with $\sum_{k=1}^4p_{k,n}=1$, it gives the exact identities
+
+$$
+p_{4,n}=a_n-2+2p_{1,n}+p_{2,n},
+\qquad
+x_{[4]\setminus\{i\},n}
+=1-p_{1,n}-p_{2,n}+L_{i,n}-y_{i,n}.
+$$
+
+Since $0\le L_{i,n}\le p_{1,n}+p_{2,n}$ and $(n-4)/n\to1$, vanishing one- and two-type mass together with $D_{i,n}/n\to(1+\alpha)/4$ forces $p_{4,n}\to\alpha-2$ and each missing-one mass to tend to $(3-\alpha)/4$. Conversely, the complete candidate profile in (3) gives
+
+$$
+y_{i,n}=p_{4,n}+\sum_{j\ne i}x_{[4]\setminus\{j\},n}+L_{i,n}
+\longrightarrow\alpha-2+\frac{3(3-\alpha)}4=\frac{1+\alpha}4,
+$$
+
+and hence the stated hub-degree limits. Both formulations retain the eventual four-hub two-layer condition and the vanishing one- and two-type mass.
+
+Conversely, (3) gives a profile converging to the equality profile of Theorem 2.2. The actual-edge remainder identity then gives $nE(G_n)\to F_4(\alpha)$, proving (3)$\Rightarrow$(2). ∎
+
+The lower capacity condition has a genuine endpoint obstruction. At $\ell=2n-8$, the graph $K_{3,n-3}$ belongs to $\mathcal G(n,\ell)$ and
+
+$$
+ nE(K_{3,n-3})\longrightarrow\frac{27}{2},
+$$
+
+whereas $F_4(2)=24$. Thus density $\alpha=2$ alone does not replace the exact lower budget $\ell\ge2n-7$. At the other boundary, $\ell=3n-14$ exceeds the four-hub simple two-layer capacity $3n-15$; the four-hub theorem therefore stops at $\alpha<3$ and makes no claim for the next capacity phase.
+
+## 6. Literature and scope
+
+The fixed-order conventions and the earlier two-hub convexity, expansion and density arguments are in [*CDSO minimizers without a universal vertex for every cyclomatic number*](CDSO_UNIVERSAL_VERTEX_ALL_CYCLOMATIC.md), §8 (*The unique eventual minimizer*) and §§10--12 (*A linear range for rigidity and the exact minimum*, *Uniform hub expansion and quantitative stability*, and *Limits with varying cyclomatic number*); the density theorem in §12 covers $0\le\alpha<1/8$ and a conditional endpoint at $\alpha=1/8$. The fixed-$C$ two-layer reduction used in §§4--5 is [*CDSO sink incidences and density limits*](CDSO_SINK_INCIDENCE_AND_DENSITY_LIMITS.md), Theorem 3.1 (*Uniform two-layer reduction at fixed cost*). Its Theorems 5.2--5.3 (*Necessary profiles and exact-budget realization* and *The hub boundary and the unique global optimizing profile*) give the preceding actual joint-profile/realization interface and hub-boundary analysis in their stated range $0\le\alpha<1$. Those subunit-density conclusions do not supply the four-hub phase by extrapolation. The actual-edge bridge needed here is derived in §§1 and 3 and applied uniformly in §§4--5 of this volume, and the exact-budget realization is proved in Theorem 3.1 here; the new load-bearing profile relations are the residual identity in Lemma 2.1 and the scalar certificate in Lemma 2.3.
+
+The original CDSO definition and the universal-vertex conjecture are in A. M. Albalahi, S. Das, A. Ali, J. Barman and A. E. Hamza, *On the hyperbolic Sombor index and its counterpart*, Discrete Mathematics Letters 16 (2025), 108--115, DOI [10.47443/dml.2025.176](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2025.176), §1 and §4. The unicyclic comparison recorded in A. Ali, K. C. Das and A. A. Attiya, *Bond incident degree indices of fixed-order unicyclic graphs*, Discrete Mathematics Letters 16 (2025), 135--142, DOI [10.47443/dml.2025.192](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2025.192), Remark 2.3, is prior one-cycle evidence and is not used as a high-density profile theorem. The two-hub construction in A. M. Albalahi, *On Two Conjectures Concerning the Hyperbolic Sombor Index and Its Counterpart*, Discrete Mathematics Letters 18 (2026), 122--128, DOI [10.47443/dml.2026.217](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2026.217), Proposition 2.1, is likewise a cited intermediate construction; its maximum theorem is a different extremal problem.
+
+The coordinate-increasing hypothesis in H. Liu, Z. Du, Y. Huang, H. Chen and S. Elumalai, *Note on the Minimum Bond Incident Degree Indices of $k$-Cyclic Graphs*, MATCH Communications in Mathematical and Computer Chemistry 91 (2024), 255--266, DOI [10.46793/match.91-1.255L](https://doi.org/10.46793/match.91-1.255L), does not hold for $g(y/x)$ at fixed $y$ when $x>y$. Likewise, condition P2 in M. Bašić, *A general algebraic characterization of extremal $\Delta$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices*, [arXiv:2610.34361](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34361), is not satisfied by CDSO for $x<\Delta$. Those results therefore do not supply the four-hub theorem above.
+
+The full text of Zhao--Zhao, DOI [10.21136/CMJ.2026.0075-26](https://doi.org/10.21136/CMJ.2026.0075-26), has not been obtained; its overlap with these results and the associated priority questions remain unassessed. Its abstract is not used to exclude overlap, and the finite literature comparison here does not certify global originality.
+
+The fixed-density statements here concern $\alpha\in[2,3)$ and the exact lower budget stated in Theorem 5.1. They do not determine the exact minimum for a fixed $s\ge5$, the least finite order threshold below $3{,}000{,}000$, or any capacity phase beginning at $\alpha=3$.

+从正向小圆 $|z|=r<1$ 的柯西系数积分出发，把它扩为半径 $R$ 的圆周加上割线 $[1,R]$ 的两岸。先在割线两侧留正宽度，并在 $1$ 和 $R$ 留小的连接弧，取不经过 $0$ 的边界；被积函数为 $\mathcal A(z)z^{-n-1}$，除 $0$ 外没有极点。取正向边界时，外圆逆时针，上岸从 $1$ 走向 $R$，下岸从 $R$ 回到 $1$，绕 $1$ 的内弧顺时针。由留数定理，整个边界积分除以 $2\pi i$ 等于 $a_n$。
+
+先固定 $n$ 与离 $1,R$ 正距离的两岸线段，使割线宽度趋于零。$U,V$ 在闭半圆盘上的连续性使该收敛在这些紧线段上一致。$R$ 处的连接弧长度趋于零，分母在那里远离零，分子由两侧连续性有界，所以该连接弧积分趋于零；外圆删去的小弧也同样消失。$1$ 处半径 $\varepsilon$ 的连接弧长至多 $2\pi\varepsilon$，且 $|z|\ge1-\varepsilon$；定理 2.3 的全域端点极限使 $\mathcal A$ 在其两侧一致有界，故其积分范数为
+
+$$
+O_n\bigl(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)^{-n-1}\bigr)\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+
+两岸积分在 $1$ 处绝对可积，因为 $U,V$ 连续且有限，在 $R$ 处亦然。这些估计允许最后使两端的小弧半径趋于零；不要求对 $n$ 一致地交换极限。得到精确恒等式
+
+$$
+a_n=E_n+\frac1{2\pi i}\int_1^R
+       \frac{U(x)-V(x)}{x^{n+1}}\,dx
+    =E_n+\frac1\pi\int_1^R\frac{\operatorname{Im}U(x)}{x^{n+1}}\,dx,
+$$
+
+其中 $E_n$ 是带有上述单侧端值的正向外圆积分除以 $2\pi i$。两岸差为 $2i\operatorname{Im}U$，所以符号是加号。外圆长为 $2\pi R$，于是
+
+$$
+|\operatorname{Re}E_n|\le |E_n|\le BR^{-n}.
+$$
+
+令 $h(x)=-\operatorname{Im}U(x)$。它在 $[1,R]$ 连续，在 $1<x\le R$ 严格为正，$h(1)=0$。选取固定的 $1<\alpha<\beta<R$，则
+
+$$
+m=\min_{\alpha\le x\le\beta}h(x)>0,\qquad
+\frac1\pi\int_1^R\frac{h(x)}{x^{n+1}}\,dx
+ \ge\frac{m(\beta-\alpha)}{\pi\beta^{n+1}}.
+$$
+
+$a_n$ 为实数，故取前式的实部可得
+
+$$
+a_n\le BR^{-n}-\frac{m(\beta-\alpha)}{\pi\beta^{n+1}}<0
+$$
+
+当 $n$ 足够大时最后一步成立，因为 $(\beta/R)^n\to0$。这同时控制外圆误差和严格负积分的优势；没有使用无限远轮廓、割线远端的符号或全局奇点分类。
+
+## 4. 总和、有限前缀与全部正整数平滑次数
+
+**定理 4.1（全参数最终符号与严格可容许下界）。** 对每个整数 $d\ge1$、$\boldsymbol{k}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}^d$ 与整数 $\ell\ge1$，存在整数 $N_0(\boldsymbol{k},\ell)\ge0$ 使
+
+$$
+C_n^{0;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}<0\qquad(n\ge N_0).
+$$
+
+对每个进一步固定的整数 $j\ge1$，存在整数 $N_j(\boldsymbol{k},\ell,j)\ge0$ 使
+
+$$
+C_n^{j;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}>0\qquad(n\ge N_j).
+$$
+
+若 $k_1>1$，同样可取 $N_j$ 使
+
+$$
+C_n^{j;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}
+ >Z^{-\ell}\binom{n+j-1}{n}\qquad(n\ge N_j).
+$$
+
+每个有限前导一块都在量词之内；阈值只针对各组固定参数。
+
+证明。沿用 $a_n$ 与 $\lambda$，取定理 3.1 的 $N\ge1$。先证明绝对收敛及总和，不能仅从径向极限推断它们。置 $P(r)=\sum_{m<N}a_mr^m$、$q_m=-a_m>0$（$m\ge N$）。对 $0\le r<1$，
+
+$$
+\sum_{m\ge N}q_mr^m=P(r)-A(r).
+$$
+
+当 $r\uparrow1$，右侧趋于有限值 $P(1)-\lambda$。左侧各项非负并单调增加，单调收敛定理给出 $\sum_{m\ge N}q_m=P(1)-\lambda<\infty$。有限前缀可取绝对值，故
+
+$$
+\sum_{m\ge0}|a_m|<\infty,\qquad
+\sum_{m\ge0}a_m=\lambda.
+$$
+
+令 $b_n=C_n^{1;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}=\sum_{m=0}^na_m$，$e_n=b_n-\lambda$。对 $n\ge N$，
+
+$$
+e_n=-\sum_{m>n}a_m=\sum_{m>n}q_m>0.
+$$
+
+因而 $b_n>\lambda\ge0$，已得 $j=1$ 的全部结论。注意 $e_n\to0$，所以仅有最终严格正性还不足以控制下一次求和的有限带符号前缀。
+
+由于 $e_n$ 的负项只可能在有限前缀内，其总和 $T=\sum_{n\ge0}e_n$ 在 $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ 中存在。对 $0\le r<1$，绝对收敛的卷积给出
+
+$$
+\sum_{n\ge0}e_nr^n=\frac{A(r)-\lambda}{1-r}.
+$$
+
+这里绝对收敛也可由 $b_n$ 有界直接推出。对 $n\ge N$ 的非负尾部再用单调收敛，有限前缀按多项式取极限，得到扩展实数意义的精确等式
+
+$$
+T=\lim_{r\uparrow1}\frac{A(r)-\lambda}{1-r}.
+$$
+
+若 $k_1>1$，`CompositionBoundary.result head tail` 给出 $\sum f_m=Z$。因此对 $0\le r<1$，
+
+$$
+0<F_{\boldsymbol{k}}(r)\le Z,\qquad
+Z-F_{\boldsymbol{k}}(r)
+ =\sum_{m\ge1}f_m(1-r^m)\ge f_1(1-r).
+$$
+
+函数 $x\mapsto x^{-\ell}$ 在正实轴凸，其在 $Z$ 处的切线界给出
+
+$$
+\frac{A(r)-Z^{-\ell}}{1-r}
+ \ge\ell Z^{-\ell-1}\frac{Z-F_{\boldsymbol{k}}(r)}{1-r}
+ \ge\ell Z^{-\ell-1}f_1>0.
+$$
+
+于是 $T\ge\ell Z^{-\ell-1}f_1>0$，允许 $T=+\infty$；不需要假设 $F'(1)$ 有限。
+
+若 $k_1=1$，则 $\lambda=0$。取定理 2.3 的 $D\ge1$ 与 $M$，保留深度归一化，得到
+
+$$
+\frac{A(r)}{1-r}
+ \ge\frac{r^{d\ell}}{D^\ell(1-r)(1+|\log(1-r)|)^{M\ell}}
+ \longrightarrow+\infty\qquad(r\uparrow1).
+$$
+
+确实 $r^{d\ell}\to1$，而对每个固定整数 $p\ge0$ 有 $t(1+|\log t|)^p\to0$（置 $t=e^{-u}$ 即为指数胜过多项式）。因此前导一情形 $T=+\infty$，没有以可容许边界总和代替这里的发散证明。
+
+现在 $T>0$ 在两种情形都已成立。因此
+
+$$
+d_n^{(2)}:=\sum_{m=0}^n e_m\longrightarrow T
+$$
+
+并存在 $\delta>0$、整数 $M_2$，使 $d_n^{(2)}\ge\delta$ 对 $n\ge M_2$ 成立。若 $T$ 有限，可取 $\delta=T/2$；若 $T=+\infty$，可取 $\delta=1$。这已经包含 $e_0,\ldots,e_{N-1}$ 的全部符号贡献。
+
+设 $d^{(1)}=e$，递归定义 $d_n^{(j+1)}=\sum_{m=0}^n d_m^{(j)}$。每次求和保留有限前缀：若 $d_m^{(j)}\ge\delta_j>0$ 对 $m\ge M_j$ 成立，则
+
+$$
+d_n^{(j+1)}
+ \ge-\sum_{m<M_j}|d_m^{(j)}|
+       +\delta_j(n-M_j+1)\longrightarrow+\infty.
+$$
+
+从 $j=2$ 起该式归纳给出每个固定 $j\ge2$ 的最终严格正性，并为下一次求和提供正的常数下界；$j=1$ 则由正尾和给出。没有把最终正性直接当成正总和或发散。
+
+最后，定理 2.2 的重复求和式与二项恒等式
+
+$$
+\sum_{m=0}^n\binom{m+j-1}{m}=\binom{n+j}{n}
+$$
+
+给出对所有 $n\ge0,j\ge1$ 的恒等式
+
+$$
+d_n^{(j)}=C_n^{j;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}
+                -\lambda\binom{n+j-1}{n}.
+$$
+
+因而当 $\lambda=0$ 时得到最终正性；当 $\lambda=Z^{-\ell}>0$ 时得到所述严格下界以及正性。取相应的有限阈值并与 $0$ 比较，即完成全部量词。
+
+## 5. 必要边界与后续系数问题
+
+**命题 5.1（初始指标及求和前缀的反例）。** 定理 4.1 中的最终限定不可替换为所有指标，也不能在重复求和中删除总和为正的论证。
+
+证明。当 $\boldsymbol{k}=(1)$、$\ell=2$ 时，$-\operatorname{Log}(1-z)=z+z^2/2+z^3/3+z^4/4+\cdots$，精确形式除法给出
+
+$$
+\left(\frac{z}{-\operatorname{Log}(1-z)}\right)^2
+ =1-z+\frac{z^2}{12}+0z^3+O(z^4).
+$$
+
+所以 $a_0>0$、$a_2>0$、$a_3=0$，均与所有指标严格为负不相容。对 $\boldsymbol{k}=(2)$，有 $F(z)=1+z/4+O(z^2)$；取 $\ell=5,j=1$，则
+
+$$
+C_1^{1;(2);5}=1-5/4=-1/4<0,
+$$
+
+故即使可容许也不能把最终正性换成所有指标正性。另取实序列 $v_0=-2$、$v_n=2^{-n}$（$n\ge1$），则尾部严格为正，但 $\sum_{m=0}^nv_m=-1-2^{-n}<0$。因此前缀控制所需的正总和或发散条件不能仅由尾部正性替代。
+
+**定义 5.2（精确阈值问题）。** 对固定参数，定义
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\nu_0(\boldsymbol{k},\ell)
+ &=\min\{N\ge0:\ \forall n\ge N,\ C_n^{0;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}<0\},\\
+\nu_j(\boldsymbol{k},\ell)
+ &=\min\{N\ge0:\ \forall n\ge N,\ C_n^{j;\boldsymbol{k};\ell}
+        >\lambda\binom{n+j-1}{n}\}\quad(j\ge1).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+定理 4.1 保证这些集合非空；命题 5.1 表明有限前缀仍有实质内容。确定这些最小阈值及其随组合、$\ell$、$j$ 的依赖，是与本卷存在性结论相区别的后续问题。有限割线证明使用依赖参数的 $R_0,\rho$ 和正积分区间；它不提供统一或有效阈值、全局奇点信息或系数主项。

+# Contraction of the Actual Free-Root Trace Energy
+
+## Abstract
+
+A real one-Lipschitz map contracts the original free-root trace energy on the fixed golden biased probability space.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (potential).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.potential`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.potential` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an arbitrary real root value c and original square-summable edge increments z, potential(c,z,p) is c plus the sum of z over all nonempty prefixes of the finite address p.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (contractedCoordinate).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractedCoordinate`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractedCoordinate` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On a nonempty edge p, the contracted coordinate is chi(potential(c,z,p)) minus chi(potential(c,z,dropLast(p))).
+
+**Definition 1.3 (contracted).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contracted`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contracted` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a real one-Lipschitz chi, these original-edge coordinates form an element of the original edge ell2 space. Each coordinate has absolute value at most that of the corresponding original increment.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (contractLp).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractLp`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.contractLp` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Composition by chi in the actual G=L2(Omega,M) is defined as the actual constant chi(0) plus composition by x mapped to chi(x)-chi(0). The shifted map vanishes at zero and is one-Lipschitz, so its L2 composition is defined. The probability measure is the original phi-biased product law M.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Actual Trace Contraction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.actual_trace_contraction`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup.actual_trace_contraction` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real one-Lipschitz map chi and every F in the original free-root trace domain D, contractLp(chi,F) equals chi composed with F almost everywhere for the actual measure M, belongs to D, and has original infimum energy at most energy(F). No condition chi(0)=0 is imposed.
+
+Choose the attained least-energy extension F=constG(c)+Jz. Contract its value at every finite vertex and take differences along the original edges. The one-Lipschitz inequality bounds every new increment by its original increment, hence bounds the entire ell2 norm. Telescoping gives the contracted original potential at every finite vertex, including the freely transformed root chi(c).
+
+The actual trace of the depth projection P_h z equals the finite prefix sum along each ray almost everywhere for M. The finite edge cutoffs are cofinal among finite subsets, so the square-summable single-edge expansion proves P_h z tends to z. Boundedness of the actual J and continuity of shifted Lipschitz composition pass the exact finite-depth telescoping identity to G. Thus the contracted trace is exactly constG(chi(c))+J(contracted increments). The attained-energy comparison then proves the energy inequality.
+
+This establishes the normal-contraction property of the actual free-root form. It does not assert order preservation of the spectral heat semigroup. That conclusion additionally requires the associated resolvent minimizer, clipping comparison and the strong limit of resolvent powers, together with compatible polar and operator coordinates.
+

+# Robustness of ancilla-free testers
+
+## Abstract
+
+Ancilla-free testers with a common normalization state have the robustness of their canonical POVMs.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Quantum testers).**
+
+$$\forall (y: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (x: \operatorname{Type}), (\forall (j: \operatorname{Type}), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(y\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(x\right)], ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(j\right)], (\forall (t: (j) \to (\operatorname{Matrix}\left((y \times x), (y \times x), \mathbb{C}\right))), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester}\left(t\right)) \Leftrightarrow ((\forall (a: j), (\operatorname{Matrix.PosSemidef}\left(t\left(a\right)\right))) \land (\exists (\sigma: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(x, x, \mathbb{C}\right)), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.Information.SLDSpectralEnergy.IsDensity}\left(\sigma\right)) \land (\sum_{a: j} (t\left(a\right)) = \operatorname{Matrix.kronecker}\left((1: \operatorname{Matrix}\left(y, y, \mathbb{C}\right)), \sigma\right)))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality.IsTester` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Michal Sedlák; Daniel Reitzner; Giulio Chiribella; Mário Ziman (2016). *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.93.052323). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.00976v2>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A tester is a finite family t of positive semidefinite effects on the output-input tensor product. Its sum is the output identity tensored with a density matrix σ on the input. Here IsDensity means positive semidefinite with complex trace equal to one. This is the tester definition in ti_pra_07.tex, lines 247–259.
+

+
+*Commentary.*
+
+First, tensoring each effect of a POVM with ρ gives a tester: Kronecker products preserve positive semidefiniteness, and the effects sum to I ⊗ ρ. Conversely, take the partial trace over x of each tester effect. This preserves positive semidefiniteness and finite sums. A tester normalized by any density matrix σ is sent to a POVM because the partial trace of I ⊗ σ is (tr σ)I = I.
+
+For a fixed lam, suppose u, v and g are noise and joint POVMs for m and n. Tensor all three families with ρ. Distributing the Kronecker product over the marginal sums, addition and real scalar multiplication gives noise and joint testers for m ⊗ ρ and n ⊗ ρ. In the reverse direction, start with arbitrary noise testers e and f and a joint tester c. Apply the partial trace over x to all three families and their marginal equations. They become POVMs, and tr ρ = 1 sends m(a) ⊗ ρ to m(a) and n(b) ⊗ ρ to n(b). Thus compatibility at lam is equivalent for the product testers and the output POVMs, even when e, f and c have different normalization states.
+
+Next tensor noise and joint POVMs with the identity on Fin r. Positivity, unit normalization and the marginal equations are preserved. For the reverse direction assume 0 < r and compress every effect to the principal submatrix indexed by pairs (b,0). Principal submatrices preserve positivity. The inclusion b ↦ (b,0) is injective, so compression preserves the identity, and it commutes with finite sums, addition and real scalar multiplication. The compressed entries of t ⊗ I are exactly the entries of t. Consequently compression turns noise and joint POVMs on y × Fin r into noise and joint POVMs on y with the required marginals.
+
+The trace equation tr ρ = 1 implies ρ ≠ 0, hence some column has a nonzero entry. The span of the columns therefore has positive dimension, giving 0 < rank ρ. The first pair of implications identifies the feasible weights in [0,1] for the product testers with those for m and n. The tensor and compression implications identify the latter set with the feasible weights for the canonical POVMs when r = rank ρ. Composing these set equalities and taking infima proves the displayed equality. No minimizer or numerical robustness value is needed.

+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, mem_cutoff, prefixes, Finset.mem_subtype,

+    exact (ray_prefix_iff ω h p).symm

+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro p hp
+  rw [hm p, hi p]

+private theorem projection_tendsto (z : H) : Tendsto (fun h : ℕ => P h z) atTop (𝓝 z) := by
+  have hc : Tendsto cutoff atTop atTop := by
+    apply tendsto_atTop.mpr
+    intro s
+    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (s.sup (fun p : Edge => p.val.length))] with h hh
+    intro p hp
+    exact (mem_cutoff h p).mpr ((Finset.le_sup hp).trans hh)

+  simpa only [Function.comp_def, ← cutoff_expansion] using hs

+private theorem shifted_lipschitz (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) :
+    LipschitzWith 1 (fun x => χ x - χ 0) := by
+  apply LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul
+  intro x y
+  simpa only [dist_eq_norm, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using hχ.dist_le_mul x y
+
+/-- Composition on the actual probability L2 space, without requiring χ(0)=0. -/
+def contractLp (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : G) : G :=
+  constG (χ 0) + (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F
+
+private theorem contractLp_ae (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : G) :
+    contractLp χ hχ F =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => χ (F ω)) := by
+  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add (constG (χ 0)) ((shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F),
+    boundary_path_split.2.2.2.1 (χ 0),
+    (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).coeFn_compLp (by simp) F] with ω ha hc hf
+  change (constG (χ 0) + (shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).compLp (by simp) F) ω = _
+  rw [ha, Pi.add_apply, hc, hf]
+  change χ 0 + (χ (F ω) - χ 0) = _
+  ring
+
+private theorem depth_ae (c : ℝ) (z : H) (h : ℕ) :
+    constG c + J (P h z) =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => potential c z
+      (D5.S0.Computability.Coding.BiasedMassFrontier.rayPrefix ω h)) := by
+  filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_add (constG c) (J (P h z)),
+    boundary_path_split.2.2.2.1 c, cutoff_trace h z] with ω ha hc hz
+  rw [ha, Pi.add_apply, hc, hz]
+  rfl
+
+private theorem trace_compatibility (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ)
+    (c : ℝ) (z : H) :
+    contractLp χ hχ (constG c + J z) = constG (χ c) + J (contracted χ hχ c z) := by
+  have hc : Continuous (contractLp χ hχ : G → G) :=
+    continuous_const.add ((shifted_lipschitz χ hχ).continuous_compLp (by simp))
+  have hlim (d : ℝ) (w : H) :
+      Tendsto (fun h : ℕ => constG d + J (P h w)) atTop (𝓝 (constG d + J w)) :=
+    tendsto_const_nhds.add (J.continuous.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (projection_tendsto w))
+  have he (h : ℕ) : contractLp χ hχ (constG c + J (P h z)) =
+      constG (χ c) + J (P h (contracted χ hχ c z)) := by
+    apply Lp.ext
+    filter_upwards [contractLp_ae χ hχ (constG c + J (P h z)),
+      depth_ae c z h, depth_ae (χ c) (contracted χ hχ c z) h] with ω hχ hF hG
+    rw [hχ, hF, hG, contracted_prefix]
+  exact tendsto_nhds_unique ((hc.continuousAt.tendsto.comp (hlim c z)).congr he)
+    (hlim (χ c) (contracted χ hχ c z))
+
+/-- The contracted original-edge extension has an actual trace in the original
+free-root domain. Its energy is no larger than that of the least extension of F,
+and its value at every finite vertex is the contracted original potential. -/
+private theorem contracted_trace_candidate (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : D) :
+    ∃ (c : ℝ) (w : H),
+      F.val = constG c + J (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) ∧
+      w = contracted χ hχ c (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) ∧
+      constG (χ c) + J w ∈ D ∧
+      energy (constG (χ c) + J w) ≤ energy F.val ∧
+      (∀ p : Address, potential (χ c) w p =
+        χ (potential c (BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F) p)) := by
+  let z := BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift F
+  let c := BiasedBoundaryCentering.mean F.val - BiasedBoundaryCentering.mean (J z)
+  let w := contracted χ hχ c z
+  have he := free_root_least_energy F
+  have hm : constG (χ c) + J w ∈ D := ⟨χ c, w, rfl⟩
+  have hw := contracted_extension χ hχ c z
+  refine ⟨c, w, he.2.2.1, rfl, hm, ?_, hw.2.2⟩
+  have hb := (free_root_least_energy ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩).2.2.2.2.1
+    (χ c) w rfl
+  calc
+    energy (constG (χ c) + J w) =
+        ‖BiasedBoundaryFreeRootForm.lift ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩‖^2 :=
+      (free_root_least_energy ⟨constG (χ c) + J w, hm⟩).2.2.2.1
+    _ ≤ ‖w‖^2 := hb.2
+    _ ≤ ‖z‖^2 := pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _) hw.2.1 2
+    _ = energy F.val := he.2.2.2.1.symm
+
+/-- Every real one-Lipschitz map preserves the actual free-root trace domain
+and decreases its original infimum energy on the actual biased probability law. -/
+theorem actual_trace_contraction (χ : ℝ → ℝ) (hχ : LipschitzWith 1 χ) (F : D) :
+    (contractLp χ hχ F.val =ᵐ[M] (fun ω => χ (F.val ω))) ∧
+    contractLp χ hχ F.val ∈ D ∧ energy (contractLp χ hχ F.val) ≤ energy F.val := by
+  obtain ⟨c,w,hF,hw,hm,hen,_⟩ := contracted_trace_candidate χ hχ F
+  refine ⟨contractLp_ae χ hχ F.val, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [hF, trace_compatibility, ← hw]
+    exact hm
+  · rw [hF, trace_compatibility, ← hw]
+    simpa only [← hF] using hen
+
+#print axioms actual_trace_contraction
+#print axioms contracted_extension
+#print axioms contracted_trace_candidate
+end D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Geometry.BiasedBoundaryMarkovSemigroup

+/- GID: D5/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality
+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S3/Quantum/QuantumChannels/AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:external-open-problem-resolution)
+   anchors: []
+   utility: none
+   digest: Ancilla-free testers with a common state have canonical POVM robustness. -/
+
+import D5.S3.Quantum.Information.SLDSpectralEnergy
+import D5.S3.Quantum.Divergence.ConditionalHockeyStickOrthogonalReduction
+
+/-! The common-normalization ancilla-free equality of Sedlák, Reitzner, Chiribella and
+Ziman, arXiv:1511.00976v2, Section VI.C. Partial trace and compression preserve the
+feasible mixing parameters, so equality follows by taking infima. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality
+
+open scoped BigOperators ComplexOrder Kronecker
+open D5.S3.Quantum.Information.SLDSpectralEnergy (IsDensity)
+open D5.S3.Quantum.Information.PartialTraceMutualInformation
+open D5.S3.Quantum.Divergence.ConditionalHockeyStickOrthogonalReduction
+  (partialTraceRight_smul)
+
+/-- Positive tester effects sum to the output identity tensored with a density matrix. -/
+def IsTester {y x j : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j]
+    (t : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) : Prop :=
+  (∀ a, (t a).PosSemidef) ∧
+    ∃ σ : Matrix x x ℂ, IsDensity σ ∧ ∑ a, t a = Matrix.kronecker 1 σ
+
+/-- Separate noise testers make the two mixtures marginals of one joint tester. -/
+def TesterCompatibleAt {y x j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (lam : ℝ)
+    (a : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) (b : k → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ (e : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) (f : k → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ)
+    (c : j × k → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ),
+    IsTester e ∧ IsTester f ∧ IsTester c ∧
+      (∀ u, ∑ v, c (u, v) = (1 - lam) • a u + lam • e u) ∧
+      (∀ v, ∑ u, c (u, v) = (1 - lam) • b v + lam • f v)
+
+/-- Infimum of the admissible mixing parameters in the unit interval. -/
+def testerRobustness {y x j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (a : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) (b : k → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) : ℝ :=
+  sInf {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ TesterCompatibleAt lam a b}
+
+/-- Separate noise POVMs make the two mixtures marginals of one joint POVM. -/
+def POVMCompatibleAt {z j k : Type} [Fintype z] [DecidableEq z]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (lam : ℝ)
+    (p : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (q : k → Matrix z z ℂ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ (u : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (v : k → Matrix z z ℂ)
+    (g : j × k → Matrix z z ℂ),
+    ((∀ a, (u a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, u a = 1) ∧
+    ((∀ b, (v b).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ b, v b = 1) ∧
+    ((∀ ab, (g ab).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ ab, g ab = 1) ∧
+      (∀ a, ∑ b, g (a, b) = (1 - lam) • p a + lam • u a) ∧
+      (∀ b, ∑ a, g (a, b) = (1 - lam) • q b + lam • v b)
+
+/-- Infimum of the POVM mixing parameters in the unit interval. -/
+def povmRobustness {z j k : Type} [Fintype z] [DecidableEq z]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (p : j → Matrix z z ℂ) (q : k → Matrix z z ℂ) : ℝ :=
+  sInf {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam p q}
+
+/-- The canonical POVMs act on the output and the support of the common input state. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (y x j k : Type) [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [DecidableEq x]
+    [Fintype j] [DecidableEq j] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ),
+    IsDensity ρ → ((∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) →
+    ((∀ b, (n b).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ b, n b = 1) →
+      testerRobustness (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+        (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ) =
+      povmRobustness (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a)
+        (1 : Matrix (Fin ρ.rank) (Fin ρ.rank) ℂ))
+        (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin ρ.rank) (Fin ρ.rank) ℂ))
+
+private theorem kronecker_sum {y x j : Type} [Fintype j]
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) :
+    (∑ a, Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) = Matrix.kronecker (∑ a, m a) ρ := by
+  exact (map_sum ((Matrix.kroneckerBilinear (R := ℂ)).flip ρ) m Finset.univ).symm
+
+private theorem povm_tensor_tester {y x j : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    IsTester (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => (hm.1 a).kronecker hρ.1, ρ, hρ, ?_⟩
+  rw [kronecker_sum, hm.2]
+
+private theorem partialTraceRight_sum {y x j : Type} [Fintype x] [Fintype j]
+    (t : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ) :
+    partialTraceRight (∑ a, t a) = ∑ a, partialTraceRight (t a) := by
+  ext a b
+  rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
+  change (∑ c, (∑ u, t u) (a, c) (b, c)) = ∑ u, ∑ c, t u (a, c) (b, c)
+  simp only [Matrix.sum_apply]
+  exact Finset.sum_comm
+
+private theorem tester_partialTrace_povm {y x j : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype x] [Fintype j] (t : j → Matrix (y × x) (y × x) ℂ)
+    (ht : IsTester t) : (∀ a, (partialTraceRight (t a)).PosSemidef) ∧
+      ∑ a, partialTraceRight (t a) = 1 := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => partialTraceRight_posSemidef (ht.1 a), ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨σ, hσ, hs⟩ := ht.2
+  rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hs, partialTraceRight_kronecker, hσ.2, one_smul]
+
+private theorem povm_to_tester_compatible {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n) :
+    TesterCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ) := by
+  obtain ⟨u, v, g, hu, hv, hg, hgm, hgn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => Matrix.kronecker (u a) ρ,
+    fun b => Matrix.kronecker (v b) ρ,
+    fun ab => Matrix.kronecker (g ab) ρ,
+    povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ u hu, povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ v hv,
+    povm_tensor_tester ρ hρ g hg, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgm a]
+    change ((1 - lam) • m a + lam • u a) ⊗ₖ ρ =
+      (1 - lam) • (m a ⊗ₖ ρ) + lam • (u a ⊗ₖ ρ)
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+  · intro b
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgn b]
+    change ((1 - lam) • n b + lam • v b) ⊗ₖ ρ =
+      (1 - lam) • (n b ⊗ₖ ρ) + lam • (v b ⊗ₖ ρ)
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+
+private theorem tester_to_povm_compatible {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : TesterCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ)
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ)) : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n := by
+  obtain ⟨e, f, c, he, hf, hc, hcm, hcn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => partialTraceRight (e a), fun b => partialTraceRight (f b),
+    fun ab => partialTraceRight (c ab), tester_partialTrace_povm e he,
+    tester_partialTrace_povm f hf, tester_partialTrace_povm c hc, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hcm a, partialTraceRight_add,
+      partialTraceRight_smul, partialTraceRight_smul,
+      partialTraceRight_kronecker, hρ.2, one_smul]
+  · intro b
+    rw [← partialTraceRight_sum, hcn b, partialTraceRight_add,
+      partialTraceRight_smul, partialTraceRight_smul,
+      partialTraceRight_kronecker, hρ.2, one_smul]
+
+private theorem povm_tensor_identity {y j : Type} [Finite y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] (r : ℕ) (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    (∀ a, (Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)).PosSemidef) ∧
+      ∑ a, Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) = 1 := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => (hm.1 a).kronecker (Matrix.PosSemidef.one), ?_⟩
+  rw [kronecker_sum, hm.2]
+  exact Matrix.one_kronecker_one
+
+private theorem povm_to_ancilla_compatible {y j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (r : ℕ) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : POVMCompatibleAt lam m n) :
+    POVMCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a)
+      (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)) := by
+  obtain ⟨u, v, g, hu, hv, hg, hgm, hgn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => Matrix.kronecker (u a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    fun b => Matrix.kronecker (v b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    fun ab => Matrix.kronecker (g ab) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ),
+    povm_tensor_identity r u hu, povm_tensor_identity r v hv,
+    povm_tensor_identity r g hg, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgm a]
+    change ((1 - lam) • m a + lam • u a) ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) =
+      (1 - lam) • (m a ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)) +
+        lam • (u a ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+  · intro b
+    rw [kronecker_sum, hgn b]
+    change ((1 - lam) • n b + lam • v b) ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) =
+      (1 - lam) • (n b ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)) +
+        lam • (v b ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+    rw [Matrix.add_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker, Matrix.smul_kronecker]
+
+private theorem compression_povm {y j : Type} [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r)
+    (m : j → Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ) (hm : (∀ a, (m a).PosSemidef) ∧ ∑ a, m a = 1) :
+    (∀ a, ((m a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))).PosSemidef) ∧
+    ∑ a, (m a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)) (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)) = 1 := by
+  refine ⟨fun a => (hm.1 a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)), ?_⟩
+  have hs := congrArg (fun z : Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ =>
+    z.submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)) (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))) hm.2
+  have hi : Function.Injective (fun b : y => (b, (⟨0, hr⟩ : Fin r))) :=
+    fun _ _ h => congrArg Prod.fst h
+  rw [Matrix.submatrix_one _ hi] at hs
+  calc
+    _ = (∑ a, m a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+        (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)) := by
+      ext a b
+      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply]
+    _ = 1 := hs
+
+private theorem ancilla_to_povm_compatible {y j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (lam : ℝ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ)
+    (h : POVMCompatibleAt lam (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a)
+      (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))) :
+    POVMCompatibleAt lam m n := by
+  have hk (t : Matrix y y ℂ) (b d : y) :
+      Matrix.kronecker t (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ)
+        (b, ⟨0, hr⟩) (d, ⟨0, hr⟩) = t b d := by
+    change t b d * (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) ⟨0, hr⟩ ⟨0, hr⟩ = t b d
+    rw [Matrix.one_apply_eq, mul_one]
+  obtain ⟨u, v, g, hu, hv, hg, hgm, hgn⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨fun a => (u a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)),
+    fun a => (v a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)),
+    fun a => (g a).submatrix (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩))
+      (fun b => (b, ⟨0, hr⟩)),
+    compression_povm r hr u hu, compression_povm r hr v hv,
+    compression_povm r hr g hg, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro a
+    ext b d
+    have he := congrArg (fun z : Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ =>
+      z (b, ⟨0, hr⟩) (d, ⟨0, hr⟩)) (hgm a)
+    simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
+      Matrix.smul_apply, hk] using he
+  · intro a
+    ext b d
+    have he := congrArg (fun z : Matrix (y × Fin r) (y × Fin r) ℂ =>
+      z (b, ⟨0, hr⟩) (d, ⟨0, hr⟩)) (hgn a)
+    simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.add_apply,
+      Matrix.smul_apply, hk] using he
+
+theorem rank_pos_of_trace_one {a : Type*} [Fintype a] [DecidableEq a]
+    {A : Matrix a a ℂ} (htr : A.trace = 1) : 0 < A.rank := by
+  by_contra hn
+  have hz : A.rank = 0 := Nat.eq_zero_of_not_pos hn
+  have hrange : LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin = ⊥ := by
+    exact Submodule.finrank_eq_zero.mp hz
+  have hlin : A.mulVecLin = 0 := LinearMap.range_eq_bot.mp hrange
+  have hA : A = 0 := by
+    apply Matrix.toLin'.injective
+    simpa only [Matrix.toLin'_apply', Matrix.mulVecLin_zero] using hlin
+  simp [hA] at htr
+
+private theorem tester_feasible_eq {y x j k : Type}
+    [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y] [Fintype x] [Fintype j] [Fintype k]
+    (ρ : Matrix x x ℂ) (hρ : IsDensity ρ)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ) :
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ TesterCompatibleAt lam
+      (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) ρ) (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) ρ)} =
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam m n} := by
+  ext lam
+  exact and_congr_right fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨tester_to_povm_compatible ρ hρ lam m n, povm_to_tester_compatible ρ hρ lam m n⟩
+
+private theorem ancilla_feasible_eq {y j k : Type} [Fintype y] [DecidableEq y]
+    [Fintype j] [Fintype k] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r)
+    (m : j → Matrix y y ℂ) (n : k → Matrix y y ℂ) :
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam m n} =
+    {lam : ℝ | 0 ≤ lam ∧ lam ≤ 1 ∧ POVMCompatibleAt lam
+      (fun a => Matrix.kronecker (m a) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))
+      (fun b => Matrix.kronecker (n b) (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ))} := by
+  ext lam
+  exact and_congr_right fun _ => and_congr_right fun _ =>
+    ⟨povm_to_ancilla_compatible r lam m n, ancilla_to_povm_compatible r hr lam m n⟩
+
+/-- Tester and canonical measurement robustness agree for a common ancilla-free state. -/
+theorem result : claim := by
+  intro y x j k _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ρ m n hρ _hm _hn
+  change sInf _ = sInf _
+  exact congrArg sInf ((tester_feasible_eq ρ hρ m n).trans
+    (ancilla_feasible_eq ρ.rank (rank_pos_of_trace_one hρ.2) m n))
+
+end D5.S3.Quantum.QuantumChannels.AncillaFreeTesterRobustnessEquality

+# Sedlák, Reitzner, Chiribella and Ziman, Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks
+
+M. Sedlák, D. Reitzner, G. Chiribella and M. Ziman, Phys. Rev. A 93, 052323 (2016); arXiv:1511.00976v2. Quotations are from the v2 TeX source, with the source's macros `\Rt`, `\Rm` and `\st` kept as written.
+
+A tester is a family $\{T_j\}$ of operators on $\mathcal H_1\otimes\mathcal H_0$ with $T_j\ge0$ and $\sum_jT_j=I_1\otimes\rho$ for a density operator $\rho$, the normalization state. Its canonical POVM is $P_j=(I\otimes\rho^{-1/2})T_j(I\otimes\rho^{-1/2})$ on $\mathcal H_1\otimes\operatorname{supp}\rho$. A tester is ancilla-free exactly when $T_j=P_j\otimes\rho$ for a POVM $\{P_j\}$ (Proposition 3). Two testers are $\lambda$-compatible if mixing each with its own noise tester at weight $\lambda$ makes them marginals of a joint tester, and $R_{\rm t}$ is the minimum such $\lambda$; $R_{\rm m}$ is the same notion for POVMs. Proposition 15 gives $R_{\rm t}(\mathsf A,\mathsf B)\le R_{\rm m}(\mathsf P,\mathsf Q)$ for a common normalization state, and Proposition 16 gives equality for a pure one. Section VI.C continues:
+
+> It is an open question whether the equality $\Rt({\st A}, {\st B}) = \Rm( \st P, \st Q )$ holds for all ancilla-free testers.

+# Ancilla-free testers with a common normalization state have canonical POVM robustness
+
+## Problem
+
+M. Sedlák, D. Reitzner, G. Chiribella and M. Ziman, *Incompatible measurements on quantum causal networks*, Phys. Rev. A 93, 052323 (2016), arXiv:1511.00976v2, Section VI.C, ask (verbatim from `ti_pra_07.tex`, line 807, retaining the source's TeX macros):
+
+> It is an open question whether  the equality $\Rt({\st A},  {\st B})  =  \Rm(  \st P,  \st Q )$ holds for all ancilla-free testers.
+
+Here $R_{\rm t}$ and $R_{\rm m}$ denote tester and measurement robustness. Section VI restricts attention to testers with the same normalization state (`ti_pra_07.tex`, lines 758 and 772); that hypothesis is retained. Proposition 3 characterizes ancilla-free testers as $T_a=M_a\otimes\rho$ for an output POVM $M$ and an input density matrix $\rho$ (lines 333–338). Definitions and locators are in [the literature note](../Library/Observer/sedlakreitznerchiribellaziman2016testers.md).
+
+Issue [#23653](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23653) fixes the following finite-dimensional reading. Let $y,x,j,k$ be finite types with decidable equality, indexing output coordinates, input coordinates and the two outcome sets. Let $\rho$ be a complex matrix on $x$ with $\rho\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Let $M=(M_a)_{a\in j}$ and $N=(N_b)_{b\in k}$ be complex output POVMs: each effect is positive semidefinite and each family sums to $I_y$. With $r=\operatorname{rank}\rho$, the statement is
+
+$$
+R_{\rm t}\bigl((M_a\otimes\rho)_a,(N_b\otimes\rho)_b\bigr)
+=R_{\rm m}\bigl((M_a\otimes I_r)_a,(N_b\otimes I_r)_b\bigr).
+$$
+
+In the module, `IsTester` means positive semidefinite effects summing to $I_y\otimes\sigma$ for some positive semidefinite $\sigma$ of trace one. `TesterCompatibleAt` at a real $\lambda$ requires noise testers $E,F$ and a joint tester $C$ with
+
+$$
+\sum_b C_{ab}=(1-\lambda)A_a+\lambda E_a,
+\qquad
+\sum_a C_{ab}=(1-\lambda)B_b+\lambda F_b.
+$$
+
+The noises have separate existential witnesses; their normalization states are not prescribed to equal $\rho$, and their effects need not be products. `POVMCompatibleAt` uses the same marginal equations with noise POVMs and a joint POVM, each positive semidefinite and summing to the identity. `testerRobustness` and `povmRobustness` are the real infima of their respective feasible $\lambda\in[0,1]$. The source uses minima; attainment is not part of `claim` or `result`. The displayed equality, with these infimum definitions and $I_r$ indexed by `Fin ρ.rank`, is proved.
+
+## Motivation
+
+For a common normalization state, the question isolates incompatibility arising from the measurements. Proposition 15 gives an upper bound by canonical POVM robustness, and Proposition 16 gives equality for a common pure normalization state (`ti_pra_07.tex`, lines 776–805). The question asks whether mixed normalization states also give equality throughout the ancilla-free class. Its resolution determines whether allowing arbitrary tester noise can reduce the required mixing parameter below that of the associated output measurements.
+

+## Route
+
+All matrix families below have finite coordinate and outcome types; the output type has decidable equality. The main statement additionally supplies decidable equality on all four types. The compatibility predicates themselves allow every real $\lambda$.
+
+1. **Tensoring POVM witnesses.** For a density matrix $\rho$, arbitrary output matrix families $M,N$ and any real $\lambda$, `povm_to_tester_compatible` takes a witness of `POVMCompatibleAt λ M N` to a witness of tester compatibility for $M\otimes\rho,N\otimes\rho$. Its helper `povm_tensor_tester` requires that $\rho$ is a density matrix and that the family being tensored is a POVM. Positivity of Kronecker products and the identity sum give the required testers.
+2. **Retracting arbitrary tester witnesses.** For a density matrix $\rho$, arbitrary output matrix families $M,N$ and any real $\lambda$, `tester_to_povm_compatible` takes tester compatibility of $M\otimes\rho,N\otimes\rho$ to `POVMCompatibleAt λ M N`. It traces out $x$ in both noises and the joint tester. For any family satisfying `IsTester`, `tester_partialTrace_povm` gives a POVM, since its normalization state $\sigma$ has trace one. The marginal equations reduce to the output equations because $\operatorname{Tr}_{x}(X\otimes\rho)=X$. No product form or prescribed normalization is assumed for the witness testers.
+3. **Removing the canonical identity factor.** For any natural $r$, arbitrary output families $M,N$ and any real $\lambda$, `povm_to_ancilla_compatible` tensors a POVM compatibility witness with $I_r$. Conversely, `ancilla_to_povm_compatible` requires $0<r$ and a compatibility witness for $M\otimes I_r,N\otimes I_r$; it compresses each witness effect to coordinates $(b,0)$. Its helper `compression_povm` requires $0<r$, decidable equality on $y$, a finite outcome type and a POVM on $y\times\mathrm{Fin}\,r$. Positivity and the identity sum survive compression. The public theorem `rank_pos_of_trace_one` supplies $0<\operatorname{rank}\rho$ for every finite-input matrix of trace one; the module `D5/S3/Quantum/Information/LiTheilHarrowChuangPurifyCloneRefutation` applies the same theorem.
+4. **Equal feasible sets.** `tester_feasible_eq` requires a density matrix $\rho$ and arbitrary output families $M,N$; `ancilla_feasible_eq` requires $0<r$ and arbitrary output families $M,N$. Together they identify the three sets of feasible weights in $[0,1]$. `result : claim` applies these equalities with $r=\operatorname{rank}\rho$ and takes `sInf` of equal sets. This uses no claim about minimizers or numerical bounds on the infima.
+

+E(G)=\Phi(G)-m
+=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}g\!\left(\frac{\min(d_u,d_v)}{\max(d_u,d_v)}\right).
+$$
+
+Each unordered edge is counted once. This is the complementary diminished Sombor index with the normalization of A. M. Albalahi, S. Das, A. Ali, J. Barman and A. E. Hamza, *On the hyperbolic Sombor index and its counterpart*, Discrete Math. Lett. 16 (2025), 108–115, DOI [10.47443/dml.2025.176](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2025.176), §1, p.109. Their Conjecture 4.1 is a historical motivation, not an open premise here: its CDSO universal-vertex assertion is refuted by the unicyclic comparison in A. Ali, K. C. Das and A. A. Attiya, *Bond incident degree indices of fixed-order unicyclic graphs*, DOI [10.47443/dml.2025.192](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2025.192), Remark 2.3, and for every positive cyclomatic number by A. M. Albalahi, *On Two Conjectures Concerning the Hyperbolic Sombor Index and Its Counterpart*, DOI [10.47443/dml.2026.217](https://doi.org/10.47443/dml.2026.217), Proposition 2.1. The latter paper's Theorem 2.2 concerns maxima.
+
+When adjacent degrees differ, orient each edge toward its endpoint of larger degree. A sink has no outgoing edge, a source has no incoming edge, and a two-layer graph has every edge joining a source to a sink. We use these notions and the fixed-cost reduction of [*CDSO sink incidences and density limits*, Definitions 1.1–1.2 and Theorem 3.1](CDSO_SINK_INCIDENCE_AND_DENSITY_LIMITS.md). In a two-layer graph, label the actual sinks by $[s]$, put $N_s=n-s$, and let $a_T$ count sources with neighborhood exactly $T$. Its actual profile is $x_T=a_T/N_s$. Then
+
+$$
+\sum_Ta_T=N_s,\qquad \sum_T|T|a_T=m,\qquad
+\sum_T(|T|-1)a_T=\ell+s-1,
+$$
+
+$$
+D_i=\sum_{T\ni i}a_T=N_sy_i,\qquad q_s=\frac m{N_s}.
+$$
+
+These identities use the vertices and degrees of one graph.
+
+## 2. An incidence certificate for arbitrary finite hub number
+
+**Theorem 2.1 (Integer support with incidence remainders).** For every integer $r\ge5$, every finite $s\ge1$, every profile of Definition 1.1, and every $2\le\beta\le\kappa_r$, one has
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)=f_r(q)+\beta(s-q)+R_{\mathrm{inc}}+R_{\mathrm{sc}}
+\ge f_r(q)+\beta(s-q),
+$$
+
+where
+
+$$
+R_{\mathrm{inc}}
+=\mathbb E\left[K\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in T}}
+ (y_i^{-1}-y_j^{-1})^2\right]\ge0,
+$$
+
+$$
+R_{\mathrm{sc}}
+=\mathbb E\left[KU_T^2-(D-\beta)K-\beta U_T+C\right]\ge0.
+$$
+
+There is no restriction $q\in[r-1,r]$ in this theorem.
+
+**Proof.** The incidence identity
+
+$$
+\mathbb E U_T=\sum_{i=1}^s\frac{\mathbb P(i\in T)}{y_i}=s
+$$
+
+uses precisely the marginals of $x$. For a fixed nonempty $T$ of cardinality $k$, the elementary identity
+
+$$
+k\sum_{i\in T}z_i^2-\left(\sum_{i\in T}z_i\right)^2
+=\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in T}}(z_i-z_j)^2
+$$
+
+with $z_i=y_i^{-1}$ gives
+
+$$
+K^2\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}=KU_T^2+
+K\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in T}}(y_i^{-1}-y_j^{-1})^2.
+$$
+
+It remains to prove the pointwise support inequality
+
+$$
+ku^2\ge(D-\beta)k+\beta u-C
+\quad\text{for every integer }k\ge1\text{ and every real }u\ge k.\tag{2.1}
+$$
+
+First, $\kappa_r\le2a^2$. Indeed $2a\le a^2-1$ for $a\ge4$, so
+
+$$
+\sqrt{2a(a^2-1)}\le a^2-1,
+\qquad 2+\sqrt{8a(a^2-1)}\le2a^2.
+$$
+
+Consequently $D-\beta\ge a^2+3a+1>0$. Let $h=\sqrt{\beta/2}$; then $1\le h\le a$.
+
+If the integer $k\ge h$, the derivative with respect to $u$ of the difference in (2.1) is $2ku-\beta\ge2k^2-\beta\ge0$. Its minimum on $u\ge k$ occurs at $u=k$ and equals
+
+$$
+k^3-Dk+C=(k-a)(k-a-1)(k+2a+1)\ge0.
+$$
+
+For an integer $k$, the first two factors are both nonpositive when $k\le a$, and both nonnegative when $k\ge a+1$; there is no integer strictly between $a$ and $a+1$.
+
+If instead $1\le k\le h$, the unconstrained minimizer $u=\beta/(2k)$ is feasible. Its value, multiplied by $4k>0$, is
+
+$$
+Q(k)=4Ck-4(D-\beta)k^2-\beta^2.
+$$
+
+This is a concave quadratic on the real interval $[1,h]$. Its endpoint values satisfy
+
+$$
+Q(1)=8a(a^2-1)-(\beta-2)^2\ge0,
+$$
+
+$$
+Q(h)=4h\bigl(h^3-Dh+C\bigr)
+=4h(h-a)(h-a-1)(h+2a+1)\ge0.
+$$
+
+The latter sign follows from $h\le a$. Concavity bounds $Q$ below by its endpoint chord, hence $Q(k)\ge0$ throughout $[1,h]$. If $h=1$ the interval is a singleton and the same endpoint computation applies. These two cases exhaust all positive integers $k$, including their common boundary. This proves (2.1).
+
+Apply (2.1) to each actual pair $(K,U_T)$, integrate, and use $\mathbb E K=q$, $\mathbb E U_T=s$. Combining with the incidence identity gives the stated exact decomposition. Types of mass zero contribute zero, with no division by $x_T$. ∎
+
+**Theorem 2.2 (Shared-budget certificate on the nine-hub interval).** Let $s$ be finite and let $x$ be one profile of Definition 1.1. For each positive integer $k$ put
+
+$$
+m_k=\mathbb E\min(k,K).
+$$
+
+For every nonempty fixed $T\subseteq[s]$, writing $k=|T|$ and $b_T=\sum_{i\in T}y_i$, one has
+
+$$
+0<b_T\le m_k\le\min(k,q),\qquad
+U_T\ge\frac{k^2}{b_T}\ge\frac{k^2}{m_k}
+\ge\max\{k,k^2/q\}.\tag{2.2}
+$$
+
+In particular the following necessary overlap bound holds for this actual array:
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge\mathbb E\frac{K^5}{m_K^2}.\tag{2.3}
+$$
+
+If $8\le q\le9$, then
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge105q+84s-1000,\tag{2.4}
+$$
+
+with equality if and only if $s=8$, $q=8$ and $x_{[8]}=1$.
+
+**Proof.** Take an independent copy $T'$ drawn from this same array. For a fixed $T$,
+
+$$
+b_T=\sum_{i\in T}\mathbb P(i\in T')=\mathbb E|T\cap T'|
+\le\mathbb E\min(k,|T'|)=m_k\le\min(k,q).
+$$
+
+The inequalities $b_T>0$ and $m_k>0$ follow from the positive marginals and nonempty types. Cauchy–Schwarz applied within this one $T$ gives
+
+$$
+k^2=\left(\sum_{i\in T}\sqrt{y_i}\,y_i^{-1/2}\right)^2
+\le b_TU_T.
+$$
+
+This proves (2.2). A second application gives
+
+$$
+U_T^2\le k\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2},\qquad
+k^2\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}\ge kU_T^2\ge\frac{k^5}{m_k^2}.
+$$
+
+Taking expectation proves (2.3) and also
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge\mathbb E(KU_T^2).
+$$
+
+The bound $U_T\ge k^2/q$ retains the shared marginal budget $\sum_i y_i=q$ for every realized type; the two moment identities alone do not impose it. All copies, marginals and expectations above come from $x$.
+
+To prove (2.4), the needed integer-support certificate is
+
+$$
+G_q(k,u):=ku^2-230k-84u+125q+1000\ge0
+\quad\left(\begin{array}{l}8\le q\le9,\ k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1},\\
+u\ge\max\{k,k^2/q\}\end{array}\right).\tag{2.5}
+$$
+
+Its equality class is exactly $q=8$, $k=8$, $u=8$. Here is a proof covering every positive integer $k$. Write $t=q-8\in[0,1]$.
+
+For $1\le k\le6$, complete the square:
+
+$$
+G_q(k,u)=k(u-42/k)^2+2000-230k-1764/k+125t.
+$$
+
+The constants after the square, before $125t$, for $k=1,\ldots,6$ are respectively
+
+$$
+6,\quad658,\quad722,\quad639,\quad2486/5,\quad326.
+$$
+
+They are all strictly positive, even without a restriction on $u$.
+
+For $k=7,8$, use $u\ge k$ and
+
+$$
+G_q(k,u)-G_q(k,k)=(u-k)\bigl[k(u+k)-84\bigr]\ge0.
+$$
+
+The bracket is positive because $2k^2-84>0$. The two endpoint values are
+
+$$
+G_q(7,7)=145+125t,\qquad G_q(8,8)=125t.
+$$
+
+Thus equality in these two cases requires exactly $t=0$, $k=8$, $u=8$.
+
+For $k=9$, put $v=81/q\ge9$. Since $u\ge v$,
+
+$$
+G_q(9,u)-G_q(9,v)=(u-v)\bigl[9(u+v)-84\bigr]\ge0.
+$$
+
+The bracket is positive. Direct expansion gives
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+q^2G_q(9,v)
+&=125q^3-1070q^2-6804q+59049\\
+&=137+76t+1930t^2+125t^3>0.
+\end{aligned}\tag{2.6}
+$$
+
+For every integer $k\ge10$, set $v=k^2/q$. Again $u\ge v$ and
+
+$$
+G_q(k,u)-G_q(k,v)=(u-v)\bigl[k(u+v)-84\bigr]\ge0,
+$$
+
+since the bracket is at least $2k^3/q-84\ge2000/9-84>0$. Put $z=1/q\ge1/9$. Then
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+&k^5z^2-84k^2z-\bigl[k^5/81-(28/3)k^2\bigr]\\
+&\hspace{1em}=(z-1/9)k^2\bigl[k^3(z+1/9)-84\bigr]\ge0,
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+because the last bracket is at least $2000/9-84>0$. Also $125q+1000\ge2000$. Therefore
+
+$$
+G_q(k,u)\ge\frac{k^5-756k^2-18630k+162000}{81}.
+$$
+
+Writing $v_0=k-10\ge0$, the numerator equals
+
+$$
+100+16250v_0+9244v_0^2+1000v_0^3+50v_0^4+v_0^5>0.\tag{2.7}
+$$
+
+This proves (2.5) and its full equality classification, without an upper bound on $k$.
+
+Apply (2.5) to the actual pairs $(K,U_T)$ using (2.2). Since $\mathbb E K=q$ and $\mathbb E U_T=s$,
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge\mathbb E(KU_T^2)
+\ge230q+84s-125q-1000=105q+84s-1000.
+$$
+
+If the final bound is an equality, the two nonnegative gaps in this chain have expectation zero. In particular $G_q(K,U_T)=0$ for every positive-mass type. The equality classification forces $q=8$ and $K=U_T=8$ on every such type. Since every $y_i\le1$, the eight summands $y_i^{-1}$ in any such type must all equal one. These eight marginals use the entire budget $\sum_i y_i=8$. The strict positivity of every marginal excludes any further hub. Thus $s=8$ and the only possible type is $[8]$. Conversely the profile $x_{[8]}=1$ gives $2J_8=512=105\cdot8+84\cdot8-1000$.
+
+In particular (2.4) is strict for every $s\ge10$. The coefficient $84$ belongs to the new constrained certificate (2.5), whose domain includes $u\ge k^2/q$. It is not a choice of $\beta$ in (2.1), which has the different domain $u\ge k$ and requires $\beta\le\kappa_r$. No sufficiency of (2.2)–(2.3) for joint realizability is asserted. Zero type masses and positive marginals with no uniform lower bound are allowed throughout. Indeed $K\ge1$ implies $w_i\ge y_i$, hence
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge\sum_i y_i^{-1}.
+$$
+
+For fixed finite $s$, an individual marginal tending to zero therefore forces the energy to infinity. Neither a limiting zero type mass nor a rare type alters the pointwise inequalities used above. ∎

+**Theorem 2.3 (Strict nine-hub comparison and quantitative compensation).** Let $s\ge10$ be finite and $8\le q\le9$. For every actual profile of mean $q$, with $t=q-8\in[0,1]$,

+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+2J_s(x)-2F_9(q)
+&>\frac{2048+23t+2360t^2+105t^3}{q^2}+84(s-10)\\
+&\ge\frac{2048}{81}+84(s-10)>0.
+\end{aligned}\tag{2.8}
+$$

+At $q=8$ this gives $2J_s(x)>680+84(s-10)$. In particular no actual profile on $[10]$ has $2J_{10}=648$ at that mean. For $s=10$, $q=8$, and the remainders of Theorem 2.1 with $r=9$, $\beta=\kappa_9=2+8\sqrt{63}$,

+$$
+R_{\mathrm{inc}}+R_{\mathrm{sc}}
+>164-16\sqrt{63}=32+(132-16\sqrt{63}).\tag{2.9}
+$$

+**Proof.** Here $2F_9(q)=81(217q-1224)/q^2$. The strict case of (2.4) gives
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)>105q-160+84(s-10).
+$$
+
+The exact difference is
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+q^2\bigl[105q-160-2F_9(q)\bigr]
+&=105q^3-160q^2-17577q+99144\\
+&=2048+23t+2360t^2+105t^3.
+\end{aligned}

+All coefficients are positive and $q^2\le81$, proving (2.8) at both endpoints and throughout the interval. At $q=8$, (2.4) gives the claimed $680+84(s-10)$ bound directly. For the remainder assertion, the incidence identity in Theorem 2.1 gives exactly

+$$
+\begin{aligned}

+&=2J_{10}-\bigl[(217-\kappa_9)8+10\kappa_9-1224\bigr]\\
+&=2J_{10}-516-16\sqrt{63}.
+\end{aligned}

+(c_1,\ldots,c_7)=
+(7,965,3269/3,1006,839,1891/3,2785/7).

+## 3. Fixed hub count, strict equality and stability
+
+**Theorem 3.1 (The fixed-$r$ remainder as a stability estimate).** For every integer $r\ge5$, every profile on $[r]$ with $q\in[r-1,r]$ satisfies $J_r(x)\ge F_r(q)$. Write
+
+$$
+\Delta=J_r(x)-F_r(q),\qquad
+p_{\mathrm{low}}=\sum_{|T|\le r-2}x_T.
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+\Delta\ge3(r-1)p_{\mathrm{low}}
++\frac{(r-1)^2}{2}\sum_{i=1}^r\left(y_i-\frac qr\right)^2,\tag{3.1}
+$$
+
+$$
+\|x-x^*(q)\|_1
+\le\frac{\sqrt{2r}}{r-1}\sqrt\Delta+\frac23\Delta.\tag{3.2}
+$$
+
+Equality $J_r(x)=F_r(q)$ holds exactly for $x=x^*(q)$, including $q=r-1$ and $q=r$.
+
+**Proof.** The following type identity is the intermediate structure needed for the estimates, rather than an assumption of equal marginals. For $\theta=q-a$ define
+
+$$
+R_i=w_i-a^2y_i-(2r-1)\theta.
+$$
+
+Expansion separately over types containing and avoiding $i$ gives
+
+$$
+R_i=\sum_{T\not\ni i}(2r-1)(r-|T|-1)x_T
++\sum_{T\ni i}(r-|T|)(r-|T|-1)x_T.\tag{3.3}
+$$
+
+All occurring coefficients are nonnegative: a type avoiding $i$ has $|T|\le r-1$, and the other product vanishes at $|T|=r-1,r$. For a type of cardinality $k\le r-2$, its coefficient in $\sum_iR_i$ is
+
+$$
+(r-k)(r-k-1)(2r-1+k)\ge6(r-1).
+$$
+
+To verify the last inequality for all such integers, set $z=r-k\in\{2,\ldots,r-1\}$. The expression is $z(z-1)(3r-z-1)$; its increment from $z$ to $z+1$ is $3z(2r-z-1)>0$, and its value at $z=2$ is $6(r-1)$. Since $y_i\le1$,
+
+$$
+J_r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^rh_\theta(y_i)+\frac12\sum_i\frac{R_i}{y_i^2}
+\ge\sum_i h_\theta(y_i)+3a p_{\mathrm{low}},
+$$
+
+$$
+h_\theta(y)=\frac{a^2}{2y}+\frac{(2r-1)\theta}{2y^2},\qquad
+h_\theta''(y)=\frac{a^2}{y^3}+\frac{3(2r-1)\theta}{y^4}\ge a^2
+\quad(0<y\le1).
+$$
+
+The ordinary strong-convexity inequality, summed at $y=q/r$ using $\sum_i(y_i-q/r)=0$, yields
+
+$$
+\sum_i h_\theta(y_i)\ge r h_\theta(q/r)
++\frac{a^2}{2}\sum_i(y_i-q/r)^2.
+$$
+
+The first term is $F_r(q)$, as is also seen by substituting $x^*$. This proves (3.1). The convexity inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz used here are standard; their consumers are the quantitative remainder and the cross-hub and finite-graph conclusions below.
+
+For the distributional estimate, put
+
+$$
+p=p_{\mathrm{low}},\qquad
+\varepsilon=\sum_{|T|\le a-1}(a-|T|)x_T,\qquad
+l_i=\sum_{\substack{|T|\le a-1\\i\notin T}}x_T.
+$$
+
+The mean identity implies $x_{[r]}=\theta+\varepsilon$, and the marginal identity implies
+
+$$
+x_{[r]\setminus\{i\}}-\frac{r-q}{r}
+=-(y_i-q/r)-l_i.
+$$
+
+Here $0\le\varepsilon\le(a-1)p$ and $\sum_i l_i=\varepsilon+p$. Thus
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\|x-x^*(q)\|_1
+&\le\sum_i|y_i-q/r|+2\varepsilon+2p\\
+&\le\sqrt r\left(\sum_i(y_i-q/r)^2\right)^{1/2}+2ap.
+\end{aligned}\tag{3.4}
+$$
+
+Combining (3.4) with (3.1) gives (3.2). Finally $\Delta=0$ forces $p=0$ and every $y_i=q/r$. The displayed identities then give exactly $x^*(q)$. Conversely that candidate attains $F_r(q)$ by Definition 1.2. The proof did not require either $\theta$ or $1-\theta$ to be positive. ∎
+
+**Theorem 3.2 (Unrestricted profiles for $r=5,6,7,8,9,10$).** Let $r\in\{5,6,7,8,9,10\}$, $q\in[r-1,r]$, and let $x$ be any profile on any finite $[s]$ with $s\ge r$. Then
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge F_r(q),
+$$
+
+with equality exactly when $s=r$ and $x=x^*(q)$, up to relabeling. For $s\ge r+1$ the stronger bound is
+
+$$
+J_s(x)-F_r(q)\ge\frac12+\frac{\beta_r}{2}(s-r-1),\qquad
+(\beta_5,\beta_6,\beta_7,\beta_8,\beta_9,\beta_{10})=(23,32,42,53,\kappa_9,\kappa_{10}).\tag{3.5}
+$$
+
+For these same six values of $r$, every profile with $s\ge r+1$ and $q\ge r$ satisfies
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge r^3+\beta_r(s-r)+(D-\beta_r)(q-r)
+\ge r^3+\beta_r.\tag{3.6}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** For $r=5,6,7,8$, the four choices of $\beta$ lie in $[2,\kappa_r]$: the comparisons $(\beta-2)^2\le8a(a^2-1)$ are respectively
+
+$$
+441\le480,\quad900\le960,\quad1600\le1680,\quad2601\le2688.
+$$
+
+For these four values, put $t=q-a\in[0,1]$ and $L_r(q)=f_r(q)+\beta_r(r+1-q)$. The following are exact polynomial identities:
+
+$$
+\begin{array}{c|l}
+r&q^2\bigl[L_r(q)-2F_r(q)-1\bigr]\\ \hline
+5&144-45t+413t^2+38t^3\\
+6&200+79t+778t^2+59t^3\\
+7&180+425t+1319t^2+85t^3\\
+8&1140t+2072t^2+116t^3.
+\end{array}\tag{3.7}
+$$
+
+The first polynomial is at least $144-45=99$; the remaining three have nonnegative coefficients. Therefore $L_r(q)\ge2F_r(q)+1$ on the entire closed interval. Theorem 2.1 now gives
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge L_r(q)+\beta_r(s-r-1),
+$$
+
+proving (3.5) for $r=5,6,7,8$. For $r=9$, Theorem 2.3 gives the stronger strict bound (2.8). Since
+
+$$
+\kappa_9=2+8\sqrt{63}<66<84,\qquad 2048/81>1,
+$$
+
+that bound implies (3.5) with $\beta_9=\kappa_9$ for every finite $s\ge10$ and $q\in[8,9]$. For $r=10$, Theorem 2.4 gives
+
+$$
+2\bigl(J_s(x)-F_{10}(q)\bigr)>29+100(s-11)
+\quad(s\ge11,\ 9\le q\le10).
+$$
+
+Since $\kappa_{10}=2+24\sqrt{10}<78<100$ and $29>1$, this implies (3.5) with $\beta_{10}=\kappa_{10}$. Neither application restricts source cardinalities, requires positive mass for every type, or discards any hub with positive marginal. For $s=r$, Theorem 3.1 gives the inequality and the complete equality class. Thus no assumption on the cardinalities in the support is needed.
+
+For (3.6), use Theorem 2.1 outside the candidate interval as allowed there. Since $f_r(r)=r^3$,
+
+$$
+f_r(q)+\beta_r(s-q)
+=r^3+\beta_r(s-r)+(D-\beta_r)(q-r).
+$$
+
+Both $D-\beta_r>0$ and $q-r\ge0$, proving (3.6). This gives a fixed positive separation even if an actual extra-hub graph has mean cardinality above $r$. ∎

+## 4. All parameters under a cardinality hypothesis
+
+**Theorem 4.1 (All-$r$ conditional comparison and Bernstein certificate).** Let $r\ge5$, let $s\ge r$ be finite, and let $x$ be a profile supported on $K\ge r-2$. If $q\in[r-1,r]$, then $J_s(x)\ge F_r(q)$, with equality exactly when $s=r$ and $x=x^*(q)$, up to relabeling. Set
+
+$$
+d=r-2,\qquad
+\gamma_r=\frac{6r^4-39r^3+52r^2-8r-8}{6r^2}\ge\frac{127}{150}.
+$$
+
+For every $s\ge r+1$ one has
+
+$$
+J_s(x)-F_r(q)\ge\gamma_r+
+\frac{(r-2)^2}{2q}\bigl[s^2-(r+1)^2\bigr].\tag{4.1}
+$$
+
+For the same support condition, every $s\ge r+1$ and every feasible $q\ge r$ satisfy
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge\frac{r^3}{2}+\gamma_r.\tag{4.2}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** For every integer $k$,
+
+$$
+k^2\ge d^2+(2d+1)(k-d),
+\qquad k^2-d^2-(2d+1)(k-d)=(k-d)(k-d-1)\ge0.
+$$
+
+For types in the support $K-d\ge0$. Consequently
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+2J_s(x)
+&\ge d^2\mathbb E\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}
+ +(2d+1)\mathbb E\left[(K-d)\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}\right]\\
+&\ge d^2\sum_i y_i^{-1}+(2d+1)\mathbb E[K(K-d)]\\
+&\ge\frac{d^2s^2}{q}+(2d+1)\bigl(\mathbb E K^2-dq\bigr).
+\end{aligned}\tag{4.3}
+$$
+
+The second step uses $y_i^{-2}\ge1$ only with nonnegative coefficients, and the third uses $(\sum_i y_i)(\sum_i y_i^{-1})\ge s^2$.
+
+For integer $K$, $(K-r+1)(K-r)\ge0$, so
+
+$$
+\mathbb E K^2\ge(2r-1)q-r(r-1).
+$$
+
+On $[r-1,r]$, (4.3) therefore gives
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge B_{r,s}(q):=
+\frac{(r-2)^2s^2}{q}+(2r-3)\bigl[(r+1)q-r(r-1)\bigr].\tag{4.4}
+$$
+
+Here is a coefficient proof valid for every $r\ge5$, including the whole $q$ interval. Put $u=r-5\ge0$, $t=q-r+1\in[0,1]$ and
+
+$$
+P_r(q)=q^2\bigl[B_{r,r+1}(q)-2F_r(q)\bigr].
+$$
+
+After expansion it has the cubic Bernstein representation
+
+$$
+P_r(r-1+t)=\sum_{j=0}^3b_j\binom3j t^j(1-t)^{3-j},
+$$
+
+where
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+b_0&=2u^4+27u^3+128u^2+244u+144,\\
+b_1&=2u^4+27u^3+\tfrac{367}{3}u^2+\tfrac{587}{3}u+\tfrac{127}{3},\\
+b_2&=2u^4+\tfrac{85}{3}u^3+\tfrac{406}{3}u^2+231u+62,\\
+b_3&=2u^4+31u^3+169u^2+369u+245.
+\end{aligned}\tag{4.5}
+$$
+
+In particular $b_1>0$. The exact differences are
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+b_0-b_1&=\tfrac13(17u^2+145u+305),\\
+b_2-b_1&=\tfrac13(4u^3+39u^2+106u+59),\\
+b_3-b_1&=\tfrac13(12u^3+140u^2+520u+608).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+All are nonnegative. The Bernstein weights are nonnegative and sum to one, so $P_r(q)\ge b_1$. Since $q\le r$,
+
+$$
+B_{r,r+1}(q)-2F_r(q)\ge\frac{b_1}{r^2}=2\gamma_r.
+$$
+
+Replacing $r+1$ by $s$ in (4.4) adds exactly $d^2[s^2-(r+1)^2]/q$, proving (4.1). Also
+
+$$
+\gamma_r=r^2-\frac{13r}{2}+\frac{26}{3}-\frac4{3r}-\frac4{3r^2}.
+$$
+
+Its derivative as a real function on $[5,\infty)$ is $2r-13/2+4/(3r^2)+8/(3r^3)>0$, and $\gamma_5=127/150$.
+
+For $q\ge r$, use $\mathbb E K^2\ge q^2$ in (4.3) instead. The lower bound obtained by replacing $s$ with $r+1$ is
+
+$$
+G_r(q)=\frac{d^2(r+1)^2}{q}+(2r-3)(q^2-dq).
+$$
+
+It is strictly increasing for $q\ge r$: its second derivative is positive and
+
+$$
+G_r'(r)=\frac{r^4+3r^3-3r^2-4r-4}{r^2}>0.
+$$
+
+For example $r^4-3r^2-4r-4>0$ for $r\ge5$, since it is at least $22r^2-4r-4>0$. At $q=r$ one has $G_r(r)=B_{r,r+1}(r)\ge r^3+2\gamma_r$. This proves (4.2). Finally Theorem 3.1 handles $s=r$, while the positive gap excludes $s>r$, proving the equality statement. ∎
+
+**Theorem 4.2 (Weighted low-cardinality defect without the hypothesis).** For any profile, define
+
+$$
+\Delta_d(x)=\sum_{1\le|T|<d}x_T(d-|T|)
+\sum_{i\in T}(y_i^{-2}-1),\qquad d=r-2.
+$$
+
+For $q\in[r-1,r]$ and $s\ge r+1$, without any restriction on the support,
+
+$$
+J_s(x)-F_r(q)\ge\gamma_r+
+\frac{d^2[s^2-(r+1)^2]}{2q}-\frac{2r-3}{2}\Delta_d(x).\tag{4.6}
+$$
+
+Thus $J_s(x)\le F_r(q)$ requires
+
+$$
+\Delta_d(x)\ge
+\frac{2\gamma_r+d^2[s^2-(r+1)^2]/q}{2r-3};\tag{4.7}
+$$
+
+a strict counterexample requires a strict inequality in (4.7).
+
+**Proof.** Retain the integer quadratic inequality at the start of (4.3), but now keep track of its signed coefficient:
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathbb E\left[(K-d)\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}\right]
+&=\mathbb E[K(K-d)]\\
+&\quad+\sum_Tx_T(K-d)\sum_{i\in T}(y_i^{-2}-1)\\
+&\ge\mathbb E[K(K-d)]-\Delta_d(x).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+The terms with $K\ge d$ are nonnegative, while the others are exactly the negative of the displayed defect. Hence $2J_s\ge B_{r,s}(q)-(2r-3)\Delta_d(x)$. Apply (4.5). The remaining implications follow by rearranging. All the favorable terms and all the defect terms belong to the same array. This is a necessary condition on a possible counterexample, not such a counterexample. ∎
