+## 5. Capacity, integer candidates and their exact cost
+
+**Definition 5.1 (Full capacity interval and balanced construction).** For $r\ge5$, define
+
+$$
+L_r(n)=(r-2)n-r^2+2r+1,\qquad
+U_r(n)=(r-1)n-r^2+1.
+$$
+
+For integers $n\ge2r$ and $L_r(n)\le\ell\le U_r(n)$ put
+
+$$
+N=n-r,\qquad c=\ell-(r-2)n+r(r-1)-1,\qquad
+b=U_r(n)-\ell.
+$$
+
+Choose nonnegative integers $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ summing to $b$ and differing pairwise by at most one. The graph $H_r(n,\ell)$ has $r$ independent hubs, $c$ distinct sources adjacent to all hubs, and $b_i$ distinct sources adjacent to all hubs except hub $i$. All sources are independent. Put
+
+$$
+M_c(z)=z g((r-1)/z)+c\bigl[g(r/z)-g((r-1)/z)\bigr]\quad(z>0).
+$$
+
+**Theorem 5.2 (Capacity exclusion and quantitative rounding).** For $n\ge2r$, the complete integer interval in which $r$ independent hubs can accommodate the edge budget and every smaller hub number is excluded by that capacity is precisely $[L_r(n),U_r(n)]$. On this interval,
+
+$$
+b+c=N,\qquad (r-1)b+rc=m=n-1+\ell,\qquad c\ge r,\quad b\ge0.
+$$
+
+The graph $H_r(n,\ell)$ is simple and connected with exactly the prescribed $n,m,\ell$. Its hub degrees are $D_i=N-b_i$. For $n\ge3r$, these are larger than the source degrees, so they are its degree-oriented sinks. Its exact excess is
+
+$$
+E(H_r(n,\ell))=\sum_{i=1}^rM_c(N-b_i).\tag{5.1}
+$$
+
+Set
+
+$$
+q_r=\frac mN=r-1+\frac cN,\qquad
+B=r\bigl[4(r-1)^2+24(2r-1)\bigr],\qquad C_0=4r^3.
+$$
+
+The actual normalized profile $x^H$ satisfies
+
+$$
+0\le J_r(x^H)-F_r(q_r)\le\frac B{N^2},\tag{5.2}
+$$
+
+and
+
+$$
+E(H_r(n,\ell))\le\frac{F_r(q_r)}N+\frac B{N^3},\qquad
+E(H_r(n,\ell))\le\frac{C_0}{n}.\tag{5.3}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** With $t$ independent hubs and $n-t$ sources, simplicity gives $m\le t(n-t)$. For integers $t\le r-1$ and $n\ge2r$, this capacity increases with $t$. Thus the condition excluding all $t\le r-1$ is
+
+$$
+m>(r-1)(n-r+1),
+$$
+
+which, for integer $\ell$, is exactly $\ell\ge L_r(n)$. Feasibility of $r$ hubs is $m\le r(n-r)$, or $\ell\le U_r(n)$. Conversely all integer edge counts in this interval are supplied by the construction. Solving its two count equations gives the displayed $b,c$. At the lower endpoint $c=r$ and at the upper endpoint $b=0$; hence $r\le c\le N$ throughout. The full sources connect every hub, and every other source has a nonempty neighborhood. All memberships are simple edges between distinct vertices. Thus connectedness, simplicity, order and size hold together in this one graph, even if a missing-one count is zero.
+
+At hub $i$, precisely $c$ incident sources have degree $r$ and $b-b_i=D_i-c$ have degree $r-1$. Every $D_i\ge c\ge r$, so the hub is a larger-degree endpoint and (5.1) holds even when the endpoint degrees are equal. For a balanced choice, $b_i\le b/r+1$ and $b\le N-r$, so $D_i\ge(r-1)N/r$. If $n\ge3r$, this is greater than $r$. This also proves the claimed orientation.
+
+For the quantitative estimate, write $\theta=c/N$ and $y_i=1-b_i/N$. Balance gives
+
+$$
+|y_i-q_r/r|<1/N,\qquad \sum_i(y_i-q_r/r)=0,
+\qquad y_i\ge\tfrac12.
+$$
+
+Only cardinalities $r-1,r$ occur. Hence (3.3) is an equality with $R_i=0$ and $J_r(x^H)=\sum_i h_\theta(y_i)$. On the segment between $y_i$ and $q_r/r$, both arguments are at least $1/2$, and
+
+$$
+h_\theta''(y)\le8(r-1)^2+48(2r-1).
+$$
+
+Taylor's formula, summed with the zero linear term, proves the upper bound in (5.2); its lower bound is Theorem 3.1. On every actual edge $g(t)\le t^2/2$, so $E(H_r)\le J_r(x^H)/N$, proving the first part of (5.3). Finally $D_i\ge N/2$, there are $m\le rN$ edges, and each source degree is at most $r$. Therefore
+
+$$
+E(H_r)\le\frac{mr^2}{2(N/2)^2}\le\frac{2r^3}{N}\le\frac{4r^3}{n}.
+$$
+
+Here $N\ge n/2$. All the cost estimates hold for $n\ge2r$; the stronger $n\ge3r$ condition was needed only for strict degree orientation. ∎
+
+## 6. Exact finite minimizers throughout the capacity interval
+
+**Theorem 6.1 (Uniform sufficient threshold and unique finite minimum).** Fix $r\ge5$. Let the admissible class $\mathcal A_r(n,\ell)$ be either of the following:
+
+1. for $r\in\{5,6,7,8,9,10\}$, all of $\mathcal G(n,\ell)$;
+2. for any $r\ge5$, the members of $\mathcal G(n,\ell)$ whose minimum degree is at least $r-2$.
+
+Define
+
+$$
+C_0=4r^3,\quad A=2C_0+1,\quad K_0=\lceil\sqrt A\rceil,
+\quad R=\frac{(3C_0)^4K_0^5}{8},
+$$
+
+$$
+B=r\bigl[4(r-1)^2+24(2r-1)\bigr],\qquad
+H=R+8B,\qquad
+\widehat\gamma=\min\{1/2,\gamma_r\}=1/2.
+$$
+
+Take any integer $n_0(r)$ strictly greater than
+
+$$
+\max\left\{
+1,2r,C_0^2,3C_0,A^3,4AK_0^2,36C_0^2A,
+\sqrt{H/\widehat\gamma},\frac{H}{3(r-1)}
+\right\}.\tag{6.1}
+$$
+
+For every integer $n\ge n_0(r)$ and every integer
+
+$$
+L_r(n)\le\ell\le U_r(n),
+$$
+
+$H_r(n,\ell)$ is the unique minimizing isomorphism class in $\mathcal A_r(n,\ell)$. In particular the exact minimum excess is
+
+$$
+E_r^{\min}(n,\ell):=\min_{G\in\mathcal A_r(n,\ell)}E(G)
+=\sum_{i=1}^rM_c(N-b_i),\tag{6.2}
+$$
+
+with $N,c,b_i$ as in Definition 5.1; the minimum of $\Phi$ is $m$ plus (6.2). The threshold is sufficient; it is not asserted to be least. For $r\ge11$, the second class here is a material minimum-degree restriction. The unrestricted conclusion includes the full intervals $[L_9(n),U_9(n)]=[7n-62,8n-80]$ and $[L_{10}(n),U_{10}(n)]=[8n-79,9n-99]$.
+
+**Proof.** The candidate belongs to either stated class, has source degrees $r-1,r$, and its hub degrees exceed $r$ at this threshold. It has $E(H_r)\le C_0/n$ by Theorem 5.2. A graph with larger excess is already strictly worse than the candidate. It suffices to consider actual graphs $G$ with $E(G)\le C_0/n$.
+
+Apply [*CDSO sink incidences and density limits*, Theorem 3.1](CDSO_SINK_INCIDENCE_AND_DENSITY_LIMITS.md) with exactly $C=C_0$, $A=2C_0+1$, $K=K_0$. The six reduction inequalities there are included in (6.1). Thus $G$ is two-layer, its actual sink number obeys $s\le K_0$, and each sink degree satisfies
+
+$$
+D_i\ge\frac n{3C_0}.
+$$
+
+This uses the existing reduction, rather than asserting an additional reduction theorem. Capacity from Theorem 5.2 forces $s\ge r$. In the second admissible class, each source also satisfies $K\ge r-2$. Let $N_s=n-s$ and use the actual array of Definition 1.3. In particular $q_s=m/N_s\ge q_r=m/(n-r)>r-1$, but $q_s$ need not be at most $r$.
+
+The uniform error on these actual edges follows from the elementary identity, also used in [*CDSO minimizers without a universal vertex for every cyclomatic number*, §11](CDSO_UNIVERSAL_VERTEX_ALL_CYCLOMATIC.md),
+
+$$
+0\le\frac{t^2}{2}-g(t)
+=\frac{t^4}{2(\sqrt{1+t^2}+1)^2}\le\frac{t^4}{8}\quad(t\ge0).
+$$
+
+The quadratic edge sum is exactly $J_s(x)/N_s$. Counting at most $s$ incidences at each source, each source degree at most $s$, gives
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+0\le\frac{J_s(x)}{N_s}-E(G)
+&\le\frac18\sum_Ta_T|T|^4\sum_{i\in T}D_i^{-4}\\
+&\le\frac{N_ss^5}{8(\min_iD_i)^4}\le\frac R{n^3}.
+\end{aligned}\tag{6.3}
+$$
+
+The candidate bound is
+
+$$
+E(H_r)\le\frac{F_r(q_r)}{n-r}+\frac{8B}{n^3},\tag{6.4}
+$$
+
+since $n-r\ge n/2$.
+
+Suppose first that $s\ge r+1$. If $q_s\le r$, use (3.5) in the unrestricted class and (4.1) in the restricted class. In either case
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge F_r(q_s)+\widehat\gamma\ge F_r(q_r)+\widehat\gamma.
+$$
+
+For completeness, $F_r$ is strictly increasing on $[r-1,r]$, because
+
+$$
+F_r'(q)=\frac{r^2}{2q^3}(2C-Dq)>0,
+\qquad 2C-Dr=r(r^2-3r+1)>0.
+$$
+
+If $q_s\ge r$, (3.6) in the unrestricted class gives
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge r^3/2+\beta_r/2\ge F_r(q_r)+\widehat\gamma,
+$$
+
+whereas (4.2) gives the same conclusion in the restricted class. In particular, for $r=9$ and an actual $s\ge10$, (3.6) is precisely
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge729+\kappa_9(s-9)+(217-\kappa_9)(q_s-9)\qquad(q_s\ge9).
+$$
+
+Here $217-\kappa_9>0$, so the gap is at least $\kappa_9/2>1/2$, even when $q_s>9$. If instead $q_s\le9$, the same graph has $8<q_s\le9$, and (2.8) gives $J_s-F_9(q_s)>1024/81+42(s-10)>1/2$. For $r=10$, (3.6) likewise gives the unrestricted estimate
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)\ge1000+\kappa_{10}(s-10)+(271-\kappa_{10})(q_s-10)
+\qquad(s\ge11,\ q_s\ge10).
+$$
+
+Here $271-\kappa_{10}>0$, so the gap above $1000/2$ is at least $\kappa_{10}/2>1/2$. In the other case the same actual graph has $9<q_s\le10$, and (2.12) gives $J_s(x)-F_{10}(q_s)>29/2+50(s-11)>1/2$. Thus the interval certificate is used only in its domain; the unrestricted certificate supplies every value $q_s>10$. For both $r=9$ and $r=10$, these two cases cover the actual budget $q_s=m/(n-s)$ without substituting $q_r$ for it. Thus $\widehat\gamma=1/2$ is a common gap in both cases, with $C_0,A,K_0,R,B,H$ as defined in the statement. This is the upper-capacity bridge: a graph with more hubs and $q_s>r$ is still separated by a fixed positive amount. Both cases therefore imply, using $F_r(q_r)>0$, $N_s\le n-r$ and (6.3)–(6.4),
+
+$$
+E(G)-E(H_r)\ge\frac{\widehat\gamma}{n}-\frac H{n^3}>0.\tag{6.5}
+$$
+
+The last inequality is exactly the square-root condition in (6.1). Thus a minimizing or tying graph must have $s=r$ throughout the closed integer capacity interval.
+
+Let $A_{\mathrm{low}}$ count its sources of degree at most $r-2$. If $A_{\mathrm{low}}\ge1$, (3.1) gives
+
+$$
+J_r(x)\ge F_r(q_r)+\frac{3(r-1)A_{\mathrm{low}}}{N}.
+$$
+
+Hence (6.3)–(6.4) yield
+
+$$
+E(G)-E(H_r)\ge\frac{3(r-1)}{N^2}-\frac H{n^3}
+\ge\frac{3(r-1)}{n^2}-\frac H{n^3}>0,\tag{6.6}
+$$
+
+by the last condition in (6.1). Every source of a minimizer consequently has degree $r-1$ or $r$. The vertex and edge budgets now force the full count $c$ and the total missing-one count $b$ in Definition 5.1. In particular $c\ge r$, independent of how these missing-one counts are distributed.
+
+It remains to minimize the exact cost, not just its quadratic approximation. For every distribution of missing-one counts,
+
+$$
+D_i=N-b_i\ge c\ge r,\quad \sum_iD_i=m,\quad
+E(G)=\sum_iM_c(D_i).
+$$
+
+The function $M_c$ is strictly convex on $(0,\infty)$. The analytic pattern in [the preceding universal-vertex volume, Theorem 8.2](CDSO_UNIVERSAL_VERTEX_ALL_CYCLOMATIC.md), extends here with adjacent source degrees $a,r$: let $f_k(z)=g(k/z)$, so
+
+$$
+M_c(z)=\sqrt{z^2+a^2}-z+c(f_r(z)-f_a(z)),
+$$
+
+$$
+f_k''(z)=\frac{k^2(3z^2+2k^2)}{z^3(z^2+k^2)^{3/2}}.
+$$
+
+For fixed $z>0$, the derivative with respect to $v>0$ of
+
+$$
+Q_z(v)=\frac{v(3z^2+2v)}{(z^2+v)^{3/2}}
+$$
+
+is
+
+$$
+Q_z'(v)=\frac{6z^4+5z^2v+2v^2}{2(z^2+v)^{5/2}}>0.
+$$
+
+Thus $f_r''(z)>f_a''(z)$ and
+
+$$
+M_c''(z)=\frac{a^2}{(z^2+a^2)^{3/2}}+c(f_r''(z)-f_a''(z))>0.\tag{6.7}
+$$
+
+Suppose $D_j\ge D_i+2$, equivalently $b_i\ge b_j+2$. At least one actual source misses hub $i$. Delete its edge to $j$ and add its missing edge to $i$. This changes that source's neighborhood from $[r]\setminus\{i\}$ to $[r]\setminus\{j\}$, raises $D_i$ by one and lowers $D_j$ by one. The operation preserves simplicity, source degree, $n,m,\ell$ and the untouched $c$ full sources, so it preserves connectedness. Hub degrees remain at least $c$, preserving the minimum-degree restriction as well. Strict convexity gives
+
+$$
+M_c(D_i+1)+M_c(D_j-1)<M_c(D_i)+M_c(D_j),
+$$
+
+for example by integrating the strictly increasing derivative over the two unit intervals. The reverse imbalance is handled by exchanging $i,j$. Repeated legal moves terminate at degrees differing pairwise by at most one, since their integer sum is fixed and each move decreases the sum of their squares. Therefore all minimizing $b_i$ are balanced. Their multiset is unique. Permuting hubs and sources identifies all graphs with that multiset, while any unbalanced graph admits a strictly improving actual move. Combined with (6.5)–(6.6), this proves the exact value and the unique graph isomorphism class. ∎

+## 7. Exact prescribed budgets and high-density stability
+
+**Theorem 7.1 (Single-array realization at a prescribed high-density budget).** Fix $r\ge5$, finite $s\ge r$, and $\alpha\in[r-2,r-1]$. Let $x$ be one profile on $[s]$ with $q=1+\alpha$ and all $y_i>0$. Suppose integer budgets $\ell_n$ satisfy $\ell_n/n\to\alpha$ and eventually
+
+$$
+0\le\ell_n\le s(n-s)-n+1.
+$$
+
+There are simple connected graphs with exactly $n$ vertices, $n-1+\ell_n$ edges and $s$ actual degree-oriented sinks whose type proportions converge to this same $x$, and whose energies satisfy
+
+$$
+nE(G_n)\longrightarrow J_s(x).
+$$
+
+If $x$ is supported on $K\ge d$ for some fixed $1\le d\le s$, the construction can preserve source degree at least $d$ provided additionally
+
+$$
+(d-1)(n-s-1)\le\ell_n
+$$
+
+eventually. In particular this lower inequality is automatic here for $d=r-2$. No positivity of all type masses is assumed.
+
+**Proof.** Reserve $s$ hubs and one source adjacent to all of them. Put $M=n-s-1$ for the remaining sources. Round the finitely many numbers $Mx_T$ to nonnegative integer counts summing to $M$, with bounded error in each type; floors followed by distributing the bounded deficit suffice. If a support restriction is imposed, do this entirely within that support. The initial additional-membership count of these sources is
+
+$$
+B_0=\sum_T(|T|-1)a_T=M\alpha+O_s(1),
+\qquad B_0-\ell_n=o(n).
+$$
+
+The exact possible interval for their additional memberships is $[0,(s-1)M]$, and
+
+$$
+(s-1)M=s(n-s)-n+1.
+$$
+
+If $B_0<\ell_n$, some source lacks a hub membership until the upper endpoint is reached; add one such membership. If $B_0>\ell_n$, some source has at least two neighbors until the lower endpoint is reached; remove one membership while leaving that source nonempty. Stop exactly at $B=\ell_n$. These are $|B_0-\ell_n|=o(n)$ edits. With a degree bound $d$, delete only from sources of degree greater than $d$, and stop at the lower endpoint $(d-1)M$; addition is unchanged. The assumed target lies within these two exact endpoints. For $d=r-2$, $\ell_n/M\to\alpha\ge r-2>d-1$, so the lower endpoint is eventually below the target.
+
+The reserved full source is unchanged, so it connects every hub at every finite order. Other sources retain nonempty neighborhoods. All memberships are subsets of $[s]$, hence the graph is simple, and its edge count is exactly
+
+$$
+s+M+B=n-1+\ell_n.
+$$
+
+The reserved source and the $o(n)$ edits change each limiting type mass by zero, even for a type whose limiting mass is zero. Thus $a_T/(n-s)\to x_T$, and $D_i/(n-s)\to y_i>0$. For sufficiently large $n$ the hub degrees exceed $s$, whereas source degrees are at most $s$; these are consequently the actual degree-oriented sinks. Applying the actual-edge expansion from (6.3), now with fixed $s$ and positive limiting marginals, gives
+
+$$
+E(G_n)=\frac{J_s(x^{(n)})}{n-s}+O(n^{-3}).
+$$
+
+Continuity in a neighborhood of the positive limiting marginals proves the energy limit. ∎
+
+**Theorem 7.2 (Capacity-constrained density limit and necessary and sufficient near-minimum structure).** Fix either admissible class of Theorem 6.1 and a prescribed integer sequence $\ell_n$ with
+
+$$
+L_r(n)\le\ell_n\le U_r(n)\text{ eventually},\qquad
+\frac{\ell_n}{n}\longrightarrow\alpha\in[r-2,r-1].
+$$
+
+Then
+
+$$
+nE_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\longrightarrow F_r(1+\alpha).\tag{7.1}
+$$
+
+For any sequence $G_n\in\mathcal A_r(n,\ell_n)$, the following are equivalent:
+
+1. $E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)=o(1/n)$;
+2. $nE(G_n)\to F_r(1+\alpha)$;
+3. eventually $G_n$ is an actual two-layer graph with exactly $r$ degree-oriented sinks, and, for its source counts and hub degrees with $N=n-r$,
+
+$$
+\frac1N\sum_{|T|\le r-2}a_T\longrightarrow0,\qquad
+\frac{D_i}{N}-\frac{q_r}{r}\longrightarrow0\quad(1\le i\le r),
+\qquad q_r=\frac{n-1+\ell_n}{n-r};\tag{7.2}
+$$
+
+4. eventually $G_n$ has exactly those $r$ actual sinks and source–sink structure, and its single profile satisfies
+
+$$
+\|x^{(n)}-x^*(q_r)\|_1\longrightarrow0.\tag{7.3}
+$$
+
+In the unrestricted class this includes $r=9$ with every $\alpha\in[7,8]$, and $r=10$ with every $\alpha\in[8,9]$; for general $r\ge5$ the second class retains its minimum-degree hypothesis. Labels of the $r$ sinks may be chosen separately at each order; the limiting candidate is permutation invariant. In particular every hub degree divided by $n$ tends to $(1+\alpha)/r$. These conclusions allow $o(n)$ low-cardinality sources and unbounded sublinear hub imbalances. They do not assert finite disappearance of exceptional sources or a bounded difference of hub degrees.
+
+**Proof.** Theorem 6.1 gives the exact minimum at every sufficiently large order. For its balanced graph, $q_r\to1+\alpha$, $y_i=q_r/r+O(1/N)$, and the actual-edge error (6.3) together with (5.2) gives
+
+$$
+E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)=\frac{F_r(q_r)}N+O_r(n^{-3}).\tag{7.4}
+$$
+
+Since $n/N\to1$, this proves (7.1) and the equivalence of 1 and 2.
+
+Assume 1. The limit is bounded by $r^3/2$, because $F_r$ increases to $F_r(r)=r^3/2$. Thus $E(G_n)\le C_0/n$ eventually. The fixed-cost reduction of the sink-incidence volume, Theorem 3.1, applies to these actual graphs. It supplies their two-layer structure, a bounded number of sinks and the positive bound $D_i/n\ge1/(3C_0)$ for every actual sink. Capacity supplies $s\ge r$; no hub with a vanishing normalized degree has been suppressed. If $s>r$ along any infinite subsequence, (6.5) gives
+
+$$
+\liminf n\bigl(E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\bigr)\ge\widehat\gamma>0
+$$
+
+on that subsequence, contradicting 1. This exclusion uses (3.6) or (4.2) when $q_s>r$, so it remains valid at $\alpha=r-1$. Eventually $s=r$.
+
+For the actual $r$-sink array let $\Delta_n=J_r(x^{(n)})-F_r(q_r)\ge0$. Equations (6.3) and (7.4) imply
+
+$$
+\Delta_n=N\bigl(E(G_n)-E_r^{\min}(n,\ell_n)\bigr)+O_r(n^{-2})\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+
+Theorem 3.1 yields (7.2) and (7.3), including the explicit estimate (3.2). This proves 3 and 4. Conversely 3 implies 4 directly from (3.4), independently of a presumed small energy gap.
+
+Finally assume 4. Then every marginal tends to $(1+\alpha)/r>0$, so the bounded source degrees and positive linear hub degrees allow the actual-edge expansion. The functional $J_r$ is continuous there, and $x^*(q_r)\to x^*(1+\alpha)$, hence
+
+$$
+nE(G_n)=\frac nN J_r(x^{(n)})+O_r(n^{-2})\longrightarrow F_r(1+\alpha).
+$$
+
+This proves 2 and completes all equivalences.
+
+The endpoint capacity hypotheses cannot be replaced by their density limits: $\alpha$ alone does not specify the least feasible integer hub count. At $\alpha=r-2$ the candidate full mass tends to zero, but its exact count is still $c\ge r$ at every finite order, connecting the entire construction. At $\alpha=r-1$ the missing-one masses may vanish, and $b=0$ gives an actual complete bipartite graph. All proofs above allow these zero-mass limits. ∎

+## 8. An unconditional upper interval and the boundary of moment relaxation
+
+**Theorem 8.1 (An explicit unconditional upper-density interval for all $r$).** For every integer $r\ge5$, put
+
+$$
+\delta_r=\min\left\{1,\frac{\kappa_r}{2r^2-\kappa_r}\right\}.
+$$
+
+For $q=r-\delta$ with $0\le\delta\le\delta_r$, every finite $s\ge r$ and every profile of mean $q$ satisfy $J_s(x)\ge F_r(q)$, with equality exactly for $s=r$, $x=x^*(q)$. For $s\ge r+1$ the following strict bound holds throughout this closed interval:
+
+$$
+2\bigl(J_s(x)-F_r(q)\bigr)
+\ge\kappa_r-(2r^2-\kappa_r)\delta+r\delta^2
++\kappa_r(s-r-1)>0.\tag{8.1}
+$$
+
+More generally, for every $q\in[r-1,r]$ and $s\ge r+1$,
+
+$$
+2\bigl(J_s(x)-F_r(q)\bigr)
+\ge\Gamma_r(q)+\kappa_r(s-r-1),
+$$
+
+$$
+\Gamma_r(q)=\kappa_r(r+1-q)
+-\left(\frac{r^2}{q^2}-1\right)f_r(q).\tag{8.2}
+$$
+
+In particular every hub count
+
+$$
+s>q+\frac{(r^2/q^2-1)f_r(q)}{\kappa_r}
+$$
+
+is strictly excluded from equality or improvement over the candidate.
+
+**Proof.** Theorem 2.1 at $\beta=\kappa_r$ gives (8.2). The positivity $2r^2-\kappa_r>0$ follows from $\kappa_r\le2(r-1)^2<2r^2$. Monotonicity of $F_r$ on $[r-1,r]$ gives
+
+$$
+\frac{f_r(q)}{q^2}=\frac{2F_r(q)}{r^2}\le r.
+$$
+
+Therefore, when $q=r-\delta$,
+
+$$
+\left(\frac{r^2}{q^2}-1\right)f_r(q)
+\le r(r^2-q^2)=2r^2\delta-r\delta^2.
+$$
+
+Substitute this in (8.2) to obtain (8.1). At $\delta=0$ its first three terms equal $\kappa_r>0$. For $0<\delta\le\kappa_r/(2r^2-\kappa_r)$ the first two terms have nonnegative sum and $r\delta^2>0$. Thus the stated endpoints are strict as well. Theorem 3.1 supplies the equality class for $s=r$. The last exclusion follows by rearranging Theorem 2.1 directly. ∎
+
+**Theorem 8.2 (Exact two-moment relaxation at $r=9$).** Consider probability laws on pairs $(K,U)$ with integer $1\le K\le10$, real $U\ge K$, and
+
+$$
+\mathbb E K=8,\qquad \mathbb E U=10.
+$$
+
+The exact infimum, attained by such a law, is
+
+$$
+\min\mathbb E(KU^2)=516+16\sqrt{63}<648=2F_9(8).\tag{8.3}
+$$
+
+An attaining law, with $h=4\sqrt{63}$, is
+
+$$
+\begin{array}{c|ccc}
+(K,U)&(1,1+h)&(8,8)&(9,9)\\ \hline
+\mathbb P&2/h&1-16/h&14/h.
+\end{array}\tag{8.4}
+$$
+
+There is also a wholly rational feasible law
+
+$$
+\begin{array}{c|ccc}
+(K,U)&(1,33)&(8,8)&(9,9)\\ \hline
+\mathbb P&1/16&1/2&7/16
+\end{array}
+$$
+
+with objective $643<648$. Neither law is induced by a genuine profile on $[10]$ through Definition 1.1.
+
+**Proof.** Here $a=8$, $D=217$, $C=1224$, $f_9(8)=512$ and $\kappa_9=2+8\sqrt{63}=2+2h$. The pointwise scalar inequality (2.1), which was proved for all integer $k\ge1$ and all $u\ge k$, integrates over any law in this relaxed problem to give
+
+$$
+\mathbb E(KU^2)\ge(217-\kappa_9)8+\kappa_9\,10-1224
+=516+16\sqrt{63}.
+$$
+
+This is weak duality proved simply by integrating a pointwise inequality; it invokes no strong-duality or joint-realizability theorem.
+
+Since $h>16$, all three probabilities in (8.4) are positive and sum to one. Direct summation gives $\mathbb E K=8$ and $\mathbb E U=10$. Equality holds in the scalar support inequality at each atom: at $K=1$, $U=\kappa_9/2=1+h$, while $K=8,9$ are the two integer zeros with $U=K$. Its objective is therefore the lower bound, proving attainment. It is strictly less than $648$ because $16\sqrt{63}<132$, equivalently $63<(33/4)^2$. The rational law has means
+
+$$
+\frac{1+64+63}{16}=8,\qquad
+\frac{33+64+63}{16}=10,
+$$
+
+and objective
+
+$$
+\frac{1089}{16}+\frac{512}{2}+\frac{7\cdot729}{16}=643.
+$$
+
+For nonrealizability, either law assigns positive mass to $(K,U)=(8,8)$. If induced by a genuine finite array, some positive-mass eight-element type $T$ would satisfy
+
+$$
+8=U_T=\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-1},\qquad y_i^{-1}\ge1.
+$$
+
+Every one of these eight marginals would equal one. Every positive-mass type would then contain all these eight elements, forcing $K\ge8$ almost surely. This contradicts the positive mass at $K=1$. The positive mass at $(K,U)=(9,9)$ also violates (2.2), since $q=8$ requires $U\ge81/8>9$ on every nine-element type of any actual array. Thus both laws exhibit the insufficiency of the relaxed moment constraints. They provide no genuine-array counterexample, and the exact relaxed optimum (8.3) coexists with the strictly larger actual-array bound of Theorem 2.3. ∎

+**Definition 8.3 (Remaining comparison and its method boundary).** For $r\ge11$ outside the unconditional region of Theorem 8.1, and without the support hypothesis of Theorem 4.1, the remaining comparison asks whether every genuine profile of mean $q\in[r-1,r]$ and finite $s\ge r$ satisfies
+
+$$
+J_s(x)\ge F_r(q).
+$$
+
+Theorem 4.2 specifies a necessary weighted low-cardinality defect for any counterexample, and (8.2) already excludes sufficiently large $s$. This unrestricted comparison for $r\ge11$ remains open in that range; the conditional graph minimum of Theorem 6.1 does not settle it.

+For $r=9$, the full interval $q\in[8,9]$ is covered by Theorem 3.2. At $q=8$, $s=10$, (2.9) supplies the quantitative compensation above the moment-relaxation optimum $516+16\sqrt{63}$, with a strict margin greater than $32$ beyond the $132-16\sqrt{63}$ needed to reach $2F_9(8)=648$. The exact actual-array minimum and all minimizing arrays at that point are not determined here. For $r=10$, Theorem 2.4 settles the comparison for the full interval $q\in[9,10]$ and every finite $s\ge11$; optimality of its numerical gap is not determined here. The overlap constraints (2.2)–(2.3) are necessary, with no claim that they characterize every realizable joint law. The certificate (2.5) is asserted only for $q\in[8,9]$, and (2.10) only for $q\in[9,10]$. Theorem 9.2 shows that even the self-consistent distribution-dependent $m_k$ constraints are insufficient by themselves to prove the all-$r$ comparison. +## 9. A self-consistent overlap relaxation that fails for every $r\ge17$
+
+**Definition 9.1 (Distribution-dependent scalar relaxation).** For a positive integer $s$ and a real $q$, consider finite probability laws on pairs $(K,U)$ such that
+
+$$
+K\in\{1,\ldots,s\},\qquad
+\mathbb E K=q,\qquad \mathbb E U=s,\qquad
+m_k=\mathbb E\min(k,K)\quad(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}),
+$$
+
+$$
+U\ge\max\{K,K^2/m_K\}\quad\text{almost surely}.
+$$
+
+The surrogate objective is $V=\mathbb E(KU^2)$. The same $K$ law is used to compute every $m_k$; these values are not independent variables. By (2.2) and the incidence identity, every actual array supplies a feasible law with $V\le2J_s(x)$. Sufficiency of these scalar constraints for an actual array is not part of this definition.
+
+**Theorem 9.2 (A rational obstruction throughout $r\ge17$).** For every integer $a\ge16$, put $r=a+1$, $q=a$, $s=a+2$, and $M=5a^2-a+1$. The following law is feasible in Definition 9.1:
+
+$$
+\begin{array}{c|ccc}
+K&1&a&a+1\\ \hline
+\mathbb P&1/(5a)&4/5&(a-1)/(5a)\\
+U&(41a^4+13a^2+1)/(aM)&5a^3/M&(a+1)^2/a.
+\end{array}\tag{9.1}
+$$
+
+Its objective satisfies
+
+$$
+V-a(a+1)^2=-\frac{P(a)}{5a^2M^2}<0,\tag{9.2}
+$$
+
+where
+
+$$
+P(a)=110a^8-1697a^7+58a^6-949a^5+56a^4-211a^3+24a^2-18a+2.
+$$
+
+No actual array on $[s]$ with all marginals positive induces this law. In particular minimizing the scalar surrogate under Definition 9.1 cannot alone give the lower bound $2F_r(a)=a(a+1)^2$ for all $r$.
+
+**Proof.** All three probabilities are positive and sum to one. Their means are
+
+$$
+\frac1{5a}+\frac{4a}{5}+\frac{(a+1)(a-1)}{5a}=a,
+$$
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\mathbb E U
+&=\frac{41a^4+13a^2+1}{5a^2M}
+ +\frac{4a^3}{M}+\frac{(a-1)(a+1)^2}{5a^2}\\
+&=a+2=s.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+The same $K$ law gives, at all cardinalities that carry mass,
+
+$$
+m_1=1,\qquad
+m_a=\frac1{5a}+a\left(\frac45+\frac{a-1}{5a}\right)
+=a-\frac{a-1}{5a}=\frac{M}{5a},\qquad
+m_{a+1}=a.
+$$
+
+Writing $U_k$ for the value of $U$ at cardinality $k$ in (9.1), one has $U_a=a^2/m_a$ and $U_{a+1}=(a+1)^2/m_{a+1}$. Since $m_a\le a$ and $m_{a+1}\le a+1$, these two values also satisfy $U\ge K$. For the singleton atom,
+
+$$
+U_1-1=\frac{41a^4-5a^3+14a^2-a+1}{aM}>0.
+$$
+
+Its numerator is $a^3(41a-5)+a(14a-1)+1>0$ for $a\ge1$, so both constraints hold there as well. Also $1\le K\le a+1<s$. This proves all of the relaxed feasibility conditions simultaneously.
+
+Direct substitution into $V$ gives
+
+$$
+V=\frac{(41a^4+13a^2+1)^2}{5a^3M^2}
++\frac{20a^7}{M^2}+\frac{(a-1)(a+1)^5}{5a^3}.
+$$
+
+Subtracting $a(a+1)^2$ and collecting terms gives (9.2). To prove its strict sign for every $a\ge16$, group the polynomial as
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+P(a)&=a^7(110a-1697)+a^5(58a-949)\\
+&\quad+a^3(56a-211)+(24a^2-18a+2).
+\end{aligned}

+The first two terms together are at least
+
+$$

+## 10. Genuine rare extra hubs and the scale of a uniform gap
+
+**Theorem 10.1 (A genuine family with gap of order $r^{3/2}$).** For every integer $a\ge4$, put $r=a+1$, $s=a+2$, $H=[a+1]$ and $e=a+2$. For each real $0<\varepsilon\le1/a$, define the one array
+
+$$
+x_{\{e\}}=\varepsilon,\qquad x_H=(a-1)\varepsilon,\qquad
+x_{H\setminus\{j\}}=\frac{1-a\varepsilon}{a+1}\quad(j\in H),
+$$
+
+with every other type mass zero. This is an actual profile of mean $q=a$ with positive marginals. Its support hypergraph, with vertices $[s]$ and hyperedges the positive-mass types, has two connected components. Define
+
+$$
+E_a=2a^3-2a-1,\qquad A_a=2a^3+2a^2-2a-1.
+$$
+
+Its energy and gap are exactly
+
+$$
+2J_s(x)=\frac{(a+1)^2[a^3+\varepsilon E_a]}{(a-\varepsilon)^2}
++\frac1\varepsilon,\tag{10.1}
+$$
+
+$$
+2\bigl(J_s(x)-F_r(a)\bigr)
+=\frac1\varepsilon+
+\frac{(a+1)^2\varepsilon(A_a-a\varepsilon)}{(a-\varepsilon)^2}>0.\tag{10.2}
+$$
+
+For $\varepsilon_a=1/(\sqrt2\,a^{3/2})$ the limit is
+
+$$
+\frac{J_s(x(\varepsilon_a))-F_{a+1}(a)}{a^{3/2}}
+\longrightarrow\sqrt2,
+\qquad
+\frac{J_s(x(\varepsilon_a))-F_{a+1}(a)}{(a+1)^{3/2}}
+\longrightarrow\sqrt2.\tag{10.3}
+$$
+
+Thus no constant $c>0$ can satisfy $J_s(x)-F_r(q)\ge cr^2$ uniformly for all integers $r\ge5$, all finite $s\ge r+1$ and all actual profiles with $q\in[r-1,r]$.
+
+**Proof.** The displayed masses are nonnegative and sum to
+
+$$
+\varepsilon+(a-1)\varepsilon+1-a\varepsilon=1.
+$$
+
+Their cardinality mean is
+
+$$
+\varepsilon+(a+1)(a-1)\varepsilon+a(1-a\varepsilon)=a.
+$$
+
+Counting the types containing each hub gives
+
+$$
+y_i=\frac{a-\varepsilon}{a+1}>0\quad(i\in H),\qquad
+y_e=\varepsilon>0,
+$$
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+w_i&=\frac{a^3(1-a\varepsilon)}{a+1}
+ +(a+1)^2(a-1)\varepsilon
+ =\frac{a^3+\varepsilon E_a}{a+1}\quad(i\in H),\\
+w_e&=\varepsilon.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+In particular the extra marginal is retained. The only positive-mass type containing $e$ is $\{e\}$, while $H$ itself has positive mass. +# 递归关系观察：首次标记的完整终止实验与事件恢复
+
+## 1. 同一源、完整档案与终止正规形
+
+**假设 1.1（PG27 的共同隐藏源）。** 固定 $a,b>0$、$a+b=1$，以及 $(0,1)$ 上的 Borel 概率测度 $\mu$。先取 $Q\sim\mu$，独立取 $X_0\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(b)$。条件于同一对 $(Q,X_0)$，从根分别向左、右生成相互独立的外向 Markov 臂，转移矩阵为
+
+$$
+P_q=\begin{pmatrix}1-q&q\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
+\tag{TEE.1}
+$$
+
+再取原始可见种子 $U\sim\lambda$，其空间 $(\mathcal U,\mathcal E)$ 为任意可测空间，$U$ 独立于上述全部源变量。已读区域从根开始，始终为连通区间。每个活动步骤只能选择 $L$ 或 $R$，取得该侧一条尚未读取的边，费用为一。回答 $0$ 表示两端不同，回答 $1$ 表示两端相同；源禁止 $11$，故回答 $1$ 必为 $00$ 标记，界面在首次标记后自动终止。策略 $\pi$ 在每个有限已获动作—回答记录上给出总定义的可测种子截面；等待标记策略在所有活动步骤都查询一条新边。全随机带属于原来的 $U$，不在存活后替换其分布。记 $p_0=a,p_1=b$。
+
+本卷定理1.3、命题2.1、定理2.3及其定理3.1、命题4.1的源内综合推导标为 `repo-derived`；几何级数、Bayes 归一化、实验随机化复合和紧区间矩唯一性只作为这些推导的既有中间步骤。
+
+本假设采用 [Process Geometry 第27节](RECURSIVE_RELATIONAL_OBSERVATION_PROCESS_GEOMETRY.md) 的源及接口，特别是定义27.15的等待策略。其定理27.2–27.4供应完整历史条件律、根位锚定和联合质量核；定理27.16供应任意 $\mu$ 下的几乎必然终止，不要求有限均值。正文的终止档案任务额外明确读取已经保留的原始种子和完整旧记录；它与第27节禁止新残余测试免费读取旧档案的任务不同。
+
+**定义 1.2（完整终止档案及事件数）。** 令
+
+$$
+H_\pi=\bigl(U;(J_1,Y_1),\ldots,(J_T,Y_T)\bigr),
+\qquad Y_1=\cdots=Y_{T-1}=0,\quad Y_T=1,
+\tag{TEE.2}
+$$
+
+其中 $T<\infty$ 是实际支付的新边数，种子与有序记录全部保留。由最后标记沿已获相邻关系解出的根位记为 $x(H_\pi)=X_0$。令 $R(H_\pi)$ 为已获边中按各臂的外向顺序发生的 $0\to1$ 次数，$D(H_\pi)$ 为 $1\to0$ 次数。唯一的 $00$ 不计入二者。最后查询的一侧称标记侧；其外端点为零。另一侧的终端外端点位记为 $B(H_\pi)\in\{0,1\}$；该侧未查询时，其端点就是根。
+
+档案空间 $\mathcal A_\pi$ 只包含与策略相容、首次标记终止、并能在禁止 $11$ 的源中实现的有限记录及原种子，配备 $\mathcal U$ 与可数有限记录空间的乘积所诱导的可测结构。它不包括零概率的无限未终止运行。单次 $H_\pi$ 不包含未读臂、真实 $Q$、重置、复制或重复试验权限。
+

+$$

+\quad F_\pi(H)=(U,x(H),R(H)),
+\qquad G_\pi=F_\pi^{-1}.
+\tag{TEE.3}
+$$

+
+$$

+=\lambda(E)p_x(1-q)q^r.
+\tag{TEE.4}
+$$

+
+$$

+$$

+
+机会必无穷多：一条臂上的每次确定 $1\to0$，除根为一时该臂的首次确定转移外，都必须有同臂先前的 $0\to1$。所以在前 $r$ 次成功机会与下一个机会之间，确定转移总数不超过 $r+2$。第 $r+1$ 个机会至迟在第 $2r+3$ 步出现。构造保留完整 $u$ 与全部有序动作；每条臂给出的位串满足式（TEE.1）的支持条件。每个有限这样的柱集在每个 $0<q<1$ 下都有正的源质量。
+
+反向，任何 $H\in\mathcal A_\pi$ 在标记前只收到零，所以动作恰为 $w_\pi(u)$ 的前缀。若标记侧在最后查询前已有 $n$ 条边，则其端点为 $x\oplus(n\bmod2)$；标记要求这个端点为零，故 $x=n\bmod2$，根唯一确定。以此根逐边重建，两臂总共恰有 $R(H)$ 次成功机会，最后是下一次失败机会。因此上述构造逐项还原 $H$，同时 $F_\pi G_\pi(u,x,r)=(u,x,r)$。
+
+可测性不需要种子空间的标准 Borel 假设。对固定 $x,r$，构造长度至多 $2r+3$；有限动作词的种子原像由有限次可测选择组成，形成有限可测分割。由此 $G_\pi$ 对每个离散截面可测；$F_\pi$ 的种子投影、有限词根奇偶与事件计数也可测。档案的合法性逐有限词判定，因此 $\mathcal A_\pi$ 是上述乘积中的可测子集。
+
+在每个种子分割片上，固定根的所获臂柱集有 $r$ 个概率因子 $q$、一个因子 $1-q$，其余因子全为一。两臂只在固定同一 $(q,x)$ 后相乘，所以该质量恰为 $q^r(1-q)$，与分割片及左右交织无关。对 $E$ 与各分割片的交集积分，再乘独立根质量 $p_x$，得到式（TEE.4）；再对原先验积分得到式（TEE.5）。没有对种子单点除法，也没有把实际存活后的种子当成独立种子。几何级数总质量为一，与原源的几乎必然终止相符。证毕。
+
+## 2. 事件守恒与四种表达的精确恢复
+
+**命题 2.1（独立于统计似然的端点事件守恒）。** 对每份定义1.2的实际终止档案，逐路径有
+
+$$
+B-2X_0=R-D,
+\qquad T=R+D+1,
+\qquad \boxed{T=2R+2X_0+1-B}.
+\tag{TEE.6}
+$$
+
+证明。沿每条臂将每条已获边的“外端位减内端位”相加，望远镜求和得到该臂终端位减根位。两臂的和为 $0+B-2X_0$。每条 $0\to1$ 贡献一，每条 $1\to0$ 贡献负一，标记 $00$ 贡献零，故第一式成立。全部已获边恰由这三类组成，且首次标记终止给出恰一个 $00$，故第二式成立。消去 $D$ 得第三式。证明只用实际边及其共同端点，没有使用式（TEE.4）、几何律或 Bayes 公式。证毕。
+
+**定义 2.2（已校准的终止记忆任务）。** 固定假设1.1中的已知先验。令
+
+$$
+z_r=\int(1-q)q^r\,\mu(dq)>0,
+\qquad \nu_r(dq)=\frac{(1-q)q^r}{z_r}\mu(dq).
+\tag{TEE.7}
+$$
+
+终止后的校准记忆任务是：对每个有界 Borel 函数 $f:(0,1)\to\mathbb R$，给出完整档案下的条件分数 $\mathbb E[f(Q)\mid H_\pi]$。摘要 $Z=Z(H_\pi)$ 对该任务精确，指每个这样的分数都有 $Z$ 的可测函数版本。此任务涵盖有界 $Q$ 决策的各动作条件损失，不把原生终止后的拒绝接口扩张成参数端口。记 $\mathsf M(H)=\nu_{R(H)}$，测度值空间取由 Borel 集求值生成的可测结构。
+
+**定理 2.3（同一终止事件关系的恢复定理）。** 在假设1.1的全部先验和等待策略上，下列结论成立。
+
+(a) 完整终止档案的参数后验恰为
+
+$$
+\mathcal L(Q\mid H_\pi)=\mathsf M(H_\pi)=\nu_R.
+\tag{TEE.8}
+$$
+
+若 $\mu$ 非 Dirac，则 $r\mapsto\nu_r$ 单射，且定义2.2的摘要精确当且仅当 $R$ 是该摘要的可测函数，均按实际联合律的几乎处处意义。若 $\mu=\delta_{q_*}$，则全部后验等于 $\delta_{q_*}$，常值摘要已经精确，后验本身不能恢复随机 $R$。
+
+(b) 对事件四元组 $(R,X_0,B,T)$ 的实际像，以下是相互一致的恢复式：
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+T&=2R+2X_0+1-B,\\
+B&=1-(T\bmod2),\\
+R&=\lfloor T/2\rfloor-X_0,\\
+X_0&=\lfloor T/2\rfloor-R.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{TEE.9}
+$$
+
+因此 $(R,X_0,B)$、$(T,X_0)$ 和 $(R,T)$ 各能恢复整个四元组。非 Dirac 时，可将这些式子中的 $R$ 换成精确后验 $\mathsf M$；Dirac 时仍可使用时间和根位的恢复式，但不能从常值后验取回 $R$。这些映射只在实际像上使用，不能把独立列出的坐标任意拼成实际档案。
+
+(c) 原种子和已知策略可以消去额外的辅助坐标。$(U,T)$ 逐项恢复完整 $H_\pi$：回放 $T-1$ 次零及一次标记，得到所有动作及根位；$(U,X_0,R)$ 则由定理1.3恢复完整档案。于是 $(U,R,T)$ 也足够，但单独的 $(R,T)$ 一般只恢复式（TEE.9）的粗四元组。对固定策略及原种子律，$(R,X_0)$ 恢复 $T$ 的充要条件是 $B$ 在这些实际纤维上存在可测因子；$T$ 恢复 $R$ 的充要条件是 $X_0$ 在 $T$ 的实际纤维上存在可测因子。这些条件有相同的几乎处处版本。任意可测值域上的“纤维常值”若未另证可测下降，只表示集合层条件。
+
+(d) 非 Dirac 时，$\mathsf M$ 与 $R$ 是同一个校准记忆，但它们均不能单独恢复 $X_0$ 或 $T$，即使同时给出 $U$ 也不能。Dirac 时常值记忆亦不能单独恢复时间或根位。粗四元组不普遍恢复左右长度、原子边身份或有序查询词；在(c)的额外数据齐备时才由完整档案重建所获有限区间的位与顺序。
+
+证明。(a) 将式（TEE.5）除以正的 $z_r$，给出对任意可测种子事件、根事件和计数事件的积分恒等式，即式（TEE.8）的显式条件核。它在任意原种子空间上成立，不依赖对完整档案作一般正则条件分布存在性假设。这是使用通常 Bayes 归一化作为定理1.3的中间步骤。
+
+为核对非退化性，置 $m_r=\int q\,\nu_r(dq)=z_{r+1}/z_r$。$\nu_r$ 与 $\mu$ 等价，因为其密度在 $(0,1)$ 处处严格正。$\nu_{r+1}$ 是 $\nu_r$ 的 $q$ 倾斜，故
+
+$$
+m_{r+1}-m_r
+=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_r}(Q)}{m_r}>0
+\quad\text{当 }\mu\text{ 非 Dirac}.
+\tag{TEE.10}
+$$
+
+因此 $m_r$ 严格递增，单个精确均值在这个特定后验族上已经编码 $r$。若 $Z$ 精确，则取 $f(q)=q$ 得到 $m_R=g(Z)$；在可数值集 $\{m_r:r\ge0\}$ 上取逆，并在其补集任意取零，给出可测 $R$。反向若已恢复 $R$，式（TEE.7）给出所有分数。Dirac 时全部分数恒为 $f(q_*)$，而 $\Pr(R=r)=(1-q_*)q_*^r>0$ 对所有 $r$ 成立，所以常值后验不恢复计数。
+
+(b) 式（TEE.6）取模二，得 $B=1-(T\bmod2)$；于是 $\lfloor T/2\rfloor=R+X_0$，给出其余两式。这也表明 $T-2R$ 只可能取 $0,1,2,3$，依次对应 $(X_0,B)=(0,1),(0,0),(1,1),(1,0)$；其中 $R=0,X_0=0,B=1$ 无实际实现，因为从根零得到另端一至少消耗一次 $0\to1$。即使满足这些算术约束，固定策略还可能排除额外组合，故恢复域始终是该策略的实际像。
+
+(c) 标记前所有回答已知为零，故给定 $u,T$ 的策略回放唯一；最后侧的已读奇偶决定根，随后所有位和事件数由相邻关系恢复。这使用已经取得的旧档案长度，没有免费旧时钟。关于 $(R,X_0)$ 的充要条件，若 $B$ 已下降则第一恢复式给出 $T$；反向从该式可解出 $B$。关于 $T$ 的条件同理由 $R+X_0=\lfloor T/2\rfloor$ 得到。
+
+(d) 式（TEE.5）表明 $X_0$ 独立于 $(U,R)$，两种根位各有严格正质量。因此 $(U,R)$ 不能恢复 $X_0$。若它能恢复 $T$，第三、四恢复式又会恢复 $X_0$，矛盾。非 Dirac 的 $\mathsf M$ 与 $R$ 可逆，Dirac 的常值记忆信息更少，故相应结论成立。下面命题的正质量实例给出其余不可恢复结论。证毕。
+
+**命题 2.4（辅助坐标及空间粗化的实际反例）。** 允许原种子含一个独立公平位时，存在同一个等待策略，使 $T$ 单独不能恢复 $R$，也存在同一个等待策略，使 $(R,X_0)$ 单独不能恢复 $B$；另一方面，确定策略可使这些辅助坐标冗余。即使 $(R,X_0,B,T)$ 全给出，一般也不能恢复完整空间区间或有序记录。
+
+证明。第一例令种子零时始终查询左边，种子一时前两次查询依次为 $L,R$，以后始终查询左边。在 $U=0,X_0=1$ 时，左侧先发生确定 $1\to0$ 再标记，给 $(T,R,B)=(2,0,1)$。在 $U=1,X_0=0$ 时，左侧先成功 $0\to1$，右侧立即标记，给 $(T,R,B)=(2,1,1)$。两事件的概率分别为 $b z_0/2$、$a z_1/2$，都严格正。同一个已付时间和终端另一侧位不能恢复根或计数；保留原种子即按定理2.3(c)恢复。
+
+同一策略也给第二例。在 $U=0,X_0=0,R=1$ 时，记录为 $L0,L0,L1$，故 $T=3,B=0$；在 $U=1,X_0=0,R=1$ 时，记录为 $L0,R1$，故 $T=2,B=1$。两事件都具有概率 $a z_1/2$，所以同一 $(R,X_0)$ 的纤维内时间和端点不同。
+
+若策略确定为始终向左，则 $B=X_0$、$T=2R+X_0+1$，故 $T$ 的奇偶已经决定根，$(R,X_0)$ 也决定时间。这不改变两个根位都可能对应同一 $R$ 的事实。
+
+最后令原种子决定始终向左或始终向右。根零且 $R=1$ 的记录分别为 $L0,L0,L1$ 和 $R0,R0,R1$，两者都有 $(R,X_0,B,T)=(1,0,0,3)$，概率各为 $a z_1/2$，而左右长度为 $(3,0)$ 和 $(0,3)$。若只丢顺序，另可取种子选择零回放前缀 $LLRR$ 或 $RRLL$、随后均查询 $L$；根零且 $R=2$ 时两者均在第五步标记，得到同样的左右长度 $(3,2)$ 及全部位，却有不同的前四次顺序。两种记录的质量各为 $a z_2/2$。这些均是原源上的正质量柱集，不是把无关对象拼成的形式反例。证毕。
+
+## 3. 恢复映射的统计实验消费者
+
+**定理 3.1（合法实验运输、主动截断与辨识边界）。** 仍使用假设1.1，以下各结论均以定理1.3及定理2.3的显式恢复映射为前提。
+
+(a) 设 $\pi,\sigma$ 是同一原种子空间及种子律上的两个等待策略。则
+
+$$
+K_{\pi\sigma}=G_\sigma F_\pi:\mathcal A_\pi\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\sigma
+\tag{TEE.11}
+$$
+
+是与参数和先验无关的可测双射，逆为 $K_{\sigma\pi}$。它保留实际提取出的 $U,X_0,R$，并对每个 $q$ 精确运输完整档案律。因此对任何有界可测损失 $\ell(q,d)$ 和同一个可测动作空间，两个实验的确定或随机化 $Q$ 决策规则可双向运输，逐参数风险及任意先验下的风险相同。可达风险集合相同，故下确界相同；一边有达到下确界的规则，当且仅当另一边也有。
+
+(b) 对任何合法因果的主动停止策略 $\rho$，存在另一个等待标记策略 $\widehat\rho$ 及可测截断映射 $C_\rho$，使 $C_\rho(H_{\widehat\rho})$ 与 $\rho$ 的完整原种子档案具有相同的逐参数分布。在同一预生成两臂与原种子的比较实现中，这份截断档案逐路径就是实际 $\rho$ 的档案，几乎处处成立。因此任何等待策略的完整终止实验都可经参数无关映射产生该主动停止实验；反向普遍等价不成立。
+
+(c) 若 $\mu$ 非 Dirac，则没有完整终止档案的可测函数等于真实 $Q$ 几乎处处；若 $\mu$ 为 Dirac，则先验中的该常数已经等于 $Q$。若 $\mu$ 无原子，任何可测精确猜测 $\widehat Q(H)$ 的成功概率都为零。若 $\mu$ 有原子，其原子在每个 $\nu_r$ 中仍有正质量，所有原来的非原子成分也保留；只要先验非 Dirac，任何原子猜测的后验成功概率都严格小于一。
+
+(d) 在固定的 PG27 设计、已识别的计数 $R$ 及原始完整计数律下，映射 $\mu\mapsto(\Pr(R=r))_{r\ge0}$ 单射。这里给出的是整个实验分布族的辨识；从一份已获档案不能在两个不同 Dirac 先验之间普遍无误辨识先验律，更不能据此为当前观察者增加重复试验。
+
+证明。(a) 双射和逆映射直接由式（TEE.3）得到。由式（TEE.4），在每个 $q$ 下两个正规形的分布都是
+
+$$
+\lambda(du)\,p_x\,(1-q)q^r.
+\tag{TEE.12}
+$$
+
+故 $K_{\pi\sigma}$ 确实运输实验。若 $\delta_\pi$ 是 $\pi$ 的随机决策核，则在 $\sigma$ 上采用 $\delta_\sigma(H)=\delta_\pi(K_{\sigma\pi}H)$，积分给出相同风险；确定规则是 Dirac 决策核的特例。反向相同。这里只使用随机化的复合这个经典实验比较中间步骤；参见 Pollard, *Some thoughts on Le Cam's statistical decision theory*, arXiv:[1107.3811v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.3811v1)，第1节关于随机化与决策核复合的讨论。显式 $F,G$ 处理本节的任意种子空间和连续参数，结论不依赖从有限参数比较定理推出未经核对的连续参数逆定理。
+
+对固定先验，还可直接用式（TEE.7）写最小风险下确界。若 $D$ 非空且 $\ell$ 有界，则
+
+$$
+\inf_\delta\mathbb E[\ell(Q,\delta(H))]
+=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}z_r\inf_{d\in D}\int\ell(q,d)\nu_r(dq).
+\tag{TEE.13}
+$$
+
+左侧允许随机规则。每个条件平均都不低于相应下确界；反向对每个可数 $r$ 选择误差不超过 $\varepsilon$ 的动作，按 $R$ 使用该动作即为可测规则，总误差不超过 $\varepsilon\sum z_r=\varepsilon$。这没有假设精确最优动作存在。例如 $D=(0,1)$、$\ell(q,d)=d$ 时，下确界为零而无任何达到它的确定或随机规则。式（TEE.13）只是正规形的决策消费者，不是额外的标量估计接口。
+
+实验运输也不宣称在同一对预生成臂上 $K_{\pi\sigma}(H_\pi)=H_\sigma$。取两策略分别始终向左、始终向右，条件于 $Q=q,X_0=0$；左侧第一条边标记、右侧第一条边成功而下一条确定返回零、第三条标记的联合事件质量为 $(1-q)^2q>0$。这时实际 $R_\pi=0,R_\sigma=1$，而运输映射保留 $R_\pi=0$。运输只陈述实验律及可转移决策，不产生另一策略在该同一源上的未获事实。
+
+(b) 定义不同的合法观察者 $\widehat\rho$：在 $\rho$ 尚未选择主动停止时，按同一 $U$ 和已获记录执行其查询；当本地模拟的 $\rho$ 首次选择主动停止时，保存该前缀，此后每个活动步骤都向左查询，直到原生首次标记终止。它不擦除原种子或旧记录，也不查询真实参数。虚拟停止标志由 $U$ 和历史可测地计算，故 $\widehat\rho$ 属于等待策略。由 PG27 定理27.16，它几乎必然有限终止，不论均值是否有限。
+
+在 $H_{\widehat\rho}$ 上回放 $\rho$，一旦它主动停止就截取此前完整前缀并保留主动停止标签；若先见标记，则保留截至标记的记录。这给出 $C_\rho$，按每个有限词检查可知可测。两观察者在该前缀前的真实动作与读取边完全相同，故在共同源及种子上截断逐路径正确。它没有让已经停止的实际 $\rho$ 继续操作；继续操作的是另一个合法比较观察者。再与式（TEE.11）的运输复合，得任意等待实验到主动停止实验的映射。
+
+非 Dirac 时，让 $\rho$ 在零次查询就停止，其档案只有独立种子，参数后验为 $\mu$；而等待实验的后验均值在 $R=0,1$ 两个正质量事件上因式（TEE.10）而不同。由平方损失的条件方差分解，等待后的最小 Bayes 风险比先验风险低 $\operatorname{Var}(m_R)>0$。因此一般不能从独立种子产生同样的联合参数—档案律，主动停止可严格损失 $Q$ 信息。
+
+(c) 所有 $\nu_r$ 都与 $\mu$ 等价。非 Dirac 的 $\mu$ 因而不可能在任何有限计数后变成 Dirac。若存在 $Q=\widehat Q(H)$ 几乎处处，则完整档案下的条件分布必须是 $\delta_{\widehat Q(H)}$，与式（TEE.8）矛盾。无原子时，显式条件核还给出
+
+$$
+\Pr(\widehat Q(H)=Q\mid H)=\nu_R(\{\widehat Q(H)\})=0.
+\tag{TEE.14}
+$$
+

+# Recursive relational observation: stopped mean cost and spatial risk on one source
+
+This companion fixes one PG27 source and relates two quantities measured on the
+same realization: fresh-edge queries actually paid before a marker or a
+voluntary stop, and prior-average root error on the connected interval that was
+actually exposed. The hidden parameter is integrated before decoding. The
+observer keeps the original independent seed and never receives a parameter
+port, a reset, a copied arm, or a survival-conditioned seed law.
+
+## 1. Source, replay horizons, and the two objectives
+
+**Definition 1.1 (fixed shared source).** Let $a,b>0$ with $a+b=1$, let
+$Q\sim\mu$ on $(0,1)$, and let $X_0\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(b)$ be
+independent of $Q$. Conditional on $(Q,X_0)$, the left and right arms are
+independent copies of the Markov chain
+$$
+P_Q=\begin{pmatrix}1-Q&Q\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
+$$
+A fresh boundary query costs one unit and returns $1$ exactly on a newly
+exposed $00$ edge. The first such marker stops source access. An observer has
+an independent seed $U\sim\nu$ and may choose sides causally from $U$ and the
+ordered action/reply journal. Every fixed finite-history seed section of the
+action, stop, and decoder rules is measurable. The seed is visible to decoding.
+The controller must decide almost surely, with a forced root label; coherent
+interval labels are obtained by propagating that root guess through the journal.
+Their event $0$-$1$ loss equals root loss: correct root plus the acquired
+relations gives every exposed label, and a correct whole labeling includes the
+root. An incoherent labeling cannot improve the minimum, since it matches
+neither of the two possible coherent labelings. On a marker the root and every label in the
+exposed connected interval are recovered by propagation. On a marker-free
+journal the observer may stop voluntarily.
+
+Put
+$$
+M_j=\int q^j\,\mu(dq),\qquad A_j=M_j-M_{j+1},\qquad
+v_j=bA_{j-1}-aA_j\quad(j\ge1),
+$$
+and $J_N=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}M_j$ for $N\ge1$. Thus $A_j>0$ and
+$M_j\downarrow0$. A zero-reply replay has arm lengths $(\ell,r)$, with
+$$
+k=\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor+\lfloor r/2\rfloor,\qquad
+s=(\ell\bmod2)+(r\bmod2).
+$$
+Its two integrated root masses are $aM_{k+s}$ and $bM_k$, so write
+$$
+e(\ell,r)=\min\{aM_{k+s},bM_k\}.
+$$
+Write $C=\mathbb E T$ for the extended mean actual paid count and $E$ for
+the prior-average error of the chosen decoder. Prior-integrated MAP minimizes
+this error separately on every finite terminal journal, including ties.
+
+For a fixed horizon $n$, a policy is required to continue on the zero-reply
+replay until exactly $n$ queries and then stop if no marker has appeared. Its
+actual paid count is the marker time truncated at $n$, not the declared
+horizon.

+## 2. A common linear description of zero-replay shapes
+
+**Lemma 2.1 (shape sequence and actual prefix cost).** At every odd depth
+$2m+1$, the zero-reply replay has one even and one odd arm. At every even
+depth $2m$, it has either two even arms or two odd arms. Let
+$\lambda_m\in[0,1]$ be the original-seed probability of the latter shape at
+depth $2m$; for a deterministic seed it is $0$ or $1$. Every prescribed
+finite sequence of even-depth shapes is realized by a lawful side schedule, and
+the schedule can be chosen independently of $(Q,X_0)$.
+
+Let $\tau$ be the marker time of any continued version of the replay route.
+For depths before the voluntary horizon, its integrated survival tails are
+$$
+\Pr(\tau>2m+1)=bM_m+aM_{m+1},
+$$
+and, for $m\ge1$,
+$$
+\Pr(\tau>2m)=M_m+\lambda_m v_m.
+$$
+Consequently $C_0=0$, $C_1=1$, and, for $N\ge1$,
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+C_{2N}(\lambda)
+ &=2J_N-a+aM_N+\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}\lambda_m v_m,\\
+C_{2N+1}(\lambda)
+ &=2J_N-a+(1+a)M_N+\sum_{m=1}^{N}\lambda_m v_m.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+**Proof.** A zero reply flips the selected arm’s parity. The conditional
+survival mass at an odd depth is $q^m(b+aq)$; at an even depth it is $q^m$
+for the even/even shape and $q^{m-1}(b+aq^2)$ for the odd/odd shape. Their
+difference is $(1-q)(b-aq)q^{m-1}$, whose $\mu$-integral is $v_m$. The
+original seed is independent of the source, so averaging the replay partition
+gives the displayed tails. Summing $\Pr(\tau>t)$ for $0\le t<n$ by Tonelli
+gives the two formulas. To realize a requested next even shape from an even
+depth, first query the
+left arm. On a zero reply the parities are mixed. Then query the arm whose
+current parity is $1$ when the target is even/even, and the arm whose parity
+is $0$ when the target is odd/odd. A marker interrupts either step.
+This is the lawful shape construction in PG27.17, with no extra clock or
+random source. $\square$
+
+**Lemma 2.2 (terminal risk at a fixed cap).** For $N\ge1$, the even-cap
+zero-replay risks of the two terminal shapes are
+$$
+E_N^{\mathrm{ee}}=\min(a,b)M_N,\qquad
+E_N^{\mathrm{oo}}=\min(aM_{N+1},bM_{N-1}).
+$$
+At an odd cap $2N+1$ with $N\ge0$, both possible zero-replay shapes have risk
+$\min(aM_{N+1},bM_N)$. Therefore the cap frontier supplied by finite-query spatial recovery is
+$$
+R_0^*=\min(a,b),\qquad R_1^*=\min(aM_1,b),\qquad
+R_{2N}^*=\min(aM_{N+1},bM_N),\qquad
+R_{2N+1}^*=\min(aM_{N+1},bM_N).
+$$
+
+**Proof.** A marker identifies a $00$ edge and hence the root and the whole
+connected exposed interval. On the only non-marker leaf, the two root masses
+are $aM_{k+s}$ and $bM_k$, so its Bayes error is their minimum. The displayed values and the fact that the even-cap minimum of the two lawful
+shapes equals the cap frontier are exactly the finite-query spatial
+recovery result. $\square$
+
+## 3. Joint attainment at every finite replay horizon
+
+**Definition 3.1 (joint finite-horizon cost).** Let $\mathcal D_N$ be the
+subset of $\{0,1\}$ consisting of the even/even indicator $d=0$ and the
+odd/odd indicator $d=1$ that attain $R_{2N}^*$; it contains one or both
+indicators according as the two values in Lemma 2.2 are unequal or equal.
+For $n\ge0$, let $K_n$ be the least expected actual paid count among lawful
+fixed-horizon policies whose terminal risk is $R_n^*$.
+
+**Theorem 3.2 (same-source joint attainment).** The quantities $K_n$ are
+attained on the original source and original seed law. They are
+$$
+K_0=0,\qquad K_1=1,
+$$
+and, for $N\ge1$,
+$$
+\boxed{
+K_{2N}=2J_N-a+aM_N+\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}\min(0,v_m),
+}
+$$
+and
+$$
+\boxed{
+K_{2N+1}=2J_N-a+(1+a)M_N+\sum_{m=1}^{N}\min(0,v_m).
+}
+$$
+At an even horizon, choose any terminal shape $d\in\mathcal D_N$; at all
+earlier even depths choose odd/odd exactly when $v_m<0$ (ties are arbitrary).
+At an odd horizon use the same sign choice through $m=N$.
+
+In fact every fixed-horizon policy, regardless of its terminal error, has
+mean cost at least $K_n$. Thus $K_n$ is also the unrestricted least paid-prefix
+mean at that horizon.
+
+**Proof.** By Lemma 2.1, the cost is affine in the shape indicators. Each
+coefficient before the terminal even depth is $v_m$, so its least value is
+obtained by choosing $\lambda_m=1$ when $v_m<0$ and $0$ when $v_m>0$.
+For $n=0,1$ the statements follow directly. At an odd cap the terminal shape
+does not change risk, so the same choice is
+made at $m=N$. At an even cap the terminal shape is restricted only by
+$d\in\mathcal D_N$ and does not occur in $C_{2N}$; it can therefore be
+chosen independently of the preceding cost-minimizing shapes. Lemma 2.1
+realizes all these choices with a single causal side schedule on the same
+source and the same original seed. The linear lower bound holds for every
+seed-randomized schedule because $0\le\lambda_m\le1$ and
+$\lambda_mv_m\ge\min(0,v_m)$. $\square$
+
+The theorem is a joint statement: the cap-risk attainer and the least actual
+paid-prefix mean are realized by one lawful route. Separate minimization of
+the two coordinates would not establish this. The horizon is a replay index;
+the cost is the expectation of the queries actually paid before a marker or
+the cap.
+
+## 4. Infinite endpoint and arbitrary original-seed selectors
+
+Assume for this section
+$$
+I_\mu=\int\frac{\mu(dq)}{1-q}=\sum_{m\ge0}M_m\in(0,\infty].
+$$
+Let $N_*\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the first index with
+$v_{N_*}<0$, with $N_*=\infty$ if there is no such index, and put
+$w_j=bM_{j-1}-aM_j$ and $w_\infty=0$.
+
+**Theorem 4.1 (infinite joint endpoint).** Query left except for the single
+right query numbered $2N_*$ when $N_*<\infty$, and stop at the first marker.
+This controller has zero terminal risk and
+actual mean cost
+$$
+K_\infty=
+\begin{cases}
+2I_\mu-a+w_{N_*},&I_\mu<\infty,\\
++\infty,&I_\mu=\infty.
+\end{cases}
+$$
+The zero-risk claim is almost sure under the fixed source. The finite value is
+attained by this controller; when $I_\mu=\infty$, zero risk remains attained
+but is outside every finite mean-cost budget.
+
+**Proof.** PG27.15--27.18 give the exact tail identity, the sign-minimizing
+shape sequence, and the telescoping correction
+$\sum_m\min(0,v_m)=w_{N_*}$. The marker occurs almost surely for every
+$q<1$, while Tonelli gives the stated finite-mean criterion. The present
+controller uses the same $Q$, both arms, and the original seed, so no new
+endpoint realization is introduced. The finite-prefix formulas also give
+$$
+K_n\uparrow K_\infty,\qquad R_n^*\longrightarrow0.
+$$
+Indeed $\sum_m|v_m|<1$ by PG27.17 and $M_N\to0$. If $I_\mu=\infty$,
+the baseline partial sums diverge while their signed correction stays bounded;
+no subtraction of two infinite quantities is used. Strict increase follows from
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+K_1-K_0&=1,\\
+K_{2N+1}-K_{2N}&=\min\{M_N,bM_{N-1}+aM_{N+1}\}>0 &&(N\ge1),\\
+K_{2N+2}-K_{2N+1}&=bM_N+aM_{N+1}>0 &&(N\ge0).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+All terms are source survival probabilities. $\square$
+
+**Theorem 4.2 (all-policy domination on the original seed).** Let any lawful
+almost-sure-decision controller and decoder have paid mean $C$ and error $E$.
+Its hypothetical all-zero replay determines a measurable horizon
+$H:U\to S:=\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$. There is a lawful replacement on
+the same source, using exactly the same seed $U$ and the same map $H$, with
+$$
+\boxed{
+\widetilde C=\int K_{H(u)}\,\nu(du)\le C,\qquad
+\widetilde E=\int R_{H(u)}^*\,\nu(du)\le E,
+}
+$$
+where $R_\infty^*=0$. Products $0\cdot\infty$ in the corresponding
+countable sums are interpreted as zero. Every measurable horizon selector has
+such an attainer; an infinite replay is allowed because the marker still
+arrives almost surely.
+
+**Proof.** Before a marker the only possible reply string is all zeros. At
+every finite depth its past actions and stop decision are measurable functions
+of $u$: induction uses a finite partition by action words and the measurable
+seed sections. The first replay stop therefore defines the measurable sets
+$\{H=h\}$, and $\{H=\infty\}$ is their complement. Extend each finite
+replay route arbitrarily after its voluntary stop. The actual paid count agrees
+with $\min(H,\tau)$ under that route, including a marker at query $H$.
+There is no other source-dependent non-marker branch on which to choose a
+horizon.
+
+For a fixed finite fiber $\{H=h\}$, each replay action word has mean at least
+$K_h$ by Theorem 3.2, and its Bayes leaf error is at least $R_h^*$ by the
+published cap supplier. The actual decoder can only have larger error. These
+statements are integrated on the finite measurable action-word partitions, not
+by conditioning on a seed singleton of possibly zero probability. On the
+infinite fiber the marker arrives almost surely for each seed route: the
+conditional cylinder tails are bounded by the larger of the two even tails,
+which tends to zero for every $q<1$. Dominated convergence and Tonelli give
+almost-sure decision after integration. The waiting mean is at least
+$K_\infty$ by PG27.17, with all waiting means infinite if $I_\mu=\infty$.
+
+Use the deterministic joint route of Theorem 3.2 on each finite horizon fiber,
+and the route of Theorem 4.1 on the infinite fiber. At a marker decode exactly;
+on a finite zero leaf compare the two already integrated root masses and use
+MAP, with either fixed choice on a tie. A countable measurable partition of the
+seed gives measurable finite-history sections for this one controller. Tonelli
+and source-seed independence give the two identities and inequalities. The
+same underlying $Q,X_0$, and two actual arms may be used for both executions;
+expected domination is claimed, not a pathwise paid-count ordering. No source
+copy or new seed draw is used. $\square$
+
+**Corollary 4.3 (exact selector integrability test).** For a joint replacement,
+finite paid mean is equivalent to
+$$
+\sum_{h<\infty}\nu(H=h)K_h<\infty,\qquad
+\nu(H=\infty)=0\ \text{or}\ I_\mu<\infty.
+$$
+For a general original policy put $\beta_m=\nu(H>2m)$,
+$\gamma_m=\nu(H>2m+1)$, and let $d_m(u)$ indicate odd/odd replay at $2m$
+on $\{H>2m\}$. Its exact cost is
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+C={}&\nu(H>0)+\sum_{m\ge0}\gamma_m(bM_m+aM_{m+1})\\
+&+\sum_{m\ge1}\left[\beta_mM_m+
+ v_m\int_{\{H>2m\}}d_m(u)\,\nu(du)\right].
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+Each bracket is nonnegative; the signed corrections are absolutely summable.
+Hence it is finite exactly when the nonnegative baseline series obtained by
+omitting the $v_m$ terms is finite. In particular, $I_\mu=\infty$ and
+$\nu(H=\infty)=0$ alone do not ensure finite mean.
+
+**Proof.** The first claim is integration of $K_H$. For the second, sum the
+actual survival events $\{H>t,\tau>t\}$ before query $t+1$, using the original
+seed event and the PG27 cylinder mass at each depth. Absolute summability follows
+from $\sum_m|v_m|<1$, so no divergent baseline can be cancelled. $\square$
+
+## 5. Exact average-budget consequences with the seed retained
+
+**Definition 5.1 (original-seed feasible weights).** Give $S$ the sigma algebra
+of all subsets and let
+$$
+\mathsf P_\nu=\{(\nu(H=h))_{h\in S}:H:U\to S\text{ measurable}\}.
+$$
+For $p\in\mathsf P_\nu$ write
+$$
+C(p)=\sum_{h<\infty}p_hK_h+p_\infty K_\infty,\qquad
+E(p)=\sum_{h<\infty}p_hR_h^*.
+$$
+For $B\in[0,\infty)$ let $F_\nu(B)$ be the infimum of actual error over all
+lawful almost-sure-decision controllers with actual mean at most $B$.
+
+**Theorem 5.2 (exact reduction, positivity, and zero error).** For every original
+seed law and every finite budget,
+$$
+\boxed{F_\nu(B)=\inf\{E(p):p\in\mathsf P_\nu,\ C(p)\le B\}.}
+$$
+An attained minimizing selector yields an optimal original-source controller.
+Conversely an optimal original-source controller yields a minimizing selector
+by Theorem 4.2. This equivalence distinguishes an infimum from an attained
+minimum without changing the seed domain.
+
+For every finite integer $L$ with $K_{L+1}>B$,
+$$
+F_\nu(B)\ge R_L^*\left(1-\frac{B}{K_{L+1}}\right)>0.
+$$
+Consequently finite-budget zero error, and also zero infimum error, occur
+exactly when $I_\mu<\infty$ and $B\ge K_\infty$. In that case the constant
+selector $H=\infty$ attains zero for every original seed law. When
+$I_\mu=\infty$, every finite budget has strictly positive infimum risk;
+arbitrarily small error remains attainable with sufficiently large finite
+budgets by constant finite horizons.
+
+**Proof.** Every $p$ in the displayed set has an original-seed realization by
+definition and Theorem 4.2, giving one inequality; every admissible policy has
+a dominating such selector, giving the other. The same argument proves the
+attainment equivalence. Because $K_h$ increases, $C(p)\le B$ implies
+$p(H\ge L+1)\le B/K_{L+1}$. The cap risks are nonincreasing and positive
+at every finite depth, so the remaining mass contributes at least $R_L^*$
+per unit, proving the bound. If $B<K_\infty$, the limit in Theorem 4.1 gives
+such an $L$. Zero error also forces $H=\infty$ almost surely since
+$R_h^*>0$ for each finite $h$, and its least mean is $K_\infty$. The infinite
+route and the finite-horizon limit prove the remaining assertions. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 5.3 (realizable randomization and two horizons).** If the original
+seed probability space is nonatomic, then $\mathsf P_\nu$ is the full set of
+probability vectors on $S$. For every finite $B$ its infimum in Theorem 5.2 is
+attained, and some optimum uses at most two horizons. The two horizons need not
+be neighbors. More generally any proposed two-horizon weight $\theta$ is
+lawful precisely when the original seed has a measurable event of mass
+$\theta$ (unless the two horizons coincide). For a purely atomic seed with
+atom masses $(c_i)$, its exact class is
+$$
+p_h=\sum_{i:f(i)=h}c_i
+$$
+for assignments $f$ of its atoms to horizons. A seed with atoms and a nonatomic
+remainder of mass $c$ realizes exactly such atomic assignments plus an arbitrary
+nonnegative vector of total mass $c$.
+
+**Proof.** We first justify the measure-splitting fact used here. In a finite
+nonatomic measure space every positive set has a positive subset of measure
+at most any prescribed $\epsilon>0$: repeatedly split it into two positive
+parts and follow the smaller part until its mass is small enough. To carve a
+subset of prescribed mass $t$, successively choose a subset of the remaining
+set with mass at most the current deficit and greater than half the supremum
+of the available masses with that bound; stop if the deficit is zero. The
+increasing union has mass at most $t$. If a positive deficit remained, the
+small-subset property applied to the residual of this union would give a fixed
+positive admissible mass at every earlier step, contradicting the increments
+tending to zero. Thus the union has mass $t$. Repeated carving gives every
+countable mass partition; the leftover is null. On an atom a countable-valued
+measurable map is almost surely constant, since its countable fibers partition
+the atom. These facts prove all the seed-feasibility statements, including
+the mixed case. They supply mathematical existence, not effective exact-real
+synthesis.
+
+For completeness, attainment follows directly by compactifying the horizon
+indices. Take a minimizing sequence of probability vectors with cost at most
+$B$. A diagonal subsequence has limits $p_h$ for every finite $h$; put
+$p_\infty=1-\sum_{h<\infty}p_h\ge0$. For each fixed $L$, the bounded
+truncated cost $\min(K_h,K_L)$ is constant for $h\ge L$, including infinity,
+so its expectation depends continuously on finitely many coordinates. Its
+limiting expectation is at most $B$. Monotone convergence as $L\to\infty$
+gives $C(p)\le B$, including the case $K_\infty=\infty$. Risk expectations
+converge too: retain finitely many coordinates and bound the remaining
+contribution by $R_L^*\to0$. Thus $p$ attains the infimum. The original
+nonatomic seed realizes this entire vector by the partition construction.
+This argument retains escaped mass at infinity and charges its actual cost.
+
+At budget zero only horizon zero is feasible. If $B\ge K_\infty<\infty$,
+the infinite horizon is optimal. In the remaining case $0<B<K_\infty$, write
+$F(B)$ for this unrestricted attained value. Mixtures make $F$ convex and it
+is nonincreasing. It is strictly decreasing below $K_\infty$: an optimizer
+has positive error by Theorem 5.2, and mixing in a sufficiently small mass at
+a finite horizon with smaller risk strictly improves it at any larger budget.
+In particular an optimizer at $B$ uses mean exactly $B$. A supporting slope
+$s<0$ exists at this interior budget: convexity orders all left secant slopes
+below all right secant slopes, and any slope between their one-sided limits
+supports the graph; local boundedness makes those limits finite. A zero slope
+would force a constant later segment,
+contradicting strict decrease. Put $\lambda=-s>0$. For every horizon of finite
+cost, the supporting inequality implies
+$$
+R_h^*+\lambda K_h\ge F(B)+\lambda B.
+$$
+The same holds at infinity when it has finite cost. Averaging over an optimal
+measure gives equality, so every horizon in its positive support lies on this
+line. If the support contains a horizon of cost $B$, that single horizon is
+optimal. Otherwise its mean $B$ supplies one supported cost below $B$ and one
+above $B$. Their unique Bernoulli mixture of mean $B$ lies on the same line
+and has risk $F(B)$. Its weight is realizable by the original nonatomic seed.
+For example, take $a=b=1/2$, $\mu=\delta_{1/2}$, and $B=2$. Then
+$$
+(K_2,K_3,K_4)=(7/4,9/4,21/8),\qquad
+(R_2^*,R_3^*,R_4^*)=(1/8,1/8,1/16).
+$$
+The original nonatomic seed can put weight $2/7$ at horizon $4$ and $5/7$ at
+horizon $2$, giving cost $2$ and risk $3/28<1/8$. Interpolation of the two
+adjacent horizons $2,3$ whose costs bracket $2$ has risk $1/8$ and is therefore
+suboptimal. For a
+restricted atomic seed these convex combinations cannot replace its own
+feasibility class, and only the infimum/attainment equivalence of Theorem 5.2
+is being asserted. $\square$
+
+## 6. Sources and limits
+
+The shared-$Q$ posterior, parity replay, and all-marker stopping identities
+are the PG27.1--27.3 and PG27.14--27.19 results in [Process Geometry](RECURSIVE_RELATIONAL_OBSERVATION_PROCESS_GEOMETRY.md).
+The terminal risks and their lawful cap attainers are supplied by [Finite-query
+spatial recovery](RECURSIVE_RELATIONAL_OBSERVATION_FINITE_QUERY_SPATIAL_RECOVERY.md),
+at immutable supplier revision `5234b4de599f6ed513dab4bbe2f65b5c743f0115`, especially §§2--4.
+The stopping-tail interface is also exposed by
+`D5/S3/Observer/ProbabilisticClosure/AdaptiveMarkerStoppingTails.lean` and
+its Blueprint source. The mixed-mean suppliers in that directory are
+BeneficialMarkerDeflection.lean and SingleDeflectionOptimalController.lean.
+The cylinder and parity helpers, including private statements, in
+FiniteAtomLinearRealization.lean and RawFiniteAtomLinearRealization.lean
+supply the same fixed-source interfaces. These are repo-derived suppliers;
+this companion adds
+the common finite-horizon cost/risk attainment and the original-seed
+replacement statement.
+
+Visible-seed averaging itself is supplied by [Wave-particle events, Theorem
+393.3](RECURSIVE_RELATIONAL_OBSERVATION_WAVE_PARTICLE_EVENTS.md); it is used
+only for prior-average cost and risk, with the seed visible and independent.
+Measure splitting, diagonal compactness of probability vectors with a retained
+infinite endpoint, and supporting lines of convex functions are used only as
+intermediate classical facts, with the needed arguments given in Proposition
+5.3. They do not supply the source-specific common realization in Theorems
+3.2 and 4.2. The new bridge and its mean-budget consequences are repo-derived
+ordinary conditional mathematics.
+
+Paid fresh-edge count excludes computation, seed bits, record/output/storage,
+effective prior precision, and physical time. Fixed-prior measurable control
+does not provide effective synthesis from arbitrary approximate descriptions
+of $\mu$, its moments, or exact Bernoulli weights. The labels recovered are
+only those of the actual exposed interval; neither the unacquired law table
+nor $Q$ is recovered. The frontier describes the best feasible tradeoff;
+an arbitrary controller can use a worse decoder at the same cost. These
+results assert no physical realization, whole-literature novelty, total-memory
+optimum, or complete four-expression recovery.

+**Proposition 5.1 (The normalized cancellation boundary).** Specialize Definition 1.2 to $r=3$, write the substitution as $\varphi_3$, and let $u_7=\varphi_3^\omega(0)$. Define the nonerasing morphism $\eta_3:\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\}^*\to\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ by
+
+$$
+\eta_3(0)=0,\quad \eta_3(1)=1,\quad \eta_3(2)=2,\quad \eta_3(3)=3,\quad
+\eta_3(4)=11,\quad \eta_3(5)=1221,\quad \eta_3(6)=12133121.
+$$
+
+For its length row $h=(1,1,1,1,2,4,8)$ and the normalized eigenvector $v_\beta$ of Definition 1.3, one has $h v_\beta=0$. Nevertheless, for the infinite image $w_3=\eta_3(u_7)$ the factor
+
+$$
+z=w_3[60,72)=301020101213
+$$
+
+has exactly $11$ distinct palindromic factors, including the empty word. Since $|z|=12$, it is not rich and its palindromic defect is $2$.
+
+**Proof.** For the cancellation, the chosen row and the normalization in Definition 1.3 give
+
+$$
+h v_\beta=(\beta-2)(\beta^5+\beta^4+\beta^3+\beta^2+2\beta+4)+8.
+$$
+
+The polynomial identity
+
+$$
+(x-2)(x^2+x^3+x^4+x^5+2x+4)+8
+=x^3(x^3-x^2-x-1)
+$$
+
+holds identically. The number $\beta$ is the positive root of $x^3-x^2-x-1$, so the displayed scalar is zero. This is the normalized relation $h v_\beta=0$, rather than a statement about an unnormalized eigenvector.
+
+It remains to locate the stated factor in the actual infinite word. Put $T_n=\varphi_3^n(0)$ and let $\nu_2(q)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in a positive integer $q$. For $0\le n\le6$,
+
+$$
+|T_n|=2^n,\qquad T_n[j]=\nu_2(j+1)\quad(0\le j<2^n).
+$$
+
+The assertion is immediate for $n=0$. If $n<6$, every letter occurring in $T_n$ is at most $n$, so only the length-two rules $\varphi_3(i)=0(i+1)$ are used. Thus
+
+$$
+T_{n+1}[2j]=0=\nu_2(2j+1),\qquad
+T_{n+1}[2j+1]=T_n[j]+1=\nu_2(2j+2),
+$$
+
+which proves the induction through $T_6$. The letter $6$ first occurs at $T_6[63]$; the exceptional rule $\varphi_3(6)=066$ is therefore not used in constructing $T_6$.
+
+The positions $55$ through $63$ of $T_6$ correspond to the integers $56$ through $64$, hence
+
+$$
+T_6[55,64)=(3,0,1,0,2,0,1,0,6).
+$$
+
+Before position $55$, a letter greater than $3$ occurs exactly when $j+1$ is a multiple of $16$. The only such positions are $15,31,47$, with letters $4,5,4$. Since the images of $4,5,4$ have lengths $2,4,2$ and every other image in $T_6[0,55)$ has length one,
+
+$$
+|\eta_3(T_6[0,55))|=55+(2-1)+(4-1)+(2-1)=60.
+$$
+
+The next eight source letters have single-letter images, so
+
+$$
+\eta_3(T_6[55,63))=30102010,
+$$
+
+while $\eta_3(6)$ begins with $1213$. Consequently
+
+$$
+\eta_3(T_6)[60,72)=301020101213.
+$$
+
+The whole prefix has length
+
+$$
+|\eta_3(T_6)|=64+(2-1)+(4-1)+(2-1)+(8-1)=76,
+$$
+
+so both endpoints of this interval lie inside $\eta_3(T_6)$. Since $T_{n+1}=T_n\varphi_3^n(1)$ is a proper prefix extension and $\eta_3$ is nonerasing, these prefixes embed compatibly in $w_3=\eta_3(u_7)$; the displayed finite word is therefore the actual factor $w_3[60,72)$.
+
+For the palindrome count, the adjacent letters of $z$ are all different, so no nonempty even-length palindrome occurs. The largest odd radii at centers $0,1,\ldots,11$ are
+
+$$
+(0,0,1,0,3,0,1,1,0,1,0,0).
+$$
+
+Every odd palindrome is obtained by choosing a center and a radius no larger than the corresponding entry. Centers $2$ and $6$ give $010$; center $4$ gives $020$, $10201$, and $0102010$; center $7$ gives $101$; and center $9$ gives $121$. Radius zero gives the four single letters. Thus the complete set of distinct palindromic factors is
+
+$$

+$$
+

+$$
+v_j=\frac{C_jp_j(1-p_j)}{B^2},\quad
+ e_j=\frac{\mu_j-C_jp_j}{B},\quad
+V=\sum_jv_j,\quad
+E(m)=\sum_j((m_j-\mu_j)/B)^2,\quad
+T_x(m)=\frac{E(m)-V}{\sqrt\delta}.
+\tag{121.8}
+$$
+
+空组补零。给定 $\sigma>0$，令
+
+$$
+\lambda_y(m)=\frac{(T_x(m)-y)^2}{2\sigma^2},\quad
+P_x^y(m)=\frac{P_x(m)e^{-\lambda_y(m)}}
+ {\sum_uP_x(u)e^{-\lambda_y(u)}},\quad
+C3_x(y)=\mathbb E_{P_x^y}
+ \left[-\log P_x^y-\mathbb E_{P_x^y}(-\log P_x^y)\right]^3.
+\tag{121.9}
+$$
+
+**定义 121.3（完整有限鞍点）。** 对 $\alpha>0$，取
+
+$$
+K_\alpha(t)=-\frac12\sum_j\log(1-2tv_j/\alpha)
+ +\sum_j\frac{te_j^2}{1-2tv_j/\alpha}
+ +\frac{\delta\sigma^2t^2}{2\alpha},\qquad
+K_\alpha'(t_\alpha)=V,\qquad W_\alpha=K_\alpha''(t_\alpha).
+\tag{121.10}
+$$
+
+若 $v_*:=\max_jv_j>0$，实定义域为 $t<\alpha/(2v_*)$；全零时为 $\mathbb R$。
+正噪声使 $K''>0$，且 $K'$ 在定义域两端分别趋于负、正无穷，故根唯一。
+全部 $\alpha$ 导数固定实际纤维、所有整数、组集合、$p_j,\mu_j,V$ 和噪声。
+系数中的求和始终包含全部原组。
+
+## 122. 第三信息累积量的响应
+
+**定理 122.1（原模型的紧输出第三累积量响应）。** 对定义 121.1 的每个固定 $\beta$，
+每个确定正数序列 $\sigma_n$ 满足
+
+$$
+L_n:=\log(1/\sigma_n)\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
+\limsup_n L_n/Q_n^3<c_q/2,
+\tag{122.1}
+$$
+
+以及每个 $R,\varepsilon>0$，均有
+
+$$
+\max_{\mathcal E\in\{\mathrm{pair},\mathrm{path}\}}
+\sup_{|S|=q_n}\mathbb P_S^{\mathcal E}\left\{
+\sup_{|y|\le R}\left|
+C3_x(y)-C3_x(0)-\sqrt{\delta_n}\,t_1'''y
+-\frac{\delta_n}{2}
+ \left.\partial_\alpha^3\frac1{W_\alpha}\right|_{\alpha=1}y^2
+\right|>\varepsilon\right\}\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{122.2}
+$$
+
+证明分解于以下各节，最后在第 127 节汇合。
+
+**定义 122.2（有限配分差）。** 置
+
+$$
+\Xi_\alpha(y)=
+ \log\frac{\sum_mP_x(m)^\alpha e^{-\alpha\lambda_y(m)}}
+ {\sum_mP_x(m)^\alpha e^{-\alpha\lambda_0(m)}}.
+\tag{122.3}
+$$
+
+若 $f_\alpha$ 为 $P_x^\alpha/\sum P_x^\alpha$ 下的 $T_x$
+加独立 $N(0,\sigma^2/\alpha)$ 的密度，则
+$\Xi_\alpha(y)=\log[f_\alpha(y)/f_\alpha(0)]$。
+每个有限纤维的精确恒等式为
+
+$$
+\log\sum_m(P_x^y(m))^\alpha-
+\log\sum_m(P_x^0(m))^\alpha
+=\Xi_\alpha(y)-\alpha\Xi_1(y),
+$$
+
+$$
+C3_x(y)-C3_x(0)=-\left.\partial_\alpha^3\Xi_\alpha(y)\right|_{1}.
+\tag{122.4}
+$$
+
+第一式由代入归一化质量得到；第三次对数配分导数是 $\log P_x^y$ 的第三中心矩，
+而惊讶多一个负号，故得第二式。
+
+## 123. 同一实际纤维的三次解析控制
+
+**约定 123.1（原纤维界与范数）。** 以下均在谱边界第 68、69、70、117、119 节的共同实际好事件上工作。
+固定其紧性常数后，原式 (117.7)–(117.10)、(119.8)–(119.10) 给
+
+$$
+m_Q:=\#\{j:C_j>0\}\le CQ^2=C\delta^{-4},\quad
+\log q=c_qQ^3+O(1),\quad N_J:=\sum_jC_j\le CB^2,
+$$
+
+$$
+c\le V\le C,\quad c\delta\le v_*\le C\delta,\quad
+c\delta\le\sum_jv_j^2\le C\delta,\quad
+|e_j|\le C\sqrt{v_j}\,e_M,\quad
+\|e\|_2\le Ce_M,\quad e_M\le C(\delta^5+q^{-1/2}),
+$$
+
+$$
+\max_j|p_j-1/2|\le Cq^{-1/2},\quad
+cq\le d_c\le d_a\le q,\quad d_a-d_c=B^2V,
+\quad d_c:=\sum_{i\notin J}p_i(1-p_i),\quad
+ d_a:=\sum_i p_i(1-p_i),
+$$
+
+$$
+|\ell(m)|\le C\delta^5(1+\mathcal D(m)^2),\quad
+\ell(m)\le C\delta^5.
+\tag{123.1}
+$$
+
+整个盒可行。原核心含 $c/\delta$ 个 $v_j\asymp\delta$ 的坐标。
+原式 (117.15)–(117.16) 还给
+$-C\|e\|^2\le s_\alpha:=2v_*t_\alpha/\alpha\le s_+<1$，$1\le\alpha\le2$。
+原式 (117.24)、(117.26)、(117.33) 的每个固定阶矩均可使用；这些是同一输出条件下的矩，
+并不由条件化前的负相关推断。
+
+对函数 $F(\alpha,y)$ 记
+$\|F\|_{3,R}=\sup_{1\le\alpha\le2,\,|y|\le R}\sum_{k=0}^3|\partial_\alpha^kF|$。
+常数可依赖固定振幅、$\beta,R$ 及上述好事件常数。
+$\operatorname{poly}(Q)$ 表示次数固定的多项式上界。
+好事件可穷尽，使其补集概率对两个实验和所有确定大小 $q$ 的支持一致趋零。
+
+**引理 123.2（直接的三次有限鞍点估计）。** 固定 $l<c_q/2$，使最终 $L\le lQ^3$。
+选取 $\chi_0>0$，满足 $2\chi_0<c_q-l$，并置
+$H=\{j:C_j\ge e^{\chi_0Q^3}\}$。
+只在本证明中，以 $K_H$ 删除 $H^c$ 的坐标项而保留原噪声项，且仍在完整根 $t_\alpha$ 处置
+
+$$
+\epsilon_H=V-K_H'(t_\alpha),\quad W_H=K_H''(t_\alpha),\quad
+D_j=1-s_\alpha v_j/v_*,\quad
+w_j=v_j/(\alpha D_j),\quad m_j=-e_j/D_j.
+\tag{123.2}
+$$
+
+有
+
+$$
+|s_\alpha^{(k)}|\le C,\quad
+|w_j^{(k)}|\le Cw_j,\quad |m_j^{(k)}|\le C|e_j|,\quad
+|W_\alpha^{(k)}|+|W_H^{(k)}|\le C\delta\quad(1\le k\le3),
+$$
+
+$$
+W_\alpha\asymp W_H\asymp\delta,\quad
+\sum_{k=0}^3\bigl(|\epsilon_H^{(k)}|
+  +|(W_\alpha-W_H)^{(k)}|\bigr)
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-b_0Q^3}
+\tag{123.3}
+$$
+
+其中 $b_0>0$。令 $X_j$ 独立且分布为 $N(-e_j,v_j/\alpha)$，$j\in H$，
+$g_\alpha$ 为 $(\sum_HX_j^2-V)/\sqrt\delta+N(0,\sigma^2/\alpha)$ 的密度，则
+
+$$
+\left\|\log\frac{g_\alpha(y)}{g_\alpha(0)}
+ +\sqrt\delta\,t_\alpha y+\frac{\delta y^2}{2W_\alpha}\right\|_{3,R}\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{123.4}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 写 $r_j=v_j/v_*$。完整根方程为
+
+$$
+G(s,\alpha):=\alpha^{-1}\sum_j\frac{v_j}{1-sr_j}
+ +\sum_j\frac{e_j^2}{(1-sr_j)^2}
+ +\frac{\delta\sigma^2s}{2v_*}-V=0.
+\tag{123.5}
+$$
+
+在原有根区间上 $G_s\ge c$，所有三阶及以下混合偏导有界。
+逐次微分 $G(s_\alpha,\alpha)=0$，先得 $G_ss'+G_\alpha=0$，再得
+
+$$
+G_ss''+G_{ss}(s')^2+2G_{s\alpha}s'+G_{\alpha\alpha}=0,
+$$
+
+$$
+G_ss'''+3(G_{ss}s'+G_{s\alpha})s''
+ +G_{sss}(s')^3+3G_{ss\alpha}(s')^2
+ +3G_{s\alpha\alpha}s'+G_{\alpha\alpha\alpha}=0.
+\tag{123.6}
+$$
+
+因此 $s',s'',s'''$ 均有界。商法则给 $w,m$ 的三阶界。再由
+
+$$
+W_\alpha=2\sum_jw_j^2+4\sum_jw_jm_j^2+\delta\sigma^2/\alpha
+\tag{123.7}
+$$
+
+得 $W$ 的界；$\sum w_jm_j^2\le C v_*\|e\|^2$。
+原低组界为
+
+$$
+\sum_{H^c}v_j\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-(c_q-\chi_0)Q^3},\qquad
+\sum_{H^c}e_j^2\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-(c_q-2\chi_0)Q^3}.
+\tag{123.8}
+$$
+
+每个删除项的前三次全导数仍带 $v_j$ 或 $e_j^2$，且
+$|t_\alpha^{(k)}|\le C/\delta$，$0\le k\le3$，这证明差量界。
+
+完整鞍点倾斜下，高组均值、方差正是 $m_j,w_j$。
+把高组能量与原能量噪声中心化并以 $\sqrt{W_H}$ 标准化，其精确特征函数为
+
+$$
+\psi_\alpha(\xi)=e^{-\beta_G^2\xi^2/2}
+\prod_{j\in H}e^{-i\xi a_j}(1-2i\xi a_j)^{-1/2}
+ \exp\left[-\frac{\beta_j^2\xi^2}{2(1-2i\xi a_j)}\right],
+$$
+
+$$
+a_j=w_j/\sqrt{W_H},\quad
+\beta_j=2m_j\sqrt{w_j}/\sqrt{W_H},\quad
+\beta_G=\sqrt{\delta\sigma^2/\alpha}/\sqrt{W_H}.
+\tag{123.9}
+$$
+
+其方差恰为一。前三次系数导数分别由 $Ca_j,C|\beta_j|,C|\beta_G|$ 控制，
+$\max a_j\le C\sqrt\delta$，核心块有 $c/\delta$ 项满足 $a_j^2\asymp\delta$。
+故
+
+$$
+|\psi_\alpha(\xi)|\le E_Q(\xi):=(1+c\delta\xi^2)^{-c'/\delta}.
+\tag{123.10}
+$$
+
+对中心对数因子逐次求导，利用
+$|\xi a_j|/|1-2i\xi a_j|\le1/2$，每个一至三阶导数均由 $C\xi^2a_j^2$ 控制。
+非中心因子相应由 $C\xi^2\beta_j^2$ 控制，噪声由 $C\xi^2\beta_G^2$ 控制。
+对指数再用三次乘法法则，得到
+
+$$
+|\partial_\alpha^k\psi_\alpha(\xi)|
+ \le C_k(1+|\xi|^{2k})E_Q(\xi),\quad 0\le k\le3.
+\tag{123.11}
+$$
+
+包络的所有固定多项式矩一致可积，尾部一致消失。
+在 $|\xi|\le\delta^{-1/2}$ 用 Gaussian 上界；在外侧置
+$u=\sqrt\delta|\xi|$，积分指数为 $-c'/\delta$ 的幂即可。
+固定频率紧集上，直接展开式 (123.9) 及其前三次导数给
+
+$$
+\log\psi_\alpha(\xi)=-\xi^2/2+O(\sqrt\delta|\xi|^3),\quad
+\partial_\alpha^k\log\psi_\alpha(\xi)
+ =O(\sqrt\delta|\xi|^3),\quad1\le k\le3.
+\tag{123.12}
+$$
+
+二次项的各阶导数为零来自恒等方差一；余项用 $\max a_j\le C\sqrt\delta$
+和平方系数和有界逐项求导。这是对精确变换的估计。
+若 $q_\alpha$ 为标准化密度，Fourier 反演给
+
+$$
+\partial_z^h q_\alpha\to\varphi^{(h)}\quad(0\le h\le3),\qquad
+\partial_\alpha^k\partial_z^h q_\alpha\to0
+ \quad(k\ge1,\ k+h\le3),
+\tag{123.13}
+$$
+
+对 $\alpha\in[1,2],z\in\mathbb R$ 一致。
+可微性由同一可积包络证明。
+$z_y=(\sqrt\delta y+\epsilon_H)/\sqrt{W_H}$ 及前三次导数在紧输出上一致有界，
+故 $q_\alpha(z_y)\ge c_R>0$，三次链式法则给
+
+$$
+\log\frac{q_\alpha(z_y)}{q_\alpha(z_0)}
+ =-\frac{z_y^2-z_0^2}{2}+o_{C^3}(1).
+\tag{123.14}
+$$
+
+精确撤销倾斜为
+
+$$
+g_\alpha(y)=\frac{\sqrt\delta}{\sqrt{W_H}}
+ e^{K_H(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha(V+\sqrt\delta y)}q_\alpha(z_y).
+\tag{123.15}
+$$
+
+比值中速率与前因子消去；式 (123.3) 支付 $\epsilon_H$ 和 $W_H-W_\alpha$ 的全部三次导数，
+得到 (123.4)。∎
+
+## 124. 完整固定总数选择的全盒二次近似
+
+**引理 124.1（同一补集的二次选择势）。** 在约定 123.1 的纤维上置
+
+$$
+c_0=\frac12\log(d_a/d_c),\qquad
+\eta=\frac{B^2}{2d_c},\qquad
+\ell_2(m)=c_0-\eta\mathcal D(m)^2.
+\tag{124.1}
+$$
+
+则 $0\le c_0\le C\delta^5$，$0<\eta\le C\delta^5$，并在整个可行盒上有
+
+$$
+|\ell(m)-\ell_2(m)|\le Cq^{-1/2}(1+|\mathcal D(m)|^3).
+\tag{124.2}
+$$
+
+令 $q_j$ 为原二项组质量，$S_j=-\log(q_j/\max q_j)$，$S_Q=\sum_jS_j$，
+$A_y=S_Q+\lambda_y$，并定义三个有限配分函数
+
+$$
+J_P(\alpha,y)=\sum_m e^{-\alpha(A_y(m)-\ell(m))},\quad
+J_2(\alpha,y)=\sum_m e^{-\alpha(A_y(m)-\ell_2(m))},\quad
+J_0(\alpha,y)=\sum_m e^{-\alpha A_y(m)}.
+\tag{124.3}
+$$
+
+则对某个 $b_1>0$，
+
+$$
+\left\|\log\frac{J_P}{J_2}\right\|_{3,R}
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-b_1Q^3}.
+\tag{124.4}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 对补集 Bernoulli 和写
+$H(t)=\sum_{i\notin J}\log(1-p_i+p_ie^t)$，$m_c=H'(0)$。
+全局校准给 $m_c=q-\sum_j C_jp_j$，故目标整数 $q-\sum_jm_j=m_c-D(m)$。
+logistic 方差满足 $e^{-|t|}d_c\le H''(t)\le e^{|t|}d_c$。
+因为 $|D|\le N_J\le Cq\delta^5$，唯一实倾斜根 $u$ 满足
+$H'(u)=m_c-D$，且 $|u|\le C|D|/q\le C\delta^5$。
+在该区间所有固定阶 $H^{(k)}$，$k\ge2$，均由 $C_kq$ 控制。
+Taylor 展开及均值方程给
+
+$$
+u=-D/d_c+O(D^2/q^2),\quad
+I:=u(m_c-D)-H(u)=D^2/(2d_c)+O(|D|^3/q^2),\quad
+|\log(H''(u)/d_c)|\le C|D|/q.
+\tag{124.5}
+$$
+
+这里 $H(0)=0$。这些界在完整盒上一致，允许其右侧在极端元组处很大。
+
+所需经典中心局部估计对任意 Bernoulli 数组，只要求方差 $d\to\infty$ 和均值为整数：
+中心质量为 $(2\pi d)^{-1/2}(1+O(d^{-1/2}))$，常数对数组一致。
+为说明其在本处的范围，中心特征乘积满足
+$|\Phi(t)|\le e^{-2d\sin^2(t/2)}$，$|t|\le\pi$。
+在 $t=\xi/\sqrt d$、$|\xi|\le d^{1/12}$ 上，
+$\log\Phi(t)=-\xi^2/2+O(|\xi|^3/\sqrt d)$；
+三阶对数导数由 $Cd$ 控制，因为单项的相应界为 $Cp_i(1-p_i)$。
+积分与 Gaussian 积分之差至多 $C/\sqrt d$；余下标准化频率由
+$e^{-c\xi^2}$ 支付。反演再乘 $d^{-1/2}$ 就得上述相对估计。
+相同证明适用于倾斜后的参数，其方差 $H''(u)\asymp q$。
+这是 Bernoulli 局部展开的经典步骤，参见 Boistard–Lopuhaä–Ruiz-Gazen，
+*Approximation of rejective sampling inclusion probabilities and application to high order correlations*，
+[arXiv:1207.5654v1](https://arxiv.org/html/1207.5654v1)，式 (2.1)、(2.5) 及 §4.1。
+该引用中的固定阶包含概率展开不作为输出条件下的相关界。
+
+在补集的倾斜均值及全体的原整数均值处分别使用该估计，撤销补集倾斜，得到
+
+$$
+\ell=c_0-\frac{D^2}{2d_c}
+ +O\left(q^{-1/2}+|D|/q+|D|^3/q^2\right).
+\tag{124.6}
+$$
+
+代入 $D=B\mathcal D$、$B^2/q=\delta^5$ 即得 (124.2)。
+$d_a-d_c=B^2V$ 给 $c_0,\eta$ 的界。
+没有删去任何总偏差元组。
+
+为证明三次配分比较，令 $\mu_{\alpha,y}(m)=e^{-\alpha A_y(m)}/J_0(\alpha,y)$。
+原式 (117.33) 对每个固定 $k$ 给
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_\mu|\mathcal D|^{2k}\le C_k,\quad
+\mathbb E_\mu S_Q^k\le C_k(1+m_Q)^k,\quad
+\mathbb E_\mu\lambda_y^k\le C_k\delta^{-k}.
+\tag{124.7}
+$$
+
+因此所有固定混合矩均为 $\operatorname{poly}(Q)$，由 Hölder 不等式可见。
+$\ell,\ell_2\le C\delta^5$，且两者绝对值均由 $C\delta^5(1+\mathcal D^2)$ 控制。
+若 $a,b\le C\delta^5$，对 $0\le k\le3$ 的函数
+$e^{\alpha a}[-(A-a)]^k$ 用均值定理，有
+
+$$
+\left|e^{\alpha a}(A-a)^k-e^{\alpha b}(A-b)^k\right|
+ \le C_k|a-b|(1+|A|^k+|a|^k+|b|^k).
+\tag{124.8}
+$$
+
+区间内指数有统一上界。取 $a=\ell,b=\ell_2,A=A_y$，
+利用 (124.2)、(124.7) 并逐项求导原有限和，得
+
+$$
+|\partial_\alpha^kJ_P-\partial_\alpha^kJ_2|/J_0
+ \le q^{-1/2}\operatorname{poly}(Q),\qquad0\le k\le3.
+\tag{124.9}
+$$
+
+又 $J_2/J_0=e^{\alpha c_0}\mathbb E_\mu e^{-\alpha\eta\mathcal D^2}
+\ge1-C\eta\mathbb E_\mu\mathcal D^2\ge1/2$，
+$|\partial_\alpha^kJ_2|/J_0\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)$。
+使用对数的前三次导数公式并代入 (124.9)，得到 (124.4)。
+这一估计在同一输出条件律内完成；它没有以未条件化概率尾界除以稀有输出概率。∎
+
+## 125. 高组条件积分中的秩一选择
+
+**引理 125.1（三次可微的条件秩一修正）。** 在引理 123.2 的高组 Gaussian 实现中置
+
+$$
+\mathcal D_G=\sum_{j\in H}(X_j+e_j),\qquad
+\lambda_y^G=\frac{((\sum_HX_j^2-V)/\sqrt\delta-y)^2}{2\sigma^2},
+\quad S_G=\frac12\sum_{j\in H}(X_j+e_j)^2/v_j.
+$$
+
+以 Lebesgue 测度定义
+
+$$
+\mathcal J_\eta(\alpha,y)=
+ \int_{\mathbb R^H}e^{-\alpha(S_G+\lambda_y^G+\eta\mathcal D_G^2)}\,dX,
+\qquad \mathcal J_0=\mathcal J_\eta\big|_{\eta=0}.
+\tag{125.1}
+$$
+
+取固定于纤维的 $\eta$ 如 (124.1)，则
+
+$$
+\left\|\log\frac{\mathcal J_\eta}{\mathcal J_0}\right\|_{3,R}
+ \le C\eta\le C\delta^5.
+\tag{125.2}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 把原输出权重写成高能量加独立能量噪声
+$N(0,\delta\sigma^2/\alpha)$ 等于 $h_y=V+\sqrt\delta y$。
+在同一个完整 $t_\alpha$ 处倾斜不改变该条件分布。
+在其标准化 Fourier 积分中置 $u=\xi/\sqrt{W_H}$。
+频率 $u$ 下，高坐标的复协方差、均值为
+
+$$
+\widehat w_j=\frac{w_j}{1-2iu w_j},\qquad
+\widehat m_j=\frac{m_j}{1-2iu w_j}.
+\tag{125.3}
+$$
+
+总偏差 $\mathcal D_G$ 的复均值、协方差分别为
+
+$$
+M_\alpha(\xi)=\sum_{j\in H}(\widehat m_j+e_j),\qquad
+S_\alpha(\xi)=\sum_{j\in H}\widehat w_j.
+\tag{125.4}
+$$
+
+注意这里 $S_\alpha(\xi)$ 是标量协方差，不是潜在支持。
+$\operatorname{Re}S_\alpha\ge0$。
+对 $0\le k\le3$，式 (123.3) 给 $|u^{(k)}|\le C|u|$。
+反复商法则及 $|u w_j|/|1-2iu w_j|\le1/2$ 给
+
+$$
+|\partial_\alpha^k S_\alpha(\xi)|\le C\sum_Hw_j\le C,\qquad
+|\partial_\alpha^k M_\alpha(\xi)|\le C\sum_H|e_j|
+ \le C\sqrt{m_Q}\|e\|_2\le C\delta^3.
+\tag{125.5}
+$$
+
+$k=0$ 包括原来的 $e_j$。这些界对所有实频率一致。
+
+复 Gaussian 积分给精确插入因子
+
+$$
+\mathcal R_\alpha(\xi)
+ =(1+2\alpha\eta S_\alpha)^{-1/2}
+ \exp\left[-\frac{\alpha\eta M_\alpha^2}
+                   {1+2\alpha\eta S_\alpha}\right].
+\tag{125.6}
+$$
+
+平方根取在 $\eta=0$ 连续等于一的分支。
+这个经典 Gaussian 二次积分可由配方得到：在复均值 $M$、协方差 $S$ 的
+Gaussian 积分中插入 $e^{-a z^2}$，完成平方后，行列式因子为
+$(1+2aS)^{-1/2}$，剩余常数为 $e^{-aM^2/(1+2aS)}$。
+此处原 Fourier 精度的实部正定，$a=\alpha\eta\ge0$，
+且 $\operatorname{Re}(1+2aS_\alpha)\ge1$，所以该积分及连续分支均合法。
+不需要把输出条件后的高坐标声明为独立。
+
+由 (125.5)、分母的实部下界及逐次微分 (125.6)，有
+
+$$
+|\mathcal R_\alpha-1|+
+ \sum_{k=1}^3|\partial_\alpha^k\mathcal R_\alpha|
+ \le C\eta.
+\tag{125.7}
+$$
+
+例如 $|\log\mathcal R_\alpha|\le C\eta(1+|M_\alpha|^2)$；
+其前三次导数也满足相同界，指数乘法法则给 (125.7)。
+
+令 $q_\alpha$ 如引理 123.2。公共撤倾斜因子抵消后，精确比值为
+
+$$
+\frac{\mathcal J_\eta}{\mathcal J_0}
+ =1+\frac{(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}
+ e^{-i\xi z_y}\psi_\alpha(\xi)
+ [\mathcal R_\alpha(\xi)-1],d\xi}{q_\alpha(z_y)}.
+\tag{125.8}
+$$
+
+$z_y$ 的前三次导数有界，$q_\alpha(z_y)\ge c_R$，其前三次导数也有界。
+对分子求导三次，(123.11)、(125.7) 将每项由
+$C\eta(1+|\xi|^9)E_Q(\xi)$ 控制，其积分为 $O(\eta)$。
+故比值与一之差及前三次导数均为 $O(\eta)$；再次取对数给 (125.2)。
+这里直接控制的是同一条件积分的三次导数，维数 $m_Q$ 没有以未中心化三阶惊讶矩的形式出现。∎
