+## 126. 三次计数回接与稀有分母
+
+**引理 126.1（原多重度的三次计数比较）。** 取
+$Z_L(\alpha)=\sum_{m_{H^c}}e^{-\alpha S_{H^c}(m)}$。
+对 $s\in\{0,\eta\}$，令
+
+$$
+J_s^{\rm count}(\alpha,y)
+ =\sum_m e^{-\alpha(A_y(m)+s\mathcal D(m)^2)},\qquad
+\mathcal C_s(\alpha,y)=B^{|H|}Z_L(\alpha)\mathcal J_s(\alpha,y).
+\tag{126.1}
+$$
+
+则对某个 $b_2>0$，
+
+$$
+\left\|\log\frac{J_s^{\rm count}}{\mathcal C_s}\right\|_{3,R}
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-b_2Q^3}.
+\tag{126.2}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 先固定高组中心盒
+$|m_j-C_jp_j|/\sqrt{C_jp_j(1-p_j)}\le Q^2$。
+在格点对应的 $B^{-1}$ 边长 Gaussian 格元内，原式 (117.27)–(117.29)、(119.41)–(119.43) 给
+
+$$
+|S_H-S_G|\le\epsilon_Q\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-\chi_0Q^3/2},
+$$
+
+$$
+|T_x-T_G|\le\Delta_Q
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)(B^{-1}+B^{-2}e^{2\chi_0Q^3}),\qquad
+\eta_Q:=\Delta_Q/\sigma\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-bQ^3},
+\tag{126.3}
+$$
+
+其中 $b>0$，因为 $l<c_q/2$、$2\chi_0<c_q-l$。
+低组接上任意原可行元组，且
+
+$$
+|\mathcal D-\mathcal D_G|\le d_Q
+ :=m_Q/(2B)+m_Qe^{\chi_0Q^3}/B
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-b'Q^3}.
+\tag{126.4}
+$$
+
+中心格元上 $|\mathcal D_G|\le C Q^2\sum_j\sqrt{v_j}+\sum_j|e_j|
+\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)$，所以
+$|s\mathcal D^2-s\mathcal D_G^2|\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)d_Q$。
+这些是完整低组和完整高组舍入的逐元组界。
+
+令 $U=(T_G-y)/\sigma$。由 (126.3)，
+
+$$
+|\lambda_y-U^2/2|\le\eta_Q|U|+\eta_Q^2/2,
+$$
+
+$$
+|e^{-\alpha\lambda_y}-e^{-\alpha U^2/2}|
+ \le C\eta_Q(1+|U|)e^{-\alpha U^2/2+C\eta_Q|U|}.
+\tag{126.5}
+$$
+
+对每个固定 $k$，
+$|a^k-b^k|\le k|a-b|(|a|+|b|)^{k-1}$。
+因此前三次配分导数的插入势能
+$[-(S_Q+\lambda_y+s\mathcal D^2)]^k$，$0\le k\le3$，
+可逐格元与 $[-(S_G+S_L+U^2/2+s\mathcal D_G^2)]^k$ 比较。
+积分误差由 (126.3)–(126.5) 乘固定混合矩支付。
+低组始终保留原质量及其幂，不作连续近似。
+
+说明这些矩与宽度成本。原式 (117.24)、(117.26) 给所有固定阶
+$\mathcal D_G,S_G,S_L,U$ 的条件矩为 $\operatorname{poly}(Q)$；
+带 $s=\eta$ 的矩分子不超过无修正的分子，分母比由 (125.2) 下界为 $1/2$。
+Young 不等式将 $e^{C\eta_Q|U|}$ 吸收入相对变化 $O(\eta_Q)$ 的稍大噪声宽度。
+在同一 $t_\alpha$ 处，$\sigma'^2-\sigma^2$ 对 $K_H,K'_H,W_H$ 的改变分别是
+
+$$
+\frac{\delta(\sigma'^2-\sigma^2)t_\alpha^2}{2\alpha},\quad
+\frac{\delta(\sigma'^2-\sigma^2)t_\alpha}{\alpha},\quad
+\frac{\delta(\sigma'^2-\sigma^2)}{\alpha}.
+\tag{126.6}
+$$
+
+它们是多项式乘指数小量。标准化位置、正密度下界和全部固定阶插入矩的多项式界保持成立，
+附近宽度的密度比有固定上下界。式 (125.3)–(125.8) 在这些附近宽度同样成立。
+因此这一吸收仅付多项式成本；配分导数仍由原势能插入计算，不对宽度夹逼求导。
+
+还须支付全部尾部。原幂律二项与 Gaussian 乘积律在高中心盒外的概率至多
+$\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-cQ^4}$。二项部分可用
+$S_j\ge c z_j^2-C$、单组配分下界 $c\sqrt{C_j+1}$ 作距离壳求和，
+再对至多 $m_Q$ 个组求并；Gaussian 部分是相同标准化阈值下的正态尾。
+二项计数盒上 $S_Q\le CN_J$，$|\mathcal D|\le CB$，
+$\lambda_y\le\exp(CQ^3+2L)$。
+故三次势能插入和其比较中任何固定次插入在尾部最多付
+$\exp(C_kQ^3+2kL)$。Gaussian 的固定多项式尾插入由较高 Gaussian 矩及
+Cauchy–Schwarz 支付，仍有 $e^{-c'Q^4}$，噪声因子至多另付 $\sigma^{-2k}$。
+选择因子 $e^{-\alpha s\mathcal D^2}$、$e^{-\alpha s\mathcal D_G^2}$ 不超过一。
+
+由 (123.15)，标准化密度在紧输出上至少 $c_R$；
+$|K_H(t_\alpha)-t_\alpha V|\le C/\delta$。
+因此乘积归一化后的原 Gaussian 输出核积分至少
+
+$$
+c_R\sigma e^{-C_R/\delta}.
+\tag{126.7}
+$$
+
+带 $s=\eta$ 的核积分由 (125.2) 再保留固定比例。
+高二项与 Gaussian 无输出归一化常数之比，由相同 Stirling 格元比较及无输出尾估计为 $1+o(1)$。
+故除以实际比较分母所付对数成本只有
+$O_k(Q^3+L+\delta^{-1})$，严格小于尾指数的 $Q^4$ 阶。
+没有对总偏差使用 $Q^2$ 或其他截断。
+
+综合格元和尾部，存在 $b_2>0$ 使
+
+$$
+\frac{|\partial_\alpha^kJ_s^{\rm count}
+              -\partial_\alpha^k\mathcal C_s|}{\mathcal C_s}
+ \le\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-b_2Q^3},\quad 0\le k\le3.
+\tag{126.8}
+$$
+
+比较配分的各固定阶未中心化势能矩均为多项式，因而
+$|\partial_\alpha^k\mathcal C_s|/\mathcal C_s\le\operatorname{poly}(Q)$。
+对数的前三次导数公式将 (126.8) 化为 (126.2)。
+格元体积给 $B^{|H|}$；模态常数已经在 $S_j$ 中精确减去。
+上述比较既未舍弃原计数多重度，也未改变原输出条件。∎
+
+## 127. 完整后验的三次桥与概率结论
+
+**引理 127.1（完整计数的三次响应桥）。** 在约定 123.1 的共同纤维类上，
+
+$$
+\left\|\Xi_\alpha(y)+\sqrt\delta\,t_\alpha y
+               +\frac{\delta y^2}{2W_\alpha}\right\|_{3,R}\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{127.1}
+$$
+
+**证明。** 由 (124.3)，$J_2=e^{\alpha c_0}J_\eta^{\rm count}$，
+$J_0=J_0^{\rm count}$。引理 124.1、125.1、126.1 给出
+
+$$
+\log J_P-\log J_0
+ =\alpha c_0+\log(\mathcal J_\eta/\mathcal J_0)
+       +O_{C^3}\bigl(\operatorname{poly}(Q)e^{-bQ^3}\bigr),
+$$
+
+$$
+\|\log J_P-\log J_0-\alpha c_0\|_{3,R}\le C\delta^5+o(1).
+\tag{127.2}
+$$
+
+原 $P_x(m)^\alpha$ 与 $e^{-\alpha(S_Q(m)-\ell(m))}$ 只差输出无关的模态质量常数。
+因此 (122.3) 恰为 $\log J_P(\alpha,y)-\log J_P(\alpha,0)$。
+式 (127.2) 中的 $\alpha c_0$ 在 $y$ 与零处消去。
+再由 $s=0$ 的 (126.2)，
+$B^{|H|},Z_L$ 和 Gaussian 归一化常数也在输出比值中精确消去。
+剩下 $\log[g_\alpha(y)/g_\alpha(0)]$ 及三次范数趋零的误差。
+引理 123.2 即给 (127.1)。∎
+
+**证明 127.2（定理 122.1）。** 对 (127.1) 的实际三次余项在 $\alpha=1$ 求导，
+并用精确有限恒等式 (122.4)，得到
+
+$$
+\sup_{|y|\le R}\left|
+C3_x(y)-C3_x(0)-\sqrt\delta\,t_1'''y
+-\frac\delta2(1/W_\alpha)'''\big|_1y^2\right|\longrightarrow0
+\tag{127.3}
+$$
+
+在每个固定好事件常数类上一致成立。
+有限函数光滑，区间端点的一侧三次导数等于普通导数。
+此处没有从二次余项推出三次导数。
+
+好事件、原完整窗口与原行估计对 pair、path 两种数据律及全部确定大小 $q$ 的支持一致。
+固定好事件常数使其补集概率任意小，再令 $n\to\infty$ 并穷尽这些常数，得到 (122.2)。
+也可直接用原核的支持置换等变性核对支持一致性：任意两个大小 $q$ 的支持由同一个正类置换联系，
+原数据律、均匀支持先验、分组、精确中心和所有响应函数在该置换下共同运输。
+连续输出函数在紧集上的上确界等于可数稠密集上的上确界，所以事件可测。
+
+完整有限系数可由下列隐函数恒等式计算，所有偏导在 $(\alpha,t_\alpha)$ 取值：
+
+$$
+t'=-K_{t\alpha}/W,
+$$
+
+$$
+t''=-\{K_{t\alpha\alpha}+2K_{tt\alpha}t'+K_{ttt}(t')^2\}/W,
+$$
+
+$$
+t'''=-\{K_{t\alpha\alpha\alpha}
+ +3K_{tt\alpha\alpha}t'+3K_{ttt\alpha}(t')^2+K_{tttt}(t')^3
+ +3(K_{tt\alpha}+K_{ttt}t')t''\}/W,
+$$
+
+$$
+(1/W)'''=-W'''/W^2+6W'W''/W^3-6(W')^3/W^4.
+\tag{127.4}
+$$
+
+这些是 (121.10) 的有限求和导数，包含全部原组、噪声与精确中心；
+尤其没有在可被放大的线性项中替换为连续轮廓极限。
+所有证明只要求 (122.1) 的严格不等式。∎
+
+**命题 127.3（结论的参数范围）。** 定理 122.1 对每个固定 $\beta\in(1/2,1)$ 和原固定振幅成立，
+不要求 $\sigma_n$ 有任何额外多项式速率。它的陈述不包含 $\sigma_n=0$、
+$\limsup L_n/Q_n^3=c_q/2$、变化的 $\beta$ 或振幅上的一致性、非紧输出集合或更高信息累积量。
+
+**证明。** $l<c_q/2$ 和 $2\chi_0<c_q-l$ 正是格元误差除以噪声后仍指数小的条件；
+其余噪声成本仅为固定多项式或对数阶 $O(L+Q^3)$。
+$\sigma>0$ 用于有限层级的正密度和根的存在。
+根区间、核心块及好事件常数依赖固定模型参数，输出正密度下界依赖 $R$。
+这些证明给出 (122.1) 下每个确定序列的结论，不给所列其他范围的结论。∎

+# The actual theta tail and a strict Robin response
+
+## Abstract
+
+The actual weighted Chebyshev theta tail equals the normalized second Mertens error and gives an explicit prefix-lcm Robin response.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (The improper integral and its arithmetic consequence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ThetaTailRobinWitness.theta_tail_mertens_robin`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Robin/ThetaTailRobinWitness.theta_tail_mertens_robin` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real x>=2 the actual function (theta(t)-t)*w(t), where w(t)=(log(t)+1)/(t²*log(t)²), is Lebesgue integrable on (x,infinity). Its negative integral is E₂p(x)-(theta(x)-x)/(x*log(x)). Here theta is the Chebyshev prime sum and E₂p is the second Mertens error with Mertens.M as its constant.
+
+Write I(x)=(theta(x)-x)/(x*log(x))-E₂p(x). Classical finite Abel summation gives I(u)=I(x)-integral_x^u (theta(t)-t)*w(t) dt. The finite calculation reuses the canonical ThetaTailPartialSummation.theta_tail_finite supplier from MertensCumulativePeak; its reciprocal logarithmic weight and prime-cutoff identities provide the finite bridge. The elementary bound 0<=theta(u)<=u*log(4), together with |E₂p(u)|<=(log(4)+6+Mertens.E₁)/log(u), proves I(u) tends to zero. ActualThetaTailLaplace supplies unconditional integrability of the same actual kernel. Taking the upper limit to infinity therefore fixes the normalization and proves the equality.
+
+For x>=10000, suppose this negative integral exceeds 7/sqrt(x). The Mertens correction E₃(x)+E₂p(x) has absolute value at most 4/x<=1/sqrt(x), and (psi(x)-theta(x))/(x*log(x))<=2/sqrt(x). These bounds give E₃(x)<-4/sqrt(x)-(psi(x)-x)/(x*log(x)). The common prefix-lcm response in LcmRobinResponse applies at this same real x.
+
+The resulting integer is exactly D=lcm(1,...,floor(x)). It satisfies D>5040, sigma(D)/D>exp(gamma)*log(log(D)), log(D)=psi(x), and D<=exp(x*log(x)), where gamma is the real Euler constant. This theorem takes the stated actual tail peak as a premise; the following application supplies it conditionally from a genuine zeta zero.

+  have htheta : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Chebyshev.theta x - x) / (x * log x))
+      atTop (𝓝 0) := by
+    apply squeeze_zero_norm' ?_
+      ((tendsto_const_nhds (x := log 4 + 1)).div_atTop tendsto_log_atTop)
+    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (2 : ℝ)] with x hx
+    have hx0 : 0 < x := by linarith
+    have hl : 0 < log x := log_pos (by linarith)
+    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_div, abs_of_pos (mul_pos hx0 hl)]
+    apply (div_le_iff₀ (mul_pos hx0 hl)).mpr
+    have hab : |Chebyshev.theta x - x| ≤ (log 4 + 1) * x := by
+      rw [abs_le]
+      constructor

+        have h4 := Real.log_nonneg (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) ≤ 4)

+      · have := Chebyshev.theta_le_log4_mul_x hx0.le
+        linarith
+    calc
+      _ ≤ (log 4 + 1) * x := hab
+      _ = (log 4 + 1) / log x * (x * log x) := by field_simp
+  have hE : Tendsto Mertens.E₂p atTop (𝓝 0) := by
+    exact Mertens.E₂p.bound'.tendsto_zero_of_tendsto (tendsto_const_nhds (x := (1 : ℝ)))
+  simpa only [I, sub_zero] using htheta.sub hE

+      apply sum_congr rfl

+      simp only [Mertens.M_eq_summand]

+    rw [Mertens.γ.eq_eulerMascheroni]

+**Definition 12.1 (The full endpoint array problem).** For each integer $a\ge4$, put $r=a+1$ and $s=a+2$. Let $\mathcal X_a$ consist of all the profiles of Definition 1.1 on $[s]$ with $\mathbb E K=a$. Explicitly, the variables are one mass $x_T\ge0$ for every nonempty $T\subseteq[s]$, subject to

+$$
+\sum_Tx_T=1,\qquad \sum_T|T|x_T=a,\qquad
+y_i=\sum_{T\ni i}x_T>0\quad(i\in[s]).
+$$
+
+No support or connectedness restriction is imposed. Define
+
+$$
+H(x)=2J_{a+2}(x)
+=\mathbb E\left[K^2\sum_{i\in T}y_i^{-2}\right],\qquad
+B_0=a(a+1)^2,\qquad d(x)=H(x)-B_0,\qquad
+g_a=\frac12\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_a}d(x).
+$$
+
+Write
+
+$$
+M_a=2a^3+2a^2-2a-1,\qquad N_a=2a^3-2a-1.
+$$
+
+Thus $M_a,N_a$ are, respectively, $A_a,E_a$ of Theorem 10.1. On the larger scalar interval $0<t<a$, set
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+h_a(t)
+&=\frac1t+\frac{a^2r^2}{a-t}
+ +\frac{(2a+1)(a-1)r^3t}{(a-t)^2},\\
+\lambda_a(t)
+&=\frac3t-\frac{a(2a+1)r^3t}{(a-t)^2}.
+\end{aligned}\tag{12.1}
+$$
+
+The quantities $K$, all conditional laws and all marginals below always refer to the same $x\in\mathcal X_a$.
+
+**Lemma 12.2 (The scalar candidate and its unique positive root).** For every integer $a\ge4$, the function $h_a$ is strictly convex on $(0,a)$. Its unique minimizer $\epsilon_a$ belongs to $(0,1/a)$ and is the unique positive real solution of
+
+$$
+(a-\epsilon_a)^3
+=r^2\epsilon_a^2\bigl[aM_a+N_a\epsilon_a\bigr].
+\tag{12.2}
+$$
+
+The family of Theorem 10.1, with its parameter set to any $0<t\le1/a$, has energy $h_a(t)$. In particular $h_a(\epsilon_a)$ is an attained upper bound for $\inf_{\mathcal X_a}H$, without presupposing global optimality.
+
+**Proof.** Reuse the array of Theorem 10.1, with its core denoted by $C$ and its remaining label by $e$:
+
+$$
+x_{\{e\}}=t,\qquad x_C=(a-1)t,\qquad
+x_{C\setminus\{j\}}=\frac{1-at}{r}\quad(j\in C),
+\qquad x_T=0\text{ otherwise}.
+\tag{12.3}
+$$
+
+Its admissibility and energy were computed there. Formula (10.2) gives
+
+$$
+h_a(t)-B_0
+=\frac1t+\frac{r^2t(M_a-at)}{(a-t)^2}.
+\tag{12.4}
+$$
+
+The right side agrees with (12.1) by expansion. Thus no new construction is required.
+
+For $U=a^2r^2>0$ and $V=(2a+1)(a-1)r^3>0$, differentiation gives
+
+$$
+h_a''(t)
+=\frac2{t^3}+\frac{2U}{(a-t)^3}
+ +\frac{V(4a+2t)}{(a-t)^4}>0.
+$$
+
+Also

+$$
+h_a'(t)=-\frac1{t^2}
+ +\frac{r^2(aM_a+N_at)}{(a-t)^3},\qquad
+h_a'(1/a)=\frac{a^3(2a^2+a+4)}{(a-1)^2}>0.
+\tag{12.5}
+$$

+Since $h_a'(t)\to-\infty$ as $t\downarrow0$, strict convexity gives one stationary point in $(0,1/a)$ and makes it the unique minimum on $(0,a)$. Equation (12.5) proves (12.2). Since $M_a,N_a>0$, (12.2) has no positive solution with $\epsilon_a\ge a$; hence this is its unique positive root. The array (12.3) at $\epsilon_a$ supplies the asserted upper bound. ∎

+$$
+\begin{gathered}
+t=y_e=\min_i y_i,\qquad C=[s]\setminus\{e\},\qquad
+I=\mathbf1_{\{e\in T\}},\qquad
+I_i=\mathbf1_{\{i\in T\}}\ (i\in C),\\

+D_i&=\mathbb E[I(2L+1)I_i],\\

+\tag{12.17}
+$$

+$$

+**Theorem 12.5 (Eventual exact global minimum and all equality arrays).** There exists an integer $a_0\ge7$ such that, for every integer $a\ge a_0$ and every $x\in\mathcal X_a$,

+$$
+H(x)\ge h_a(\epsilon_a).
+\tag{12.24}
+$$
+
+Equality holds if and only if, for some label $e$ and $C=[a+2]\setminus\{e\}$,
+
+$$
+x_{\{e\}}=\epsilon_a,\qquad
+x_C=(a-1)\epsilon_a,\qquad
+x_{C\setminus\{j\}}=\frac{1-a\epsilon_a}{a+1}\quad(j\in C),
+\qquad x_T=0\text{ otherwise}.
+\tag{12.25}
+$$
+

+
+$$
+g_a=\frac1{2\epsilon_a}
+ +\frac{r^2\epsilon_a(M_a-a\epsilon_a)}
+        {2(a-\epsilon_a)^2}.
+\tag{12.26}
+$$

No explicit or smallest $a_0$ is specified, and no classification for $4\le a<a_0$, other values of $q,s$, or exact finite graph budgets is asserted.

+
+$$
+H(x)\ge h_a(t)+\beta\lambda_a(t)\ge h_a(\epsilon_a).

+The last step uses $\beta\ge0$, $\lambda_a(t)>0$, and the scalar minimum on the whole interval $(0,a)$. Thus the bound holds for all arrays, with the single threshold $a_0$ independent of the array. The feasible family in Lemma 12.2 attains it.

+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+0={}&h_a(t)-h_a(\epsilon_a)+\beta\lambda_a(t)

+$$

+=\frac1{\sqrt2\,a^{3/2}}

+\begin{aligned}
+b_a&=\frac{r^2M_a}{a^2}

+t_b&=b_a^{-1/2},\\

+\frac{r^2t^2(2aM_a-a^3-M_at)}{a^2(a-t)^2}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+An exact rearrangement of (12.4) is
+
+$$
+h_a(t)-B_0=\frac1t+b_at+W_a(t).
+\tag{12.29}
+$$
+
+The stationary equation (12.2) is equivalently the clean positive-factor identity
+
+$$
+\epsilon_a^{-2}
+=b_a\left(1+\frac{N_a}{M_a}\frac{\epsilon_a}{a}\right)
+       \left(1-\frac{\epsilon_a}{a}\right)^{-3}.
+\tag{12.30}

+$$

+\epsilon_a=t_b+O(a^{-4}).
+\tag{12.31}
+$$

+
+$$
+c_{2,a}=r^2\left(\frac{2M_a}{a^3}-\frac1a\right)
+=4a^2+11a+6-\frac7a-\frac8{a^2}-\frac2{a^3}.

+$$

+
+$$
+\frac1{\epsilon_a}+b_a\epsilon_a-2\sqrt{b_a}
+=\frac{b_a(\epsilon_a-t_b)^2}{\epsilon_a}.
+$$

+By (12.31) its right side is $O(a^{-7/2})$. Since
+$c_{2,a}=O(a^2)$, (12.31)–(12.32) similarly imply
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+W_a(\epsilon_a)
+&=\frac{c_{2,a}}{b_a}+O(a^{-7/2}),\\
+g_a
+&=\sqrt{b_a}+\frac{c_{2,a}}{2b_a}+O(a^{-7/2})
+ =\sqrt{b_a}+\frac1a+O(a^{-2}).
+\end{aligned}\tag{12.33}
+$$

+$O(a^2\cdot a^{-3/2}\cdot a^{-4})=O(a^{-7/2})$;

+$$
+\frac{b_a}{2a^3}

+\begin{aligned}

+&=\sqrt2\,a^{3/2}
+ \left(1+\frac3{2a}-\frac1{8a^2}+O(a^{-3})\right),\\

+&=\frac1{\sqrt2\,a^{3/2}}

+电学伪逆和迹公式的经典出处仍是
+[Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi，DOI:10.1137/050645452](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/eff_res.pdf)，
+§§2.4–2.5，式 (8)、(13)–(15)；这里只使用其电学恒等式。
+由 (5.4) 和谱分解，内点上有
+
+$$
+L(c)^+|_H=sM(p),\qquad
+\lambda_2(L(c))=\frac1{s\rho(p)},\qquad
+R(c)=nsT(p),\qquad \lambda_2R=\Phi(p).
+\tag{5.5}
+$$
+
+向量 $a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ 线性无关：若
+$\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\alpha_i a_i=0$，其未投影的累积向量为常数，
+但第 $n$ 坐标为零，故各坐标均为零，依次相减给出所有 $\alpha_i=0$。
+因此 $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}$ 仿射无关，且
+
+$$
+M(p)=\sum_i p_i(a_i-\bar a)(a_i-\bar a)^{\mathsf T}
+\tag{5.6}
+$$
+
+在支撑大小为 $k$ 的点上秩恰为 $k-1$。
+事实上二次型为零当且仅当该向量与全部支撑点之差正交。
+非顶点时 $k\ge2$，故 $T,\rho>0$；连续性由矩阵元素和最大特征值的
+连续性得到。内点时 $M$ 在 $H$ 上正定。
+
+先取 $\ell=0$。删边后的普通路径若有正边电阻 $q_i$，
+其唯一流为 $z_i=\langle a_i,h\rangle$，同一能量计算给出
+$L_{P_n}^+|_H=K_0(q)$。
+因此约定 4.2 的完整路径定理直接给出 $\Psi_0(q)\le A_n$，
+并在 $q_i$ 与 $d_i/s_i$ 成比例时取等号。
+若一些 $q_i=0$，以正 $q$ 逼近：由于
+
+$$
+\|a_i\|^2=\frac{i(n-i)}n\ge\frac{n-1}n,\qquad
+\operatorname{tr}K_0(q)\ge\frac{n-1}n,
+$$
+
+分母在整个闭方向单纯形上不为零，连续延拓保持该上界。
+这一步没有以单位质量的缩点路径替换原来的 $n$ 个顶点。
+对一般 $\ell$，循环重标号给出完全相同的路径、电学恒等式和范数界。
+
+令 $v=\sum_{i\ne\ell}q_i(a_i-a_\ell)$、$K=K_\ell(q)$。
+将 (5.6) 在 $p=(1-\epsilon)\varepsilon_\ell+\epsilon q$ 处展开，得到
+
+$$
+M(p)=\epsilon(K-\epsilon vv^{\mathsf T}),\qquad
+vv^{\mathsf T}\preceq K.
+\tag{5.7}
+$$
+
+后一不等式是标量 Cauchy–Schwarz 不等式
+$(\sum_i q_i\langle a_i-a_\ell,h\rangle)^2
+\le\sum_i q_i\langle a_i-a_\ell,h\rangle^2$。
+所以
+
+$$
+(1-\epsilon)K\preceq K-\epsilon vv^{\mathsf T}\preceq K.
+$$
+
+对迹和最大特征值分别使用这些序界，即得 (5.1)，继而得 (5.2)。
+上界对全部闭方向一致；下界取上述严格正的路径最优方向，令
+$\epsilon\downarrow0$，便证明 (5.3)。∎
+
+## 6. 路径值的严格超越与每个真面的排除
+
+**定理 6.1（实际正环严格超过完整路径常数）。** 对每个整数 $n\ge5$，
+存在全部 $n$ 条边电导均有限且严格为正的实际 $C_n$，满足
+$\lambda_2R>A_n$。因此 $B_n>A_n$。
+
+证明。仅调用约定 4.2 的完整路径最优点，取
+$c_i=s_i/d_i$、$1\le i<n$。
+令 $K=L_{P_n}^+|_H$、$T=\operatorname{tr}K$、
+$r_i=d_i/s_i$。被引定理给出
+
+$$
+\lambda_{\max}(K)=1,\qquad T=\frac{A_n}{n},\qquad
+u_j=\frac{s_j-s_{j-1}}{\sqrt{A_n}},\qquad K\nu=\nu,
+\quad\|\nu\|=1.
+$$
+
+此最大特征值单重：路径 Laplacian 的任一特征向量由其第一个坐标
+通过首行及后继行唯一递推确定，若第一个坐标为零便全为零；
+实对称性使几何重数与代数重数相同。
+
+令 $b=\delta_1-\delta_n$、$v=Kb$、$\ell=b^{\mathsf T}Kb=\sum_i r_i$。
+给缺失的实际边 $e_0$ 添加电导 $h>0$，在 $H$ 上直接相乘验证逆矩阵为
+
+$$
+K_h=(L_{P_n}|_H+hbb^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
+=K-\tau vv^{\mathsf T},\qquad
+\tau=\frac{h}{1+h\ell}>0.
+\tag{6.1}
+$$
+
+为计算严格增益，$\langle a_i,b\rangle=1$ 给出
+$v=\sum_i r_i a_i$，且
+
+$$
+\langle\nu,a_i\rangle=\frac{s_i}{\sqrt{A_n}},\qquad
+\langle\nu,v\rangle=\frac{\sum_i d_i}{\sqrt{A_n}}
+=\frac{2\sqrt{n-1}}{\sqrt{A_n}}.
+\tag{6.2}
+$$
+
+对 $1\le i\le j<n$，
+
+$$
+\langle a_i,a_j\rangle=\frac{i(n-j)}n
+\le\frac{s_is_j}{n},
+$$
+
+其中 $i<j$ 时严格，因为 $i(n-j)<j(n-i)$。
+所有 $r_i>0$，且有至少两个不同的路径边指标，所以
+
+$$
+\|v\|^2=\sum_{i,j}r_ir_j\langle a_i,a_j\rangle
+<\frac1n\left(\sum_i r_i s_i\right)^2
+=\frac{4(n-1)}n.
+\tag{6.3}
+$$
+
+使用有限维简单特征值的一阶展开，
+
+$$
+\lambda_{\max}(K-\tau vv^{\mathsf T})
+=1-\tau\langle\nu,v\rangle^2+O(\tau^2).
+\tag{6.4}
+$$
+
+这里的余项可直接由谱隙得到：在
+$\mathbb R\nu\oplus\nu^\perp$ 中，右下块的最大特征值与 $1$ 有严格间隙，
+交叉块为 $O(\tau)$。Rayleigh 下界取 $\nu$；上界对交叉项配方，
+便与左上标量相差 $O(\tau^2)$。
+于是 (5.5)、(6.1)–(6.4) 给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\lambda_2(L_{P_n}+hbb^{\mathsf T})R
+&=\frac{n(T-\tau\|v\|^2)}{\lambda_{\max}(K-\tau vv^{\mathsf T})}\\
+&=A_n+\tau\bigl(4(n-1)-n\|v\|^2\bigr)+O(\tau^2)>A_n
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+对所有充分小的 $h>0$ 成立。式 (6.3) 保证一阶系数严格为正，
+因此选择的是有限正电导，并非只在删边极限取值。∎
+
+**定理 6.2（任意非顶点真面的严格内点支配）。** 固定 $n\ge5$。
+对每个 $p\in\partial\Delta\setminus\mathcal V$，存在
+$p'\in\Delta^\circ$ 使 $\Phi(p')>\Phi(p)$。
+此结论涵盖每个真面的全部非顶点，包括任意数目的零坐标，
+并在原来的 $n$ 个计数质量上成立。
+
+证明。令 $S_p=\{i:p_i>0\}$，$k=|S_p|\ge2$，并置
+
+$$
+W=\operatorname{span}\{a_i-a_l:i\in S_p\}\subset H
+$$
+
+其中 $l\in S_p$。式 (5.6) 表明 $M(p)$ 的像恰为 $W$，
+在 $W^\perp$ 上为零，在 $W$ 上正定。
+至少有一个零坐标，故可在循环边指标上选取相邻的两个支撑指标 $l,r$，
+它们之间沿选定方向有 $m-1\ge1$ 个零坐标。
+因支撑至少有两个，$2\le m\le n-1$。
+在该间隙任选距 $l$ 为 $j$ 的指标 $k_0$，$1\le j<m$，置
+
+$$
+\theta=\frac jm,\qquad
+ d=a_r-a_l,\qquad
+ w=a_{k_0}-(1-\theta)a_l-\theta a_r,\qquad
+ z=(1-\theta)a_l+\theta a_r-\bar a(p).
+\tag{6.5}
+$$
+
+跨过循环指标 $0$ 时，用 $a_n=a_0$ 和
+$a_i-a_{i-1}=P\delta_i$（顶点指标也按周期解释）计算。
+若 $I$ 是间隙对应的 $m$ 个原始顶点，$J$ 是其中前 $j$ 个，则
+
+$$
+d=P\mathbf1_I,\qquad
+w=\mathbf1_J-\frac jm\mathbf1_I,\qquad
+\|w\|^2=\frac{j(m-j)}m=:b_0>0,\qquad
+\|d\|^2=\frac{m(n-m)}n.
+\tag{6.6}
+$$
+
+每个 $a_i-a_l$、$i\in S_p$ 在 $I$ 的全部坐标上取同一数值，
+所以 $w\perp W$。同时 $d,z\in W$。
+这一步保留了每个原始顶点的内积；若以块常数 $x_i=y_I$ 表示，
+范数贡献是 $|I|y_I^2$，不是 $y_I^2$。
+
+取
+
+$$
+p(t)=p+t\bigl(\varepsilon_{k_0}-(1-\theta)\varepsilon_l
+-\theta\varepsilon_r\bigr).
+$$
+
+对充分小的 $t>0$，它仍在 $\Delta$，因为只减去两个严格正的支撑坐标。
+其均值变化为 $tw$。逐项展开协方差，得到精确恒等式
+
+$$
+M(p(t))=M(p)-t\theta(1-\theta)dd^{\mathsf T}
++t(zw^{\mathsf T}+wz^{\mathsf T})+t(1-t)ww^{\mathsf T}.
+\tag{6.7}
+$$
+
+因此，无论 $\rho=\rho(p)$ 的重数是多少，$W$ 上的整个压缩都不增加。
+另一方面，取迹并使用 $w\perp W$，得到
+
+$$
+T(p(t))=T(p)+a_0t-b_0t^2,\qquad
+ a_0=b_0-\theta(1-\theta)\|d\|^2=\frac{j(m-j)}n>0.
+\tag{6.8}
+$$
+
+以下控制整个最大特征空间，而非单独选择一个特征向量。
+令 $T=T(p)$，并取 $0<t<1$ 足够小，使 $tb_0\le\rho/2$。
+在 $W\oplus W^\perp$ 中，(6.7) 对任意向量 $(x,y)$ 给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\langle M(p(t))(x,y),(x,y)\rangle
+&\le\rho\|x\|^2+2t\|z\|\|w\|\|x\|\|y\|
++\frac\rho2\|y\|^2\\
+&\le(\rho+C t^2)\|x\|^2+\rho\|y\|^2,\qquad
+ C=\frac{2\|z\|^2b_0}{\rho}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+最后一步使用 $2AB\le 2A^2/\rho+\rho B^2/2$。
+于是 $\rho(p(t))\le\rho+Ct^2$，并由 (6.8) 得到
+
+$$
+\Phi(p(t))\ge\frac{n(T+a_0t-b_0t^2)}{\rho+Ct^2}
+>\frac{nT}{\rho}=\Phi(p)
+\tag{6.9}
+$$
+
+只要再取 $t<\rho a_0/(\rho b_0+TC)$。
+所有限制都可与两个支撑坐标的正性限制同时满足。
+若 $p(t)$ 还有零坐标，令
+$p'=(1-\eta)p(t)+\eta(1/n,\ldots,1/n)$；
+定理 5.1 的非顶点连续性保证对充分小的 $\eta>0$ 仍保留 (6.9) 的严格性。
+此时 $p'\in\Delta^\circ$，对应同一实际 $n$ 顶点环上的有限正电导
+$c_i'=1/p_i'$。由 (5.5)，其乘积恰为 $\Phi(p')$。∎
+
+## 7. 全边界排除后的达到性与定量分离
+
+**定理 7.1（有限正最大点与严格双界）。** 对每个整数 $n\ge5$，
+$B_n$ 在实际标号环的有限严格正电导处达到，并且
+
+$$
+A_n<B_n<n(n-1).
+\tag{7.1}
+$$
+
+每个 $R_0>0$ 都满足
+
+$$
+\max_{c\in(0,\infty)^n,\ R(c)=R_0}\lambda_2(L(c))=\frac{B_n}{R_0}.
+\tag{7.2}
+$$
+
+证明。由 (5.5) 和 (4.2)，$B_n=\sup_{p\in\Delta^\circ}\Phi(p)$。
+$M(p)$ 在 $H$ 上正定，维数为 $n-1$，所以
+$\Phi(p)\le n(n-1)$，从而上确界有限。
+定理 6.1 已经给出 $B_n>A_n$。
+
+取 $\Phi(p^{(k)})\to B_n$ 的内点序列，先在闭单纯形内取一个收敛子列，
+记其极限为 $p^*$。若 $p^*$ 是顶点，定理 5.1 的一致界给出
+$\limsup_k\Phi(p^{(k)})\le A_n<B_n$，矛盾。
+若 $p^*\in\partial\Delta\setminus\mathcal V$，连续性给出
+$\Phi(p^*)=B_n$，而定理 6.2 给出实际内点 $p'$ 满足
+$\Phi(p')>B_n$，也矛盾。
+已经排除全部边界，故 $p^*\in\Delta^\circ$，连续性才给出
+$\Phi(p^*)=B_n$，这证明达到性。
+
+若某一内点有 $\Phi(p)=n(n-1)$，迹与最大特征值之比取等号迫使
+$M(p)=\rho(p)I_H$。式 (5.4) 于是给出
+
+$$
+L(c)=\frac1{s\rho(p)}P.
+$$
+
+但右边任意两个不同顶点间的矩阵元都是负数，而 $n\ge5$ 的实际环
+存在非相邻顶点，它们之间的 Laplacian 矩阵元为零，矛盾。
+将这一严格性应用于刚证明存在的最大点，便得 (7.1) 的严格上界。
+
+最后任取内点 $p$，令 $\widehat c_i=1/p_i$。
+此时总边电阻为 $1$，由 (5.5) 得
+$R(\widehat c)=nT(p)$。定义
+
+$$
+c_i^{(R_0)}=\frac{nT(p)}{R_0p_i}.
+\tag{7.3}
+$$
+
+缩放律给出
+
+$$
+R(c^{(R_0)})=R_0,\qquad
+\lambda_2(L(c^{(R_0)}))=\frac{\Phi(p)}{R_0}.
+$$
+
+取 $p=p^*$ 就达到 (7.2)；任一其它可行电导的乘积不超过 $B_n$，
+所以 (7.2) 的上界也对全部独立正电导成立。∎
+
+**定理 7.2（全部近最大点的一致内部分离）。** 对每个固定整数 $n\ge5$，
+存在仅依赖于 $n$ 的 $\epsilon_n>0$ 和 $\delta_n>0$，使
+
+$$
+p\in\Delta^\circ,\quad \Phi(p)\ge B_n-\epsilon_n
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \min_i p_i\ge\delta_n.
+\tag{7.4}
+$$
+
+尤其所有趋于 $B_n$ 的序列最终都落入同一个开单纯形内的紧子集。
+任意固定 $R_0>0$ 时，这些点经 (7.3) 对应的电导也落入
+$(0,\infty)^n$ 的一个紧子集。
+
+证明。定义实际边界水平
+
+$$
+\Gamma_n=\max\left\{A_n,\,
+\sup_{p\in\partial\Delta\setminus\mathcal V}\Phi(p)\right\}.
+$$
+
+首先证明 $\Gamma_n<B_n$。每个非顶点边界点都被定理 6.2 的内点严格支配，
+故其值严格小于 $B_n$。若这些边界值的上确界仍为 $B_n$，
+取逼近它的边界序列并在闭单纯形取收敛子列。
+极限非顶点时，连续性会给出一个值为 $B_n$ 的边界点，矛盾；
+极限为顶点时，(5.1) 对闭方向也成立，给出上极限不超过
+$A_n<B_n$，仍矛盾。结合 $A_n<B_n$，得所需严格间隙。
+
+令 $\epsilon_n=(B_n-\Gamma_n)/4>0$。
+存在 $\delta_n>0$ 使
+
+$$
+p\in\Delta^\circ,\quad\min_i p_i<\delta_n
+\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\Phi(p)\le\Gamma_n+\epsilon_n.
+\tag{7.5}
+$$
+
+否则可选取 $\min_i p_i\to0$ 而
+$\Phi(p)>\Gamma_n+\epsilon_n$ 的内点序列。其收敛子列的极限在边界；
+非顶点极限由连续性否定这一严格下界，顶点极限由 (5.1) 否定它。
+这证明 (7.5)，并因
+$\Gamma_n+\epsilon_n=B_n-3\epsilon_n<B_n-\epsilon_n$
+得到 (7.4)。必要时减小 $\delta_n$，可使 $\delta_n<1/n$。
+该论证证明分离常数存在，没有指定未经推导的数值。
+
+集合 $\{p\in\Delta:p_i\ge\delta_n\ \text{对所有 }i\}$ 是开单纯形内的紧集。
+其上 $T(p)$ 连续且严格为正，(7.3) 因而是取值于有限正电导的连续映射，
+像亦紧。这同时排除固定总电阻下近最大点的任一电导逃逸。∎
+
+## 8. 内点最大值的必要重数与尚未确定的精确问题
+
+**定理 8.1（任何内点局部最大值的 Fiedler 重数恰为二）。** 固定 $n\ge5$。
+若实际正环的电导 $c$ 是尺度不变量 $\lambda_2R$ 的局部最大点，
+或是任意固定 $R_0>0$ 水平上 $\lambda_2$ 的局部最大点，则
+
+$$
+\lambda_2(L(c))=\lambda_3(L(c))<\lambda_4(L(c)).
+\tag{8.1}
+$$
+
+因此 (8.1) 适用于定理 7.1 的每一个全局最大点。
+
+证明。先在 $p\in\Delta^\circ$ 上证明 $\rho(p)$ 在 $\Phi$ 的局部最大点
+不能单重。暂设它单重，取单位最大特征向量 $u\in H$，并记
+
+$$
+v_i=a_i-\bar a(p),\qquad h_i=\langle u,v_i\rangle,\qquad
+T=T(p),\quad\rho=\rho(p),\quad\beta=\frac T\rho.
+$$
+
+若 $\xi\in\mathbb R^n$ 满足 $\sum_i\xi_i=0$，协方差的一阶变化为
+$\sum_i\xi_i v_i v_i^{\mathsf T}$。
+简单特征值的 Rayleigh 展开（与 (6.4) 的谱隙配方论证相同）给出
+
+$$
+D\Phi(p)[\xi]=\frac n\rho
+\sum_i\xi_i\bigl(\|v_i\|^2-\beta h_i^2\bigr).
+\tag{8.2}
+$$
+
+局部最大点允许所有这样的双向变化，故括号对 $i$ 为常数；
+其 $p$ 加权和是 $T-\beta\rho=0$，所以
+
+$$
+\|v_i\|^2=\beta h_i^2\qquad\text{对所有 }i.
+\tag{8.3}
+$$
+
+仿射无关性和 $p_i>0$ 保证 $\bar a(p)\ne a_i$，所以每个 $v_i\ne0$，
+继而每个 $h_i\ne0$。定义
+
+$$
+S=\sum_i\frac{p_i}{h_i},\qquad
+w=\sum_i\frac{p_i v_i}{h_i},\qquad
+C=\sum_i\frac{p_i}{h_i}v_i v_i^{\mathsf T}.
+$$
+
+由 $\sum_i p_iv_i=0$、$\sum_i p_i h_i=0$ 以及 (8.3)，有
+
+$$
+\langle u,w\rangle=1,\qquad Cu=0,\qquad\operatorname{tr}C=0,
+\qquad \|w\|^2<\sum_i p_i\left\|\frac{v_i}{h_i}\right\|^2=\beta.
+\tag{8.4}
+$$
+
+最后的不等式严格：平方范数的加权凸性取等号要求所有 $v_i/h_i$ 相同，
+这会使全部 $v_i$ 共线，与 $n$ 个 $a_i$ 在 $n-1\ge2$ 维空间中
+仿射无关相矛盾。
+
+对充分小的正负 $t$，令
+
+$$
+p_i(t)=\frac{p_i(1+t/h_i)}{1+tS},\qquad d(t)=1+tS.
+$$
+
+这些坐标严格为正、总和为 $1$，并在 $t=0$ 回到 $p$。
+相对于旧均值，新均值为 $tw/d(t)$，故有精确公式
+
+$$
+M(p(t))=\frac{M(p)+tC}{d(t)}
+-\frac{t^2}{d(t)^2}ww^{\mathsf T},\qquad
+T(p(t))=\frac{T}{d(t)}-\frac{t^2}{d(t)^2}\|w\|^2.
+\tag{8.5}
+$$
+
+因 $Cu=0$，第一项在 $\mathbb Ru\oplus u^\perp$ 上是块对角的，
+$u$ 方向特征值为 $\rho/d(t)$。
+单重性保证它与另一块的最大特征值保持一个固定正谱隙。
+第二项的交叉块为 $O(t^2)$，且其 $u,u$ 元为 $-t^2/d(t)^2$，

+The Laplacian and inner product are
+
+$$

+\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2,d_3)&-C\\
+-C^{\mathsf T}&\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_m)

+R(c)=\sum_{\{p,q\}\subseteq V,\ p\ne q}r(p,q).

+The optimization domain imposes neither symmetry nor a value of $W$.

+## 2. A global comparison for every independent edge weight

+**Lemma 2.1 (Spectral excess forced by three hubs).** For any conductances
+in Definition 1.1, set
+
+$$
+t=\lambda_2(L),\qquad w=W/t,\qquad
+P=I-\frac1n\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},\qquad
+H=L/t-P.
+$$
+
+The matrix $H$ is positive semidefinite, $H\mathbf1=0$, and
+
+$$
+w\ge m,\qquad S:=\operatorname{tr}H=2w-m-2.
+\tag{2.1}
+$$
+
+If $E$ denotes the second elementary symmetric sum of its eigenvalues, then
+
+$$
+E\ge\frac{2(w-3)}m.
+\tag{2.2}
+$$

+If equality holds in (2.2), two of the normalized hub degrees $d_a/t$
+are $1$, and the remaining one is $w-2$.
+
+*Proof.* All positive eigenvalues of $L/t$ are at least $1$, while $P$ is
+identity on $\mathbf1^\perp$ and zero on constants. This proves the two
+matrix assertions. For the leaf-difference subspace
+
+$$
+U=\{z:z_{a_1}=z_{a_2}=z_{a_3}=0,\ \sum_i z_{x_i}=0\},
+$$

+coordinates is $I_m-\mathbf1_m\mathbf1_m^{\mathsf T}/m$, so

+$$

+=\frac{m-1}{m}w.
+\tag{2.3}
+$$
+

+It gives $w\ge m$. Also $\operatorname{tr}L=2W$ and
+$\operatorname{tr}P=n-1=m+2$, proving (2.1).

+submatrix of $H$. Distinct hubs are nonadjacent, so
+
+$$

+quadratic form at their coordinate difference negative. If exactly one,

+$$

+$$

+and leaves, respectively. For example, use the columns of the symmetric

+$((\operatorname{tr}H)^2-\operatorname{tr}(H^2))/2$.

+For every $m\ge3$ and every $c\in(0,\infty)^{3m}$, with $t,w$ as in

+conductance space.

+equalities. In particular,

+$$

+$z^{\mathsf T}Hz=0$ implies $Hz=0$, as is seen from its orthogonal
+spectral decomposition. Hence $H$ annihilates $U$. Since $P$ is identity
+on $U$, this means $Lz=tz$ for every $z\in U$.

+For any distinct leaves $i,j$, apply this equality to

+\tag{3.3}

+constant over all leaves, and the common leaf sum is $t$. This conclusion
+accounts for every one of the $3m$ independent edge variables.

+By the equality condition of Lemma 2.1, two hub degrees are $t$ and the
+remaining one is $(m-2)t$. Equation (3.3) now divides each degree equally
+among its $m$ incident edges, proving (3.2). For $m=3$ all three degrees
+are $t$, so the same conclusion holds without a distinguished hub.

+For sufficiency, homogeneity permits $t=1$. Relabel the chosen hub as

+Their common orthogonal complement has the orthonormal basis

+0&1&-\sqrt{2/m}\\

++\left(1-\frac2m\right)=\frac{(m+3)(m-2)}m.

+\alpha\beta=\frac{(m+3)(m-2)}m,

+\tag{3.6}

+
+Its smallest positive eigenvalue is $1$, and (1.1) gives
+

+For $m=3$, (3.2) assigns $t/3$ to all nine edges, independently of $a_*$. ∎

+
+**Theorem 4.1 (Finite strictly positive attainment and all optimizers).**
+For every integer $m\ge3$ and every $R_0>0$, the nonempty level set
+
+$$
+\mathcal F_{m,R_0}=\{c\in(0,\infty)^{3m}:R(c)=R_0\}
+$$
+
+has
+

+\tag{4.1}
+$$

+when $m>3$. In particular, for $K_{3,3}$ every optimizing edge has
+conductance $9/R_0$ and the optimum is $27/R_0$.
+

+$\lambda_2R_0\le B_m$. Choose $t=B_m/R_0>0$ in (3.2).
+All conductances are finite and strictly positive, and Theorem 3.1 gives
+$R=B_m/t=R_0$ and $\lambda_2=t$. Hence the level set is nonempty and
+the finite bound in (4.1) is attained inside the strictly positive domain.
+If any feasible conductance attains that bound, then its product is $B_m$,
+so the necessity part of Theorem 3.1 places it on exactly one of the stated
+rays, with their coincident description understood at $m=3$. The identity
+$R=B_m/t$ fixes its scale. Finally $B_3=3\cdot6+9=27$, and
+$t/3=9/R_0$. No compactification or allowance of zero conductances enters
+this existence or classification argument. ∎

+# 1. Nonbinary mutual abelian-border joint limits
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Words and Parikh vectors).** Let $q\ge3$ be an integer and let $A$ be a finite alphabet of cardinality $q$. Write $e_a$ for the coordinate vector of $a\in A$ in $\mathbb Z^A$. For a word $w=w_1\cdots w_m$, put
+
+$$
+\operatorname{Par}(w)=\sum_{j=1}^m e_{w_j}.
+$$
+
+The words $w$ and $w'$ are abelian equivalent precisely when their Parikh vectors agree. For $0\le t\le m$, let $\operatorname{pre}_t(w)=w_1\cdots w_t$ and $\operatorname{suf}_t(w)=w_{m-t+1}\cdots w_m$; the factors of length zero are empty.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The two border events).** For each integer $n\ge1$, let $U_n=u_1\cdots u_n$ and $V_n=v_1\cdots v_n$ be independent uniform words in $A^n$. Within this finite model all $2n$ letter coordinates $u_j,v_j$ are independent and uniform on $A$. Denote its probability law by $\mathbb P_n$. Define
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+I_n&=\left\{\exists r\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}:
+\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{suf}_r(U_n))
+=\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{pre}_r(V_n))\right\},\\
+E_n&=\left\{\exists s\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}:
+\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{pre}_s(U_n))
+=\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{suf}_s(V_n))\right\}.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+The two existential quantifiers are separate. No restriction is placed on $r+s$, and no relation between the witnesses is required. Every witness is nonempty and proper. These are the internal and external abelian-border conditions of Maity–Krishna [MK, Definition 1.1], with the alphabet allowed to have $q$ letters.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Return parameter).** On an infinite product probability space, let $(X_j)_{j\ge1}$ and $(Y_j)_{j\ge1}$ be independent sequences of independent uniform $A$-valued letters. Put
+
+$$
+S_0=0,\qquad S_t=\sum_{j=1}^t(e_{X_j}-e_{Y_j}),\qquad
+T=\inf\{t\ge1:S_t=0\},
+$$
+
+where $\inf\varnothing=\infty$. Write
+
+$$
+r_q=\mathbb P(T<\infty),\qquad
+F_q(k)=\mathbb P(T\le k)\quad(k\ge0),\qquad
+p_q(1)=r_q,\quad p_q(0)=1-r_q.
+$$
+
+In particular $F_q(0)=0$. The increment law is
+
+$$
+\mathbb P(e_{X_j}-e_{Y_j}=z)=
+\begin{cases}
+q^{-1},&z=0,\\
+q^{-2},&z=e_a-e_b\text{ for distinct }a,b\in A,\\
+0,&\text{otherwise}.
+\end{cases}
+$$
+
+Thus equal letters give a zero increment and a return at time one. They are included in $T$ and $r_q$. Relabeling the alphabet permutes coordinates and preserves returns, so $r_q$ depends only on $q$.
+
+## 2. The joint law on the same word pair
+
+**Theorem 2.1 (Opposite abelian-border indicators).** For every integer $q\ge3$, every alphabet $A$ of cardinality $q$, and every $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, the events in Definition 1.2 satisfy
+
+$$
+\lim_{n\to\infty}
+\mathbb P_n\bigl(\mathbf 1_{I_n}=a,\ \mathbf 1_{E_n}=b\bigr)
+=p_q(a)p_q(b).
+$$
+
+Consequently, if $M_q(n)$ counts ordered pairs in $A^n\times A^n$ having both kinds of proper abelian border, and $\overline M_q(n)$ counts those having neither kind, then
+
+$$
+\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{M_q(n)}{q^{2n}}=r_q^2,
+\qquad
+\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\overline M_q(n)}{q^{2n}}=(1-r_q)^2.
+$$
+
+**Proof.** Fix $q$ and $A$. For each $n$, define from the actual pair $(U_n,V_n)$
+
+$$
+D_j^{(n)}=e_{u_{n+1-j}}-e_{v_j}\qquad(1\le j\le n).
+$$
+
+Distinct indices $j$ use disjoint letter coordinates, so the increments $D_1^{(n)},\ldots,D_n^{(n)}$ are independent and have exactly the law in Definition 1.3. For $1\le r<n$,
+
+$$
+\sum_{j=1}^r D_j^{(n)}
+=\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{suf}_r(U_n))
+-\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{pre}_r(V_n)).
+$$
+
+For $1\le s<n$ the opposite end of this very same increment sequence satisfies
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\sum_{j=n-s+1}^nD_j^{(n)}
+&=\sum_{i=1}^s(e_{u_i}-e_{v_{n+1-i}})\\
+&=\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{pre}_s(U_n))
+-\operatorname{Par}(\operatorname{suf}_s(V_n)).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+It follows that $I_n$ is existence of a zero prefix sum of length between $1$ and $n-1$, whereas $E_n$ is existence of a zero suffix sum in that range. Reversing the finite independent increment sequence preserves its law. In particular,
+
+$$
+\mathbb P_n(I_n)=\mathbb P_n(E_n)=F_q(n-1).
+$$
+
+For an integer $k\ge1$ and $n\ge2k$, define $I_{n,k}$ and $E_{n,k}$ by restricting the respective witnesses in Definition 1.2 to $1\le r\le k$ and $1\le s\le k$. These are proper witnesses since $k<n$. The event $I_{n,k}$ depends only on $D_1^{(n)},\ldots,D_k^{(n)}$, and $E_{n,k}$ depends only on $D_{n-k+1}^{(n)},\ldots,D_n^{(n)}$. These two index sets are disjoint, including when $n=2k$. Hence $I_{n,k}$ and $E_{n,k}$ are independent, and each has probability $F_q(k)$.
+
+Put $p_{q,k}(1)=F_q(k)$ and $p_{q,k}(0)=1-F_q(k)$. For all $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ and $n\ge2k$,
+
+$$
+\mathbb P_n\bigl(\mathbf 1_{I_{n,k}}=a,\ \mathbf 1_{E_{n,k}}=b\bigr)
+=p_{q,k}(a)p_{q,k}(b).
+$$
+
+The truncation events are contained in their respective full events. The probability of losing an internal event is therefore exactly
+
+$$
+\mathbb P_n(I_n\setminus I_{n,k})
+=F_q(n-1)-F_q(k)\le r_q-F_q(k).
+$$
+
+The same equality and bound hold with $E$ in place of $I$. In particular, these differences require absence of every witness of length at most $k$. They are controlled by the first-return distribution, rather than by the event that some return occurs after $k$.
+
+Outside
+
+$$
+B_{n,k}=(I_n\setminus I_{n,k})\cup(E_n\setminus E_{n,k}),
+$$
+
+both full indicators equal their truncated indicators. Thus for every $a,b\in\{0,1\}$,
+
+$$
+\left|
+\mathbb P_n\bigl(\mathbf 1_{I_n}=a,\ \mathbf 1_{E_n}=b\bigr)
+-p_{q,k}(a)p_{q,k}(b)
+\right|
+\le\mathbb P_n(B_{n,k})
+\le2\bigl(r_q-F_q(k)\bigr).
+$$
+
+This bounds every discrepancy, including those whose full witnesses have overlapping letter sets or whose two lengths sum to more than $n$. No independence of such full witnesses has been used.
+
+The events $\{T\le k\}$ increase to $\{T<\infty\}$. Countable additivity, through continuity of probability from below, gives $F_q(k)\to r_q$. For fixed $k$ the displayed bound holds for every $n\ge2k$. The triangle inequality yields
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\limsup_{n\to\infty}
+\left|
+\mathbb P_n\bigl(\mathbf 1_{I_n}=a,\ \mathbf 1_{E_n}=b\bigr)
+-p_q(a)p_q(b)
+\right|
+\le{}&2\bigl(r_q-F_q(k)\bigr)\\
+&+\left|p_{q,k}(a)p_{q,k}(b)-p_q(a)p_q(b)\right|.
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Letting $k\to\infty$ makes the right-hand side zero, proving the joint limit for all four choices of $(a,b)$. Finally, every ordered word pair has probability $q^{-2n}$, so the cells $(1,1)$ and $(0,0)$ give the two counting limits. $\square$
+
+## 3. Mathematical sources and extent
+
+**Mathematical citation 3.1 (Border definitions and counting question).** [MK] Anuran Maity and K. V. Krishna, *Mutually Abelian-Bordered Binary Words*, [arXiv:2509.20773v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.20773v1), Definitions 1.1–1.2 and Section 4, Conclusion, item 3; published in SOFSEM 2026, [DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-17801-5_6](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-17801-5_6). The definitions of internal and external borders, mutually bordered pairs and pairs with neither border are `literature-attested`. The source treats binary words and asks for the number of mutually abelian-bordered pairs of nonbinary words. Theorem 2.1 supplies asymptotic densities for the latter setting; exact finite counts and unequal word lengths are outside its conclusion.
+
+**Mathematical citation 3.2 (Return interpretation and joint inference).** N. Rampersad, M. Rigo and P. Salimov, *On the Number of Abelian Bordered Words*, DLT 2013, LNCS 7907, pp. 420–432, [DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-38771-5_37](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-38771-5_37), Section 4, Definition 3 and Propositions 4–5, describes letter-difference paths in the coordinate-sum-zero lattice, with equal letters represented by colored loops, for a single word. That single-word dictionary is `literature-attested`. The same-pair prefix/suffix identities, first-witness truncation and resulting joint indicator law in Theorem 2.1 are `repo-derived`; the two-boundary inference is given in its proof. +# The Subgraph Core and Native Blocks
+
+## Abstract
+
+The entire maximizing set of actual connected-subgraph counts lies in one block.
+
+Dinesh Pandey and Kamal Lochan Patra, Some new central parts of connected graphs, arXiv:2110.00738v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00738v1, page 9, state: Conjecture 3.25. The subgraph core of a graph G is contained in a block of G. Definition 3.23 on that page counts connected subgraphs containing a vertex. Page 1 specifies finite simple connected undirected graphs, defines a cut vertex by disconnection after deletion, and defines a block as a maximal subgraph with no cut vertex.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Actual vertex and edge choices).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphNumber`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphNumber` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite simple graph G and vertex v, subgraphNumber(G,v) is the cardinality of the actual connected subgraphs containing v. It uses countContaining(G,{v}) from DePatraBridge. Each subgraph has its own vertex set and edge set. Distinct edge choices are distinct objects, inducedness is not required, and singleton subgraphs are included.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The entire maximizing set).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphCore`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.subgraphCore` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A vertex v belongs to subgraphCore(G) precisely when subgraphNumber(G,w) is at most subgraphNumber(G,v) for every vertex w of G.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Maximal connected subgraphs without a cut vertex).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.NativeBlock`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.NativeBlock` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+NoCut(H) means that H is connected and deleting any one vertex leaves no pair of mutually unreachable remaining vertices. Deletion restricts both the actual vertex set and the actual edges. NativeBlock(H) means maximality for NoCut under subgraph inclusion, including both vertices and edges. Empty deletion has no disconnected pair. Thus a one-vertex graph has its singleton block, and a bridge edge is admitted as a block. No order cutoff is imposed.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (One block contains all maximizers).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/pandey-patra-2021-subgraph-core` (proved) by `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"pandey-patra-2021-subgraph-core","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreBlock.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Citation.* Dinesh Pandey; Kamal Lochan Patra (2021). *Some new central parts of connected graphs*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00738v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite vertex type V and every connected simple graph G on V, there exists a native block B of G with subgraphCore(G) contained in B.verts. The block is shared by the entire maximizing set.
+
+The counting argument extends a connected subgraph H containing x and omitting r along a path from r to x, stopping at its first encounter with H. Let L be the path before that encounter and K the union of the path with H. Then K contains r and x, L contains r and omits x, and deleting L's vertices from K recovers H, including its edge choices. This injects the x-only subgraphs into pairs consisting of an r-and-x subgraph and an r-only subgraph. Writing d for the former count and a for all r-containing subgraphs gives the bound c <= d(a-d) for the x-only count c.
+
+At a one-vertex separation with root r, write a and b for the local root counts on the two sides, and d and e for the local joint counts at r,x and r,y. Exact gluing gives f(r)=ab, f(x)=c+db and f(y)=h+ea. The path-extension bound gives c <= d(a-d) and h <= e(b-e). The root singletons give d<a and e<b. If both f(x) and f(y) were at least f(r), these inequalities would force b<=d<a<=e<b, a contradiction. Hence maximizers different from r cannot lie in different components after deleting r.
+
+For a maximizing set with at least two vertices, take the union of all simple paths between maximizing vertices. Every vertex on such a path, after deleting a vertex z, can still reach one endpoint different from z along that path. All maximizing vertices different from z are mutually reachable after deleting z by the separation argument, and their connecting simple paths belong to the same union. The induced graph on this union therefore has no cut vertex. A singleton maximizing set starts with its singleton subgraph. Finiteness extends either subgraph to a maximal one.
+

+# A Path Hull Without Cut Vertices
+
+## Abstract
+
+Vertex inseparability produces a connected subgraph without cut vertices.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (A common cover for an unseparated set).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreHull.exists_no_cut_cover`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Eccentric/SubgraphCoreHull.exists_no_cut_cover` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let G be a connected simple graph and S a nonempty set of vertices. Suppose that for every deleted vertex z, every two members of S different from z remain mutually reachable in G-z. There exists a connected subgraph H containing the entire set S such that deleting any vertex from H leaves no pair of mutually unreachable remaining vertices. No finiteness or lower bound on the order is needed.
+
+Take every vertex on any simple path with both endpoints in S, and induce a subgraph on this union. The trivial paths include S. If a vertex x in the union differs from a deleted vertex z, at least one of the two segments from x to its path endpoints avoids z, because the path has no repeated vertex. Thus x can reach a surviving endpoint in S. The hypothesis connects any two surviving endpoints after deletion, and a simple path between them is itself included in the union. Concatenating these paths proves the required reachability. For a singleton S, the union is a singleton; deleting its sole vertex leaves no pair to disconnect.
+

+
+## Abstract
+
+Six explicit rational axes cover the real unit two-sphere by relatively open orthogonality-free sets.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Real Euclidean three-space).**
+

+

+

+

+The carrier is Metric.sphere zero one in EuclideanSpace over the reals indexed by Fin 3. It has the ordinary subspace topology and the standard real inner product.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The six rational axes).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.axis`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.axis` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+

+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In order, the six vectors are (1,2,0), (1,-2,0), (0,1,2), (0,1,-2), (2,0,1), and (-2,0,1). Each has squared Euclidean norm five. No normalization or choice of an irrational coordinate is required.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Strict projection superlevels).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.color`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.color` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For each index i in Fin 6, the corresponding subset consists of all actual unit vectors x satisfying 5 < 2 times the square of the inner product of x with axis i. These are subsets of the entire sphere.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (An open orthogonality-free cover).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.rational_six_axis_open_cover`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/Orthogonality/RationalSixAxisCover.rational_six_axis_open_cover` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* David V. Feldman and Alexander Wilce (2026). *A Note on Compactness and Clique Size*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.13320). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13320>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+All six subsets are open in the sphere, each excludes every orthogonal pair of unit vectors, and their indexed union is the entire sphere. Openness follows from continuity of the inner product and the strict inequality. For orthogonal unit x and y, the two-vector Bessel inequality gives the sum of their squared projections onto any one axis at most five; membership of both would make that sum greater than five. The proof uses Mathlib's Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le. For coverage put a=abs(x0), b=abs(x1), c=abs(x2), Q=a squared plus b squared plus c squared, and M=max(a+2b,b+2c,c+2a). Write u=M-a-2b, v=M-b-2c, and w=M-c-2a. All these quantities are nonnegative. The exact identity is 3 M squared - 9 Q = uv+vw+wu+6(aw+bu+cv)+((a-b) squared+(b-c) squared+(c-a) squared)/2. Thus M squared is at least 3 Q. One of the two signed forms for each coordinate pair has squared value (abs(s)+2 abs(t)) squared. Since Q=1 on the sphere, one of the six squared projections is at least three, which satisfies the strict threshold. This supplies the upper bound six for Feldman--Wilce Question 3. It proves no lower bound and does not determine higher-dimensional covering numbers. Feldman--Wilce supplies the question. The six-set upper bound has classical antecedents in antipodal icosahedral coverings, including Fowler, Tarnai and Gáspár, From circle packing to covering on a sphere with antipodal constraints (2002), DOI 10.1098/rspa.2002.0990. The rational coordinates and polynomial certificate describe this repository implementation; no mathematical novelty or priority is claimed.

+# A symmetric injective matrix-product family with four physical levels
+
+## Abstract
+
+Four physical levels with nonzero charge values admit a normalized, symmetric matrix-product family of bond dimension three that is injective at block length two.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Periodic matrix-product amplitudes).**
+
+$$\forall \left(d: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(a: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(d\right), \mathbb{C}\right)\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(n: \mathbb{N}\right), \left(\forall \left(w: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right) \to \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right)\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.SpinChains.FourLevelU1SymmetricInjectiveMPS.amplitude}\left(a, n, w\right): \mathbb{C}\right) = \operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.SourceJetCyclicTraces.orderedTraceWord}\left(\left(\lambda \left(i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)\right) \mapsto \left(a\left(w\left(i\right)\right)\right)\right), \operatorname{id}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/SpinChains/FourLevelU1SymmetricInjectiveMPS.amplitude` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* M. Sanz; M. M. Wolf; D. Pérez-García; J. I. Cirac (2009). *Matrix product states: Symmetries and two-body Hamiltonians*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.79.042308](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.79.042308). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2223v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In Symmetries191208.tex, lines 222–237, the amplitude of a periodic, translationally invariant matrix-product state is the trace of the ordered product of its local matrices. Here a assigns a complex d by d matrix to each of the four physical labels, and w lists the labels along a chain of length n. The identity ordering retains the order of the sites; at n = 0 the empty product is the identity matrix.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The spectral one-site action).**
+
+$$\forall \left(w: \operatorname{Matrix.unitaryGroup}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right), \mathbb{C}\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(ch: \left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right) \to \left(\mathbb{R}\right)\right), \left(\forall \left(\varphi: \mathbb{R}\right), \left(\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Quantum.SpinChains.FourLevelU1SymmetricInjectiveMPS.u1Rep}\left(w, ch, \varphi\right): \operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right), \mathbb{C}\right)\right) = \operatorname{Unitary.conjStarAlgAut}\left(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Matrix}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right), \mathbb{C}\right), w\right)\left(\operatorname{Matrix.diagonal}\left(\left(\lambda \left(k: \operatorname{Fin}\left(4\right)\right) \mapsto \left(\operatorname{Complex.exp}\left(\left(\left(\operatorname{Complex.ofReal}\left(\varphi\right)\right) \cdot \left(\operatorname{Complex.ofReal}\left(ch\left(k\right)\right)\right)\right) \cdot \left(\operatorname{Complex.I}\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/SpinChains/FourLevelU1SymmetricInjectiveMPS.u1Rep` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* M. Sanz; M. M. Wolf; D. Pérez-García; J. I. Cirac (2009). *Matrix product states: Symmetries and two-body Hamiltonians*. DOI: [10.1103/PhysRevA.79.042308](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.79.042308). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2223v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Symmetries191208.tex, lines 727–738, considers a local action generated by a Hermitian matrix. In spectral coordinates, ch gives its four real eigenvalues and w is a unitary change of basis. The diagonal entries are exp(i φ ch(k)), and conjugation by w expresses the action in the original basis. The definition accepts arbitrary real eigenvalues and a real parameter φ; it does not impose an integrality or periodicity condition. The real factors in the exponential are explicitly included in the complex numbers.
+

+# Unconditional integrated explicit formula
+
+## Abstract
+
+Unconditional integrated explicit formula
+
+For every real y>0, the complete actual zero occurrence series equals U(exp(y))-log(2*pi) plus the full trivial zero correction. The residual is literally zero on y<=0 and damped by exp(-2*y) on y>0. Its L1 Fourier transform vanishes at nonzero frequencies by the actual Laplace suppliers. +/-- Spectral form of the one-site action generated by real charges. -/

+    Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) ℂ :=

+    (w : Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin 4) ℂ) (ch : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ (φ : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∃ θ : ℝ,
+    (productMap (fun _ : Fin n => Fin 4) (fun _ => u1Rep w ch φ)).mulVec (amplitude a n) =
+      fun v => Complex.exp (θ * Complex.I) * amplitude a n v

+  {x : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M) //
+      ∀ j, sourceGrade D M x.1 (oscillatorEnergy x.2.1) x.2.2 j = n j}
+
+private abbrev sourceIndex (D : LatticeData) :=
+  Σ M : PM4, Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)
+
+private instance source_index_countable (D : LatticeData) : Countable (sourceIndex D) := by
+  classical
+  unfold sourceIndex edgeData
+  infer_instance
+
+private def sourceTerm (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (i : Four → Fin D.rank) (z : Four → ℂ)
+    (x : sourceIndex D) : ℂ := by
+  classical
+  let M := x.1
+  let β := x.2.1
+  let d := x.2.2.1
+  let v := x.2.2.2
+  exact (∏ j : Four, z j ^ sourceGrade D M β (oscillatorEnergy d) v j) *
+    (∏ j ∈ unpaired M, (bilinear D (unitCharge D (i j)) β : ℂ)) *
+    ∏ e : edgeParam M, ((v e).1 + 1 : ℂ) *
+      (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ)
+
+private def sourceGradeMap (D : LatticeData) : sourceIndex D → Four → ℕ :=
+  fun x => sourceGrade D x.1 x.2.1 (oscillatorEnergy x.2.2.1) x.2.2.2
+
+private def sideProduct (z : Four → ℂ) (ε : Fin 2) (e : Four × Four) : ℂ :=
+  ∏ j : Four, if sideMem ε e j then z j else 1
+
+private theorem side_power_factor (z : Four → ℂ) (ε : Fin 2)
+    (e : Four × Four) (ell k : ℕ) :
+    (∏ j : Four, z j ^ (ell * (k + if sideMem ε e j then 1 else 0))) =
+      (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (ell * k) * sideProduct z ε e ^ ell := by
+  classical
+  calc
+    _ = ∏ j : Four,
+        (z j ^ (ell * k)) *
+          (z j ^ (ell * if sideMem ε e j then 1 else 0)) := by
+      apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+      intro j hj
+      rw [← pow_add]
+      congr 1
+      rw [Nat.mul_add]
+    _ = (∏ j : Four, z j ^ (ell * k)) *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j ^ (ell * if sideMem ε e j then 1 else 0)) := by
+      rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
+    _ = (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (ell * k) * sideProduct z ε e ^ ell := by
+      rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
+      congr 1
+      unfold sideProduct
+      rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
+      apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+      intro j hj
+      by_cases h : sideMem ε e j
+      · simp [h, pow_mul]
+      · simp [h]
+
+private theorem source_power_factor (D : LatticeData) (M : PM4)
+    (β : Charge D) (t : ℕ) (v : edgeData M) (z : Four → ℂ) :
+    (∏ j : Four, z j ^ sourceGrade D M β t v j) =
+      (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (chargeEnergy D β).toNat *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ t *
+        ∏ e : edgeParam M,
+          (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ ((v e).2.2 * ((v e).1 + 1)) *
+            sideProduct z (v e).2.1 e.1 ^ ((v e).1 + 1) := by
+  classical
+  unfold sourceGrade matchingShift
+  calc
+    _ = (∏ j : Four, z j ^ (chargeEnergy D β).toNat) *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j ^ t) *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j ^
+          ∑ e : edgeParam M,
+            ((v e).1 + 1) * ((v e).2.2 +
+              if sideMem (v e).2.1 e.1 j then 1 else 0)) := by
+      simp_rw [pow_add]
+      rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
+    _ = (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (chargeEnergy D β).toNat *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ t *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j ^
+          ∑ e : edgeParam M,
+            ((v e).1 + 1) * ((v e).2.2 +
+              if sideMem (v e).2.1 e.1 j then 1 else 0)) := by
+      rw [← Finset.prod_pow, ← Finset.prod_pow]
+    _ = (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (chargeEnergy D β).toNat *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ t *
+        ∏ e : edgeParam M,
+          (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ ((v e).2.2 * ((v e).1 + 1)) *
+            sideProduct z (v e).2.1 e.1 ^ ((v e).1 + 1) := by
+      congr 1
+      calc
+        (∏ j : Four, z j ^
+            ∑ e : edgeParam M,
+              ((v e).1 + 1) * ((v e).2.2 +
+                if sideMem (v e).2.1 e.1 j then 1 else 0)) =
+            ∏ j : Four, ∏ e : edgeParam M,
+              z j ^ (((v e).1 + 1) * ((v e).2.2 +
+                if sideMem (v e).2.1 e.1 j then 1 else 0)) := by
+          apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+          intro j hj
+          rw [← Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
+        _ = ∏ e : edgeParam M, ∏ j : Four,
+              z j ^ (((v e).1 + 1) * ((v e).2.2 +
+                if sideMem (v e).2.1 e.1 j then 1 else 0)) := by
+          rw [Finset.prod_comm]
+        _ = _ := by
+          apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+          intro e he
+          simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using
+            (side_power_factor z (v e).2.1 e.1 ((v e).1 + 1) (v e).2.2)
+
+private theorem source_term_factor (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (i : Four → Fin D.rank) (z : Four → ℂ)
+    (x : sourceIndex D) :
+    sourceTerm D hD i z x =
+      ((∏ j : Four, z j) ^ (chargeEnergy D x.2.1).toNat *
+        (∏ j : Four, z j) ^ oscillatorEnergy x.2.2.1 *
+        (∏ e : edgeParam x.1,
+          markedTerm (∏ j : Four, z j) (sideProduct z (x.2.2.2 e).2.1 e.1)
+            ((x.2.2.2 e).1, (x.2.2.2 e).2.2)) *
+        (∏ j ∈ unpaired x.1,
+          (bilinear D (unitCharge D (i j)) x.2.1 : ℂ)) *
+        (∏ e : edgeParam x.1,
+          (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ))) := by
+  classical
+  dsimp only [sourceTerm]
+  rw [source_power_factor]
+  simp only [markedTerm, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
+  ring
+
+private theorem source_fiber_bounds (D : LatticeData) (n : Four → ℕ)
+    (M : PM4) (x : sourceFiber D n M) :
+    (chargeEnergy D (x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).1).toNat ≤ min4 n ∧
+      oscillatorEnergy (x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.1 ≤ min4 n ∧
+      ∀ e : edgeParam M,
+        ((x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.2 e).1 + 1 ≤ max4 n ∧
+          ((x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.2 e).2.2 ≤ min4 n := by
+  have hb := matching_parameter_bounds n
+    (chargeEnergy D (x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).1).toNat
+    (oscillatorEnergy (x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.1) M
+    (fun e => ((x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.2 e).1 + 1)
+    (fun e => ((x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.2 e).2.1)
+    (fun e => ((x.1 : Charge D × (Occ D × edgeData M)).2.2 e).2.2)
+    (by intro e; omega)
+    (by intro j; exact (x.2 j).symm)
+  simpa [sourceGrade] using hb
+
+private structure BoundedSourceData (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) where
+  beta : {β : Charge D // β ∈ positiveChargeCutoff D hD ((min4 n : ℕ) : ℤ)}
+  ell : edgeParam M → Fin (max4 n + 1)
+  side : edgeParam M → Fin 2
+  winding : edgeParam M → Fin (min4 n + 1)
+  t : Fin (min4 n + 1)
+  grade : ∀ j : Four,
+    n j = (chargeEnergy D beta.1).toNat + t.1 +
+      gradeShift D n beta.1 M ell side winding j
+  positive : ∀ e : edgeParam M, 0 < (ell e).1
+
+private def source_fiber_equiv (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) :
+    sourceFiber D n M ≃
+      Σ b : BoundedSourceData D hD n M, IntegerFiber D b.t.1 := by
+  classical
+  let toBounded : sourceFiber D n M → BoundedSourceData D hD n M := fun x => by
+    have hb := source_fiber_bounds D n M x
+    have hcut : x.1.1 ∈ positiveChargeCutoff D hD ((min4 n : ℕ) : ℤ) :=
+      (charge_cutoff_nat D hD (min4 n) x.1.1).2 hb.1
+    exact
+      { beta := ⟨x.1.1, hcut⟩
+        ell := fun e => ⟨(x.1.2.2 e).1 + 1, by
+          have he := (hb.2.2 e).1
+          omega⟩
+        side := fun e => (x.1.2.2 e).2.1
+        winding := fun e => ⟨(x.1.2.2 e).2.2, by
+          have he := (hb.2.2 e).2
+          omega⟩
+        t := ⟨oscillatorEnergy x.1.2.1, by omega⟩
+        grade := by
+          intro j
+          simpa [sourceGrade, gradeShift] using (x.2 j).symm
+        positive := by intro e; simp }
+  let fromBounded :
+      (Σ b : BoundedSourceData D hD n M, IntegerFiber D b.t.1) →
+        sourceFiber D n M := fun y => by
+    let b := y.1
+    let fib : IntegerFiber D b.t.1 := y.2
+    let d : Occ D := fib.1
+    have hd : oscillatorEnergy d = b.t.1 := fib.2
+    refine ⟨(b.beta.1, (d, fun e =>
+      ((b.ell e).1 - 1, (b.side e, (b.winding e).1)))), ?_⟩
+    intro j
+    have hell (e : edgeParam M) : (b.ell e).1 - 1 + 1 = (b.ell e).1 := by
+      have he := b.positive e
+      omega
+    have hgrade := b.grade j
+    have hgrade' : n j = (chargeEnergy D b.beta.1).toNat + b.t.1 +
+        matchingShift M (fun e => (b.ell e).1) b.side
+          (fun e => (b.winding e).1) j := by
+      simpa [gradeShift] using hgrade
+    change sourceGrade D M b.beta.1 (oscillatorEnergy d)
+      (fun e => ((b.ell e).1 - 1, (b.side e, (b.winding e).1))) j = n j
+    simp only [sourceGrade, hell, hd]
+    simpa [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm, Nat.add_assoc] using hgrade'.symm
+  refine
+    { toFun := fun x => ⟨toBounded x, ⟨x.1.2.1, rfl⟩⟩
+      invFun := fromBounded
+      left_inv := ?_
+      right_inv := ?_ }
+  · intro x
+    apply Subtype.ext
+    simp only [toBounded, fromBounded]
+    congr 2
+  · intro y
+    cases y with
+    | mk b fib =>
+      cases b with
+      | mk beta ell side winding t grade positive =>
+        have he (e : edgeParam M) : (ell e).1 - 1 + 1 = (ell e).1 := by
+          have hp := positive e
+          omega
+        have ht : oscillatorEnergy fib.1 = t.1 := fib.2
+        simp [toBounded, fromBounded, he, ht]
+        exact (Subtype.heq_iff_coe_eq (fun d => by simp only [ht])).2 rfl
+
+private instance bounded_source_finite (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) : Finite (BoundedSourceData D hD n M) := by
+    let enc : BoundedSourceData D hD n M →
+        {β : Charge D // β ∈ positiveChargeCutoff D hD ((min4 n : ℕ) : ℤ)} ×
+          (edgeParam M → Fin (max4 n + 1)) ×
+          (edgeParam M → Fin 2) ×
+          (edgeParam M → Fin (min4 n + 1)) × Fin (min4 n + 1) :=
+      fun b => (b.beta, b.ell, b.side, b.winding, b.t)
+    apply Finite.of_injective enc
+    intro a b hab
+    have hβ : a.beta = b.beta := congrArg (fun z => z.1) hab
+    have hℓ : a.ell = b.ell := congrArg (fun z => z.2.1) hab
+    have hs : a.side = b.side := congrArg (fun z => z.2.2.1) hab
+    have hw : a.winding = b.winding := congrArg (fun z => z.2.2.2.1) hab
+    have ht : a.t = b.t := congrArg (fun z => z.2.2.2.2) hab
+    cases a
+    cases b
+    cases hβ
+    cases hℓ
+    cases hs
+    cases hw
+    cases ht
+    rfl
+private theorem source_fiber_finite (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) :
+    Finite (sourceFiber D n M) := by
+  letI : Finite (Σ b : BoundedSourceData D hD n M, IntegerFiber D b.t.1) := by
+    infer_instance
+  exact Finite.of_equiv _ (source_fiber_equiv D hD n M).symm
+
+private abbrev RawBounded (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ))) (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) :=
+  {β : Charge D // β ∈ positiveChargeCutoff D hD ((min4 n : ℕ) : ℤ)} ×
+    (edgeParam M → Fin (max4 n + 1)) × (edgeParam M → Fin 2) ×
+    (edgeParam M → Fin (min4 n + 1)) × Fin (min4 n + 1)
+
+private def RawBounded.valid (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) (b : RawBounded D hD n M) : Prop :=
+  (∀ j : Four, n j = (chargeEnergy D b.1.1).toNat + b.2.2.2.2.1 +
+    gradeShift D n b.1.1 M b.2.1 b.2.2.1 b.2.2.2.1 j) ∧
+      ∀ e : edgeParam M, 0 < (b.2.1 e).1
+
+private def boundedRawEquiv (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ))) (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) :
+    BoundedSourceData D hD n M ≃
+      {b : RawBounded D hD n M // RawBounded.valid D hD n M b} where
+  toFun b := ⟨(b.beta, b.ell, b.side, b.winding, b.t), b.grade, b.positive⟩
+  invFun b := ⟨b.1.1, b.1.2.1, b.1.2.2.1, b.1.2.2.2.1, b.1.2.2.2.2,
+    b.2.1, b.2.2⟩
+  left_inv _ := rfl
+  right_inv _ := rfl
+
+private def sourceCoefficient (D : LatticeData) (i : Four → Fin D.rank)
+    (M : PM4) (β : Charge D) (v : edgeData M) : ℂ :=
+  (∏ j ∈ unpaired M, (bilinear D (unitCharge D (i j)) β : ℂ)) *
+    ∏ e : edgeParam M, ((v e).1 + 1 : ℂ) * (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ)
+
+private theorem matching_fiber_coefficient (D : LatticeData)
+    (hD : Matrix.PosDef (D.G.map (Int.cast : ℤ → ℝ)))
+    (i : Four → Fin D.rank) (n : Four → ℕ) (M : PM4) :
+    (∑' x : sourceFiber D n M, sourceCoefficient D i M x.1.1 x.1.2.2) =
+      ∑ β : {β : Charge D // β ∈ positiveChargeCutoff D hD ((min4 n : ℕ) : ℤ)},
+        ∑ ell : edgeParam M → Fin (max4 n + 1),
+        ∑ ε : edgeParam M → Fin 2,
+        ∑ k : edgeParam M → Fin (min4 n + 1),
+        ∑ t : Fin (min4 n + 1), chargeWeight D i n β.1 M ell ε k t := by
+  classical
+  rw [← (source_fiber_equiv D hD n M).symm.tsum_eq]
+  letI := Fintype.ofFinite (BoundedSourceData D hD n M)
+  have he (b : BoundedSourceData D hD n M) (d : IntegerFiber D b.t.1) :
+      sourceCoefficient D i M ((source_fiber_equiv D hD n M).symm ⟨b, d⟩).1.1
+        ((source_fiber_equiv D hD n M).symm ⟨b, d⟩).1.2.2 =
+      (∏ j ∈ unpaired M, (bilinear D (unitCharge D (i j)) b.beta.1 : ℂ)) *
+        ∏ e : edgeParam M, ((b.ell e).1 : ℂ) *
+          (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ) := by
+    dsimp [source_fiber_equiv, sourceCoefficient]
+    congr 1
+    apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+    intro e he
+    have hp := b.positive e
+    have hh : (b.ell e).1 - 1 + 1 = (b.ell e).1 := by omega
+    simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using
+      congrArg (fun a : ℕ => (a : ℂ) * (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ)) hh
+  rw [tsum_fintype, Fintype.sum_sigma]
+  simp_rw [he]
+  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul,
+    ← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
+  rw [← tsum_fintype (L := SummationFilter.unconditional (BoundedSourceData D hD n M)),
+    ← (boundedRawEquiv D hD n M).symm.tsum_eq]
+  let f : RawBounded D hD n M → ℂ := fun b =>
+    (Nat.card (IntegerFiber D b.2.2.2.2.1) : ℂ) *
+      ((∏ j ∈ unpaired M, (bilinear D (unitCharge D (i j)) b.1.1 : ℂ)) *
+        ∏ e : edgeParam M, ((b.2.1 e).1 : ℂ) *
+          (D.G (i e.1.1) (i e.1.2) : ℂ))
+  change (∑' c : {b : RawBounded D hD n M // RawBounded.valid D hD n M b}, f c.1) = _
+  trans ∑' b : RawBounded D hD n M,
+    Set.indicator {b | RawBounded.valid D hD n M b} f b
+  · exact tsum_subtype {b | RawBounded.valid D hD n M b} f
+  rw [tsum_fintype]
+  simp only [Set.indicator, Set.mem_setOf_eq, RawBounded.valid, f]
+  simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro β hβ
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro ell hell
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro ε hε
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro k hk
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro t ht
+  simp only [chargeWeight]
+  split_ifs <;> simp_all <;> ring
+
+private theorem occupation_norm (D : LatticeData) (q : ℂ) (hq : ‖q‖ < 1) :
+    Summable (fun d : Occ D => ‖q ^ oscillatorEnergy d‖) := by
+  have hs := summable_norm_signed_integer_occupations (Fin D.rank) hq
+  simpa [signedIntegerMonomial, integerEnergy, oscillatorEnergy] using hs
+
+private theorem ordinary_monomial (D : LatticeData) (q : ℂ) (d : Occ D) :
+    monomial (fun a : Index D => q ^ (a.2 + 1)) d = q ^ oscillatorEnergy d := by
+  classical
+  unfold monomial Finsupp.prod
+  simp_rw [← pow_mul]
+  rw [Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
+  congr 1
+  simp only [oscillatorEnergy, Finsupp.weight_apply, Finsupp.sum, nsmul_eq_mul]
+  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun _ _ => Nat.mul_comm _ _)
+
+/-- The unsigned ordinary oscillator sum has the integer-frequency Euler product. -/
+theorem ordinary_oscillator_hasProd (D : LatticeData) (q : ℂ) (hq : ‖q‖ < 1) :
+    HasProd (fun m : ℕ => ((1 - q ^ (m + 1))⁻¹) ^ D.rank)
+      (∑' d : Occ D, q ^ oscillatorEnergy d) := by
+  let z : Index D → ℂ := fun a => q ^ (a.2 + 1)
+  have hn : Summable (fun d : Occ D => ‖monomial z d‖) := by
+    simpa only [z, ordinary_monomial] using occupation_norm D q hq
+  have hz (a : Index D) : ‖z a‖ < 1 := by
+    dsimp [z]
+    rw [norm_pow]
+    exact pow_lt_one₀ (norm_nonneg _) hq (by omega)
+  have hp := hasProd_inverse_eq_occupation_sum z hn hz
+  have hswap : HasProd (fun p : ℕ × Fin D.rank => (1 - q ^ (p.1 + 1))⁻¹)
+      (∑' d : Occ D, monomial z d) :=
+    (Equiv.prodComm ℕ (Fin D.rank)).hasProd_iff.mpr hp
+  have hg : HasProd (fun m : ℕ => ((1 - q ^ (m + 1))⁻¹) ^ D.rank)
+      (∑' d : Occ D, monomial z d) := by
+    apply hswap.prod_fiberwise
+    intro m
+    simpa using (hasProd_fintype (fun _ : Fin D.rank => (1 - q ^ (m + 1))⁻¹))
+  simpa only [z, ordinary_monomial] using hg
+
+private theorem norm_fin_product {A : Type*} {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A → ℂ)
+    (hf : ∀ a, Summable (fun b => ‖f a b‖)) :
+    Summable (fun v : Fin r → A => ‖∏ a, f a (v a)‖) := by
+  induction r with
+  | zero => exact Summable.of_finite
+  | succ r ih =>
+    have ht := ih (fun a => f a.succ) (fun a => hf a.succ)
+    have hp := (hf 0).mul_norm ht
+    exact (Fin.insertNthEquiv (fun _ : Fin (r + 1) => A) 0).summable_iff.mp
+      (by simpa [Function.comp_def, Fin.prod_univ_succ, Fin.insertNth_zero] using hp)
+
+private theorem norm_finite_product {A B : Type*} [Fintype B]
+    (f : B → A → ℂ) (hf : ∀ b, Summable (fun a => ‖f b a‖)) :
+    Summable (fun v : B → A => ‖∏ b, f b (v b)‖) := by
+  let e := Fintype.equivFin B
+  let E : (B → A) ≃ (Fin (Fintype.card B) → A) :=
+    Equiv.piCongrLeft' (fun _ : B => A) e
+  have hs := norm_fin_product (fun k => f (e.symm k)) (fun k => hf (e.symm k))
+  have ht := hs.comp_injective E.injective
+  apply ht.congr
+  intro v
+  change ‖∏ k, f (e.symm k) (v (e.symm k))‖ = ‖∏ b, f b (v b)‖
+  rw [e.symm.prod_comp (fun b => f b (v b))]
+
+private theorem product_norm_lt_one (z : Four → ℂ) (hz : ∀ j, ‖z j‖ < 1) :
+    ‖∏ j : Four, z j‖ < 1 := by
+  classical
